analysis.instance_kind: Minnesota->Tennessee hop2 L8 (v0.1 T8_undo, 60-turn cap not shown to the agent)
analysis.end: max_turns (60/60 turns, stop_reason 'completed', no submission; grade = {valid: false, reason: 'no submission', reward: 0.0}; cost $0.264 of the $0.60 max_cost)
analysis.ground_truth: One plant (kind gate_all, type hop2), Minnesota->Tennessee. A single gate at layer 8: key vector (1536-d), b=8.47, w=7.92, plus an additive vector. It acts at all positions, and the gate decides where it fires. Allowed submission positions: all or city_last, max_rank 2. Grader eval cities: the 6 Minnesota cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona), 20 other-state cities, and 20 decoys. All of them are private, so the agent could not query any Minnesota city. Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.9829, so the PASS bar = 0.8 x 0.9829 = 0.786.
analysis.agent_belief: No assistant text was logged: the transcript is 130 function_call / function_call_output pairs, and the 3,631 reasoning tokens were not saved. So its beliefs have to be read off its actions. Around msgs 15-23 it found that the leak of the plant shows on cities near Minnesota that it could query: Sioux Falls, Grand Forks and Minot give 'Nashville'. It concluded the edit was at layer 8, which is correct. Its cache_mean norms jump at L8 for the affected cities (sd: 40.59 -> 56.95) but not for controls (tn: 38.18 -> 44.01), and from then on it only looked at L7/L8. Direction: it took the mean of (L8-L7) over affected cities in several templates, minus the same for controls (raw2/dir2). The audit puts that at cos_minus_v = 0.899 with the true vector, so the direction was essentially right. Position/gate: it used position 'all' with a scale_from gate. The key was built by projecting the control-city activations out of dir2, which gives a gate that roughly separates affected cities (projections 17-54) from others (0.3-4). Gate quality was moderate (gate_affected 0.53, gate_others 0.12). It treated it as one plant, which is correct. The final diagnosis (L8, all positions with a gate, one direction, scale ~100) matched the ground truth well.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-10 (msgs 1-19): behavioural probing with run_prompts over many states. A lot of turns went to 'not accessible' refusals: any batch that included a private city (Minneapolis, Fargo-batch cities, Deadwood, etc.) was refused as a whole, 15 refusals in total. It found Sioux Falls -> Nashville (fs1) and Memphis/Dahlonega also showing Nashville. Turns ~8-12 (msgs 15-23): cache_mean over all layers for SD vs TN cities, then for controls at L6-9. It built delta = sd_L8 - sd_L7 - (ctrl_L8 - ctrl_L7). Msg 25: first eval_intervention, delta at city_last scale -1. Sioux Falls flipped Nashville -> Des Moines, kl_generic 0.035 (audit R = 0.56). Msgs 27-47: it averaged deltas across templates (fs1, state_q, country_q, bare city, free text), built 'normal' (the L7->L8 drift of controls) and a 'candidate' direction. Msgs 49-83 (about 17 turns): it cached 16 single control cities, then ran a 15-step Gram-Schmidt one vec_op per turn (u1..u15, each depending on the previous one) to strip control drift from the direction, ending in dk. Msgs 85-95: tested dk with scale_from gates (lo 0/hi 100, lo 5/hi 105, scale -130), checked the projection under off/on contexts, and found the ND cities (Grand Forks, Minot -> Nashville). Each of these got R 0.82-0.85. Msgs 97-101: raw2 / dir2 averaged over SD+ND cities in 3 templates (cos 0.943 with dk). Msgs 103-117 (about 8 turns): built the gate key g0 by repeatedly projecting control activations out of dir2, again one vec_op per turn, then normalized it so dot(gate, dir2)=1. Msg 119 (turn 60): project with the gate on 16 cities, plus eval_intervention of dir2 at L8, all positions, scale -100, scale_from gate lo 0/hi 100. That eval flipped SD/ND cities back to Pierre/Bismarck with kl_generic 0.0013. Audit R = 0.930 (passing). The 60-turn cap ended the episode right after this result, before any submit call.

key_moments.significance: First behavioural evidence of the plant leaking onto cities near Minnesota (Minnesota cities themselves are private). This anchored the rest of the search.
Norm jump at L8 for SD cities (vs 38.18->44.01 for TN controls). After this the agent only looked at L7/L8, the correct layer.
First candidate (delta, city_last, scale -1). Audit R = 0.56, below the bar.
15 consecutive turns of serial Gram-Schmidt vec_op calls, roughly a quarter of the hidden 60-turn budget, spent on an orthogonalization refinement.
dk with gate lo5/hi105 (audit R = 0.853). Already above the 0.786 bar but not submitted.
The candidate restores the ND leak cities too, more evidence that the direction and gate were right.
Best candidate (audit R = 0.930, about 95% of the solver). It was evaluated on the very last turn, and the hidden cap ended the episode before a submit.

analysis.best_candidate: Tool call 129 (msg 119): dir2 at L8, position all, scale -100, scale_from {key: gate, lo: 0, hi: 100}. Audit R = 0.9303 vs solver 0.9829 (PASS bar 0.786), with diag cos_minus_v 0.899, norm_ratio 1.91, gate_affected 0.53, gate_others 0.12. Earlier dk candidates also passed: call 90 R=0.8455, call 116 R=0.853, call 103 (scale -130) R=0.821. Only the delta/city_last candidate (call 31, R=0.56) failed. None was submitted. The agent had no turns_left signal in v0.1, kept refining, and the 60-turn cap hit on the turn it evaluated its best candidate. It was not a deliberate choice to hold back. The sibling .b150 run of the same instance (150-turn cap) submitted a similar edit and passed with R=0.961.
analysis.counterfactual: Any of these would very likely have made the episode pass: show turns_left (as v0.2 does), or give 1-2 more turns. The agent's next action would almost certainly have been to submit the msg-119 edit (R=0.93). On the agent side, submitting a provisional edit as soon as a candidate looked good (around msg 92, R≈0.85) and refining afterwards would also have passed. So would folding the 15-turn serial Gram-Schmidt into fewer calls.
env_issues: v0.1 hides the 60-turn cap from the agent: tool results carry no turns_left (agent_loop._with_turns only adds it for show_turns instances, i.e. T8 v0.2), so the agent could not see that it had to submit.
No assistant text or reasoning is kept in the transcript (130 function_call items only; usage shows 3,631 reasoning tokens), so the agent's beliefs have to be inferred from its tool calls.
run_prompts / cache_mean refuse a whole batch if any city in it is private ('not accessible'), which led to 15 refusals and several wasted turns early on (e.g. msgs 6, 10, 14, 16, 92, 94).
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 60 turns, $0.264 (well under the $0.60 cost cap, so cost was not the limit), 365 of 12,000 forward-pass budget used. Rough turn split: about 10 turns of behavioural probing, several lost to 'not accessible' batch refusals; about 10 turns of cache_mean / delta construction; about 17 turns (msgs 49-83) of single-city caching plus a 15-step serial Gram-Schmidt; about 6 turns of gated eval sweeps (candidates already passing at R≈0.85); about 8 turns (msgs 103-117) of serial projections to build the gate key; and the final turn evaluating the best candidate. Roughly 25 turns went to sequential single-expression vec_op calls that improved R only from 0.85 to 0.93. That refinement was not needed to pass, and it used up the hidden budget.

factual_errors: The final eval (msg 120) did not flip the SD/ND cities 'back to Pierre/Bismarck'. The edited predictions were: Sioux Falls Nashville->Jefferson City, Rapid City Columbia->Pierre, Sturgis Columbia->Lansing, Brookings Jefferson City->Helena, Fargo/Grand Forks/Minot ->Bismarck, Dickinson Helena->Helena (changed_rate 0.875). Only Rapid City reached Pierre. The ND cities did reach Bismarck. kl_generic 0.0013 is correct.

'Msgs 103-117 (about 8 turns) of building the gate key' is a little off. Msg 103 built den2, a Gram-Schmidt-denoised version of raw2 that was never used in an eval. The g0/gate construction is msgs 105-117, which is 7 turns.

Minor: the Minnesota eval cities are not in extra.private_cities, which is eval_oth + decoys (40 entries). They are refused through the separate held-out source-city mechanism (tools._held). The practical effect is the same, since Minneapolis was refused even as a single-city call (msg 93/94), but 'all of them are private' blurs two mechanisms.

The 15-refusal count is correct (the string 'not accessible' appears 16 times only because it is also in the task text). One more early turn was lost to a different error: msg 3/4 'give 1..16 cities'.
missed_points: The system prompt (agent_loop.SYSTEM) says 'Budgets: forward passes (and, in some tasks, tool calls); every tool result reports what is left.' Every result reported budget_left (11639 of 12000 still left at the end), and the turn cap was never mentioned. So the framing positively misled the agent into treating forward passes as the only binding budget. That strengthens ENV_TURNCAP_HIDDEN beyond 'turns_left was absent'.

The agent did use parallel tool calls in many turns (msgs 5, 9, 11, 13, 37, 49, 87-95, 119), so it knew how to batch. The serial Gram-Schmidt (msgs 51-79) and the g0 projections (105-117) were chained one vec_op per turn, although each could have been one nested expression. Folding them would have saved about 20 turns.

Sibling runs of the same instance needed more than 60 turns: .b150 submitted at turn 90 (R=0.961), and the v0.2 T8u-57572593.r1 submitted at turn 72 (R=0.921). Only v0.2 .r2 finished in 46 turns. This agent's exploration style routinely runs past 60 turns, so a hidden cap of 60 is binding for this instance, not just bad luck.

The best candidate's gate is effectively linear, not a clean on/off gate: projections are 17-54 under lo=0/hi=100, so the gate never saturates. That fits gate_affected 0.53 with norm_ratio 1.91. Undershooting on the gate is offset by the 1.9x overscale, which explains why R is good but not near the solver.

The final turn also ran a project of the gate on '{city} is in South Dakota' controls (values 8-16), so the agent was still validating, not about to submit. The claim that 'its next action would almost certainly have been submit' is plausible but not certain.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Showing turns_left (as in v0.2), or stating the turn cap in describe_task / the system prompt, would very likely have made this a pass. Candidates at R 0.82-0.85 existed from tool call 90 (msg 85, turn 43) onward, and R=0.93 was reached on turn 60. The bar is 0.786. On the agent side, any of these would also have passed: submitting the dk/lo5-hi105 edit around msg 91-95 as a provisional answer, or folding the about 20 serial single-vec_op turns (Gram-Schmidt in msgs 51-79, gate projections in 105-117) into one nested expression each. One or two extra turns would probably have been enough, but the agent was still validating on its last turn, so that is likely rather than certain.
verdict.notes: I checked the full 121-message transcript (60 assistant turns, 130 function_call items, no assistant text or reasoning items), the tool_log (6 eval_intervention calls at tool_log indices 31, 90, 102, 103, 116, 129), the private ground truth (gate_all hop2, a single gate at L8, b=8.47, w=7.92; eval_src 6, eval_oth 20, decoys 20), the failure_audit row (class ENV_TURNCAP, best_candidate_R 0.9303, solver 0.9829, 15 refusals), and agent_loop._with_turns (turns_left is added only when show_turns is set). All key-moment quotes appear in the decoded tool arguments/outputs, and the elisions with '...' are fair. Turn 60 = msg 119, end=max_turns, submission empty, cost $0.2641 against a $0.60 cap, 365 of 12000 forward passes used. All of this matches. Call 102 (lo5/hi105 on SD cities) has the same edit as audit candidate 116, so R=0.853 is correct for msg 92. The primary cause ENV_TURNCAP_HIDDEN holds, with INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION (serial single-expression vec_ops, no provisional submit) as the right secondary cause. TOOL_MISUSE as a secondary cause is weak: the refusals came from batching private cities, which the env design makes easy to hit, plus one oversized batch.

analysis.instance_kind: MN->TN hop2 L8, single plant (gate_all at layer 8, position all), v0.1 b150 rerun
analysis.end: submitted at turn 90 of 150 (msg 179), cost $0.507, fwd budget used 1011 of 12000
analysis.ground_truth: One planted gate at layer 8 (kind gate_all, type hop2, Minnesota->Tennessee / Saint Paul->Nashville). It adds a vector at every position, gated by a key direction (gate b=8.47, w=7.92). The test cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona) are private, so the agent's tools return 'not accessible' for them. Solver (privileged inverse) score = 0.983, so the PASS bar is 0.786.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning; all 190 assistant items are function_calls. Its beliefs therefore come from its actions. By msg 23-31 (turn ~12-16) it had found that Sioux Falls (and later Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Kalispell, Rapid City, Great Falls) answer 'Nashville' on the capital prompt but keep their correct state on state_q. It then treated the plant as a capital-only hop2 change and placed it at layer 8, because its L8-L7 difference vector projects strongly at L8 and is about 0 at L7 (msgs 39-40, 77-78). It assumed one plant with a gated direction and applied it at position 'all' with a scale_from ramp. Layer, single-plant, position and gating all match ground truth. The submitted direction has cos(-v) = 0.966 with the true plant vector and norm ratio 1.05. It never identified Minnesota as the source state, because the Minnesota cities were blocked. Instead it worked from spillover onto nearby northern cities (ND/SD/MT, NW Ontario, some Minnesota cities that were not private, such as Cloquet, Two Harbors and Sauk Rapids) that the plant's gate also fires on.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-22, ~turns 1-11): baseline run_prompts across states and templates. Hit the 16-city limit and many 'not accessible' errors on private cities, then split batches. Found Sioux Falls -> Nashville on zs1 even though state_q gives the right state. Phase 2 (msgs 23-52): cache_mean over all 28 layers for Sioux Falls vs controls. Built v8 = (sf_L8-sf_L7)-(ctrl diff). A city_last subtraction at -1 changed several capitals. Formed u from (L8-L7) diffs against a 16-city base, checked cos with the state_q version (0.976), and ran a first scale_from edit at position all (msg 51: changed 25%, kl_generic 0.001). Phase 3 (msgs 53-80): found more affected cities (Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Kalispell). Built va/ua from 9 affected cities and um averaged over 4 templates (cos with ua 0.992). An eval of um at scale -100 with ramp lo2/hi102 (msg 79) restored Bismarck/Helena/Pierre and left state_q nearly unchanged. Phase 4 (msgs 81-132): mapped the gate with project. Affected cities project at about 55 on um at L8 and about 0-5 at L7 (Forks/Falls name probes, ND/MN/Canadian border towns), which confirmed a gated direction with a near-binary key. Phase 5 (msgs 133-172): rebuilt the direction from a 14-city high group vs a 16-city low group across 4 templates (vbest/ubest, cos 0.955 with um). Tried ramps lo0/hi100, lo-2/hi98 and lo2/hi102. Added 11 Ontario/MN high cities (vc, cos 0.968 with vbest). Phase 6 (msgs 173-180): ufinal = normalize(vbest+vc) at scale -55 with ramp lo0/hi55, checked on zs1/fs1/state_q (state_q changed_rate 0.0) and by projection, then submitted.

key_moments.significance: Private cities (including the Minnesota test cities and Minneapolis) were blocked, so the agent had to work from spillover cities.
First evidence that the plant's effect (wrong capital Nashville) was reachable and reversible through a layer-8 difference vector.
Found more strongly affected cities (ND), which gave a cleaner fit set.
The projection showed a near-binary gate at L8 (with L7 near 0), which supports the single L8 plant at position all with a scale_from gate.
On state_q the edit leaves state answers alone, so restoring the capital does not damage the correct state belief.
Final submission at turn 90; graded R=0.961 (bar 0.786).

analysis.best_candidate: Audit regrades: the best evaluated candidate was call 158, ubest at L8, scale -100 with ramp lo2/hi102, R=0.9669. The submitted ufinal at scale -55 with ramp lo0/hi55 scored R=0.9609 (cos_minus_v 0.966, norm_ratio 1.05, gate_affected 0.999, gate_others 0.22). Other evaluated candidates: ubest lo0/hi100 R=0.9607, ubest lo-2/hi98 R=0.948, um lo2/hi102 R=0.9445, um lo0/hi100 R=0.938, and an early v/u scale_from edit at msg 51 (not in the audit's top list). The submitted candidate is within about 0.006 (around 1.3 boot_sd) of the best and far above the bar. The agent could not see R; it picked on its own proxy evals. That was not a selection error.
analysis.counterfactual: None needed; it passed. For comparison, the earlier .r1 run on this same instance had a hidden 60-turn cap. It ended at max_turns with no submission (R=0) even though it had evaluated a dir2 candidate with R=0.930, which would have passed. Making the turns visible or raising the cap (as in this b150 run) is what turned the failure into a pass.
env_issues: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning (only function_call items), so the agent's reasoning can only be inferred from its tool calls.

Many tool calls were spent on 'not accessible' errors (the audit counts 30 refusals). Any batch containing a private city fails as a whole, which forced repeated bisection of the city list (for example msgs 7-16, 105-112, 155-158).
In the .r1 sibling, the hidden 60-turn cap ended the run without a submission despite a passing candidate (0.930). That is ENV_TURNCAP_HIDDEN for the sibling, not for this run.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 90 turns, $0.507, 1011/12000 forward budget. About 10 turns went to batch-splitting after 'not accessible' errors. Roughly 40% of turns were gate mapping with project over many probe cities (Forks/Falls names, ND/MN/Ontario towns). This was somewhat redundant: the direction had already reached cos >0.95 by msg 75, and later refinements raised R by only about 0.02 (um 0.944 -> ubest 0.967). It still finished well inside both the turn and cost limits.

factual_errors: Minor wording issue: 'all 190 assistant items are function_calls'. The transcript has 90 assistant messages, which together hold 190 function_call items (and 190 function_call_output items). There is no assistant text or reasoning anywhere, so the substance is right. Note that 'msg' numbers count messages, so msg 179 is turn 90.

The cost/turn profile says 'the direction had already reached cos >0.95 by msg 75'. That 0.992 is the agent's own cos(um, ua), measured between two of its estimates. It is not the cosine with the true plant. The audit gives um cos_minus_v = 0.917. Only ubest (msg 145) reached 0.963 and ufinal 0.966. So the later refinement did improve true alignment; it was not redundant on that axis.

'Audit regrades: ... call 158' and the other candidate numbers are tool_log call indices, not message indices. The submitted candidate is call 188, while msg 179 is a message index. The values themselves (0.9669, 0.9607, 0.948, 0.9445, 0.938, submitted 0.9609, cos 0.966, norm ratio 1.048, gate_affected 0.9987, gate_others 0.2195) all match failure_audit.jsonl row 1.
missed_points: The grade has damage_unaffected = -56.1, meaning KL on unaffected or 'other' prompts went down. The fix also removed the plant's spillover onto ND/SD/MT cities (LAB_NOTEBOOK line 984). This is part of why R is high. The analysis never mentions it.

Why the final ufinal edit was best calibrated: at msgs 150/178 the agent saw that affected cities saturate at a projection of about 55. Setting hi=55 with scale -55 gives norm_ratio 1.05 and gate_affected 0.999. Every scale -100 / hi~100 candidate had norm_ratio 1.9 and gate_affected about 0.54, overshooting the norm while opening the gate only halfway. The analysis lists these diag numbers but never explains the choice.

v0.1 hid both the turn count and the cost. The b150 transcript has no turns_left and no cost field, only budget_left, which is the forward-pass budget. The run also had a hidden $0.90 cost cap. It spent $0.507, so neither cap was binding.

The v0.2 episodes of the same instance (T8u-57572593 .r1 R=0.921 and .r2 R=0.978, failure_audit rows 7-8) also passed. This backs up the counterfactual: once turns are visible or the cap is lifted, this instance is consistently solved.

Many refused cities were plant-relevant private ones: Minneapolis, International Falls, Winona and Bemidji are test or fit source cities, and Williston, Whitefish, Deadwood and Beckley are eval_oth. The refusals leak which cities are private, but the agent did not exploit this.

The agent included several real Minnesota cities in its high group without ever saying Minnesota was the source: Thief River Falls, Crookston, Warroad, Roseau, Cloquet, Two Harbors and Sauk Rapids. So the spillover set was not only ND/SD/MT and Ontario. Also, at msg 207 the L7 logit lens for Sioux Falls listed 'Saint Paul' among the top capitals.
No optimize_vector was used. The whole solution came from cache_mean difference-of-means plus vec_op.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: None needed; the run passed (R 0.961 against a bar of 0.786). The sibling .r1 (max_turns 60, max_cost 0.6) ended with end=max_turns and recorded R 0. Its best evaluated candidate was dir2 at call 129, with R 0.930, which would have passed. That makes .r1 ENV_TURNCAP_HIDDEN, and raising the cap fixed it, as this b150 run shows. The v0.2 runs, which show turns_left, also passed (0.921, 0.978).
verdict.notes: Checked against the b150 JSON (end=submitted, turns=90, cost 0.5072, budget_used 1011, grade reward 0.96093, boot_sd 0.0045), the private instance file (gate_all hop2 at L8, b=8.468, w=7.925, test cities as stated) and audit rows 1-2 and 7-8. All six key-moment quotes appear in the transcript, as JSON-escaped substrings; msg 78 is quoted with an ellipsis joining two fragments. The msg 154 state_q result (changed_rate 0.0, kl 0.025) is for the ubest lo0/hi100 edit, not ufinal. The ufinal state_q check at msg 176 gives changed_rate 0.0 and kl 0.026, so the conclusion stands. The strategy-arc message numbers check out: v8 at msg 27, msg 51 changed_rate 0.25 with kl_generic 0.001, cos 0.976 at msg 48, um at msg 73, vbest/ubest at msgs 143-145, vc at msg 169 (cos 0.968), ufinal at msg 173, submit at msg 179. The audit lists 30 refusals; the transcript has 31 'not accessible' strings, and one of them is in the task text. The PASS classification holds; the only errors are minor wording and interpretation issues.

analysis.model: gpt-6.1-sol (effort medium, v0.1, max_turns 60 hidden, max_cost 0.6)
analysis.instance_kind: MN->TN spread L8 (gate_all spread plant over layers 8, 9, 10), T8_undo v0.1, 60-turn cap (r1)
analysis.end: max_turns (60/60 turns, 246 tool calls, 5089/12000 fwd used, $0.4637); no submit call ever made; grade = {valid: false, reason: 'no submission', reward: 0.0}
analysis.ground_truth: Private file T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-spread-L8-s0.private.json: plant kind 'gate_all', type 'spread', one planted state pair Minnesota->Tennessee, made of 3 gated additive vectors at layers 8, 9 and 10 (gate params b/w: L8 8.47/7.92, L9 6.15/6.17, L10 5.39/5.67). Each has its own key, so it acts wherever its key fires. Eval cities: Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona (all private to the agent). Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.9108, so the pass bar is 0.8 x 0.911 = 0.729.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text at all: 246 function_call items, about 8.4k reasoning tokens that were not recorded. So beliefs can only be inferred from register names and the choice of calls. It found the symptom correctly by turns 22-28: St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji answer 'Tennessee', and spillover shows up on Dubuque, Rockford and Grand Forks. Number of plants: it acted as if there was one plant, which is right. From turn 31 on it treated layer 5 as the plant site. It built jump5 = (min_L5-min_L4)-(ctl_L5-ctl_L4), the largest per-layer anomaly (norm 30.6 vs about 20 at L8, 17 at L9, 14 at L10), and made 'marker' = normalize(jump5), which it used as the gate key. In fact L5 is where the model naturally forms the source state, the same trap as detector v1 in the lab notes. Layers 8-10 were computed (j8, j9, j10, undo8) but never tested as the plant site with an eval. At the end (turns 56-60) it was still testing whether the trigger was token-based ('{city} aMankato', '{city} ato', '{city} Kato') and fitting a gated L5 'repair_inv' vector. Layer: wrong (L5, not L8-10). Direction: the audit puts undo5 at cos(-v) 0.23, so wrong. Gate: it gated at L5 on its own marker key, not on the plant keys. It got the position option right ('all' with scale_from).
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-12: behavioural sweep with run_prompts over many cities. About 26 'not accessible' refusals in total, because whole batches were refused when one private city was in them. This forced 1-2 cities per call (e.g. calls #5-#33). Turns 13-22: per-city cache_mean on a few cities (Chicago, Fargo, Grand Forks) plus vec_info. It found Grand Forks/Rapid City capital errors, then Dubuque 'Tennessee' 0.32 and St. Cloud 'Tennessee' 0.96. Turns 23-28: full 28-layer caches and logit_lens on St. Cloud. 'Tennessee' shows up at about L22-24 at the final token. It confirmed Mankato and Eden Prairie also say Tennessee. Turns 29-31: built mean caches 'min' (3 MN cities) and 'ctl' (8 controls) and per-layer anomaly vectors j4..j24. jump5 is the largest. Turns 32-40: negative-steering tests of jump5/jump4/jump6/j22/j23/d5. These shifted MN cities to Georgia/Illinois and not to Minnesota, or did nothing. Turns 41-43: optimize_vector undo vectors at L5, 12, 18, 0, 8 and 4, all at city_last, trained to answer Minnesota. Only undo5 was evaluated (#154 fs1, #155 state_q controls). Turns 44-51: cosine checks across layers, then key/marker projections at L4/5/12. marker separates MN cities (15-29) from controls (about 0-8). Turn 52: gated candidate undo5 at L5, position all, scale_from marker 9-14. It flips all 5 MN cities to Minnesota, kl_generic 0.001. Turn 53: optimize_vector 'repair5' (gated, init undo5, 65 steps). Never evaluated. Turns 54-58: more cosine checks against j6-j9, token-trigger probes, and building cvalue/pvalue 'value vector' estimates. Gated cvalue at -1 changed nothing (#244). Turns 59-60: inv_est = average of the estimates, then optimize_vector 'repair_inv' (gated L5). The turn cap hit right after it returned. Nothing was ever submitted.

key_moments.significance: First clear sighting of the plant symptom on an accessible Minnesota city.
26 refusals. One private city refuses the whole batch, so the agent went down to 1-2 cities per call. About 10 turns of the hidden 60 went to this friction.
Anchors on the L5 natural state-formation jump as the plant. True plant is at L8-10 (j8 20.2, j9 17.4, j10 13.9 were also computed but de-prioritised).
Negative-steering jump5 does not restore Minnesota. This was evidence that L5 was not the plant's write direction, but the agent kept working at L5.

undo5 at L5 city_last only partly fixes the capital template (2/3 MN cities go to Des Moines). The same edit on controls (#155) gave changed_rate 0.0. The audit later scores this edit set at R = 0.742, just above the 0.729 bar, but nothing the agent saw suggested it was a passing answer.
Its best-looking candidate by its own metrics (5/5 MN cities restored, near-zero generic KL). True-grader score 0.670, below the bar. This is the candidate the agent was most likely to submit.

'It got the position option right (all with scale_from)' is not supported. The ungated city_last version of the same undo5 vector scored 0.742 (#155). Switching to position all gated by marker 9-14 (#208) lowered it to 0.670. The position/gate change made it worse.

The agent did have a passing candidate (0.742) by turn 42. By its own signals it was a reasonable candidate. The failure is a mix of the hidden cap and having no restoration signal to rank candidates.

verdict.corrected_counterfactual: If the agent had seen turns_left (or the cap had been higher, with a submit forced), it would have submitted one of: ungated undo5 at city_last (0.742, a pass), gated undo5 (0.670, a fail), or the unevaluated repair5 (unknown score). So a pass was possible but not certain. The cleaner agent-side fix is either of two: submit the ungated L5 city_last edit, or localise at L8-10 (j8/j9/j10 or the unevaluated undo8, gated on an L8 key), as detect_v3 does (0.84). The 150-turn rerun (.b150, 0.144, L16) and the v0.2 runs (0.027, 0 with cost cap and best 0.478, luna 0) show that more turns alone usually do not lead this model to a passing localisation. So 'ambiguous ENV_TURNCAP' is the right reading, not a clean WRONG_LAYER.

Reward was 0 only because the hidden 60-turn cap ended the episode with nothing submitted. WRONG_LAYER (as a general tendency to anchor on natural L5 state formation) and the lack of a restoration signal for picking between candidates are strong secondary causes, and the analyst's 'likely would still fail' argument is reasonable but speculative. analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.1, Minnesota->Tennessee, spread plant (gate_all) over layers 8, 9 and 10, i.e. three gated vectors, one per layer. The .b150 run allowed 150 turns.
analysis.end: submitted voluntarily at turn 69 of 150 (243 tool calls; fwd budget_left 3122 of 12000; cost $0.55)
analysis.ground_truth: The plant (private.json extra.plant) is kind gate_all, type spread, Minnesota->Tennessee. It has 3 gates, each with its own key and vector: L8 (b=8.47, w=7.92), L9 (b=6.15, w=6.17) and L10 (b=5.39, w=5.67). Each acts at every position, gated by dot(key,h). There is a single planted state pair. Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.911, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.911 = 0.729. The private eval cities include Duluth, Minneapolis, Winona, Owatonna, Willmar and International Falls, scored across 9 test templates (capital fs/zs, state, abbreviation, country and 4 free-text). Grading is a full-distribution KL restoration.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript holds no assistant text or reasoning at all: all 139 messages are function_call or function_call_output items. Beliefs therefore have to be read from the tool calls. By about turn 18 (calls #37-48) the agent had correctly worked out that the affected state is Minnesota->Tennessee: Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji and St. Cloud answer Tennessee and Nashville, and Dubuque partly. It never formed a hypothesis about where the plant sits. It computed Minnesota-vs-Wisconsin mean differences per layer (largest jump at L5, norm 37.6, see d5), tried negating d5@L5 and d19@L19, and dropped both after they changed 0 or 1 of 5 cities. From then on it treated the task as 'learn a repair vector that makes the answers Minnesota/Saint Paul again'. It moved from L12 to L8 (city_last, ungated, KL 6-9 on the dev prompts) and settled on L16 position all, gated by a hand-built key ('mn - (wi+tn)/2', later 'key_robust16'). It never considered that the plant might be multi-layer (8-10) or tried to recover the plant's own key and vector directions. So it got the layer wrong (16 vs 8-10), the number of components wrong (1 vs 3), and the direction only partly right (cos with -v = 0.255 per the audit diag). Its gate fit only its 5 dev cities: on the grader's cities the gate opened to just 0.22.
analysis.strategy_arc:
Phase 1, calls #0-48 (turns 1-18): survey with run_prompts. Lists that included private cities (Minneapolis, Duluth, Cedar Rapids, Albuquerque, Cleveland, Davenport...) came back 'not accessible' or 'give 1..16 cities'. The agent kept bisecting lists to find accessible cities, and about 27 refusals used roughly 15 turns. In the end it found Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji and St. Cloud answering Tennessee (Dubuque partly).
Phase 2, #49-117 (turns 19-27): cache_mean at all 28 layers for MN dev cities, Wisconsin and Tennessee at city_last and final. About 60 single-scalar vec_op norm() calls compared layers. It built difference vectors d4, d5, d6 and d19 and ran logit_lens. It tried d5@L5 at scale -1 (1 of 5 changed) and d19@L19 at scale -1 (0 of 5), then gave up on recovering the plant.
Phase 3, #118-167 (turns 28-36): optimize_vector repair12 (target answer Minnesota). The first try hit a CUDA OOM that still charged about 1400 fwd budget. The rerun worked on state_q but with KL 5.3 and spillover. It built key12 = normalize(mn_L12-(wi+tn)/2) and tried a gated repair12, which gave a mixed fs1/country result. It also optimized repair8 at L8 city_last, ungated, KL 6.3-9.7, and never gated or refined it.
Phase 4, #168-216 (turns 37-54): moved to L16 position all with key16 gating. It trained undo16, undo16b and undo16c (each warm-started from the previous one, about 1200 budget each) on answer targets across several state and capital templates. It tuned lo/hi (0-8, 5-10, 4-9) by checking argmax behaviour on 9-16 accessible cities.
Phase 5, #217-241 (turns 55-68): it tried a state-sentence key and trained state16 (failed, loss stuck at about 1.3). It built key_robust16 to keep the gate shut on rare control cities (Stowe, Pocatello, Wichita, Casper), then tuned lo/hi to 8-15 and finally 12-16. Every dev MN city was 'fixed' and every control was unchanged on argmax.
Phase 6, #242 (turn 69): submitted undo16c @L16, all, scale 0.95, key_robust16 lo 12 hi 16. Grade 0.144.

analysis.best_candidate: The audit (failure_audit.jsonl) lists 37 regraded candidates. The best was call 239: undo16c @L16, all, scale 0.95, key_robust16 lo 8 hi 15, R = 0.231 (gate_affected 0.41, gate_others 0.13). Other scored candidates: undo16 lo5/hi10, R = 0.224; undo16b scale 0.85, R = 0.096; state16 scale 1.5, R = 0.058; undo16c lo4/hi9, R = 0.0. The submission (lo12/hi16) scored 0.144. Tightening the gate from 8-15 to 12-16 to protect the controls cut the score from 0.231 to 0.144, a small selection loss. No candidate came close to the 0.729 pass bar, so this is not a SELECTION_ERROR. The agent saw only argmax predictions and never a restoration score, so it could not rank candidates by the real metric.
analysis.counterfactual: The most likely fix was to look for the plant rather than train an answer-repair vector. Specifically: diff the residuals of affected MN cities against controls at each layer, near the earliest layer where they diverge (L5-10), and build a gated subtraction there with a looser gate (low lo). Two signs point this way. The ungated L8 repair already flipped every dev city. In the sibling .r1 run of the same instance, a gated L5 undo ('undo5' lo9/hi14) scored 0.67-0.74. Calibrating the gate to project values of all MN cities, and checking KL on free-text templates rather than argmax, would also have exposed how low the gate's coverage was. On the environment side, a restoration-style dev score on accessible cities would have shown the agent that its argmax-perfect L16 repair restored only about 0.2.
env_issues: The transcript has no assistant reasoning or text: every message is a function_call or function_call_output, so 'why it failed' cannot be read from the agent's own words, only inferred from tool calls. This is a logging gap.
optimize_vector hit an internal CUDA OOM (msg 56) and still deducted about 1400 fwd budget.
Private-city refusals ('not accessible') reject the whole batch with no indication of which city was private, so the agent spent about 15 turns bisecting lists.

The dev feedback the agent could see (argmax changed_rate, kl_on_these_prompts) is poorly matched to the graded metric (full-distribution KL restoration on private cities and free-text templates). An argmax-perfect fix on dev cities scored 0.14.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 69 of 150 turns, $0.55 of the $0.90 cap, 8878 of 12000 fwd budget used. Turns 1-18 went mostly to run_prompts calls refused for private cities or the 16-city limit. Turns 19-27 went to about 60 single-scalar vec_op norm/cos calls. The fwd budget was dominated by 9 optimize_vector calls (about 1000-1400 each, including the OOM). It stopped with 81 turns and 3122 fwd budget unused, with no turn or cost pressure, so the budget was not binding. It submitted because its argmax-based dev checks looked perfect.

factual_errors: Counterfactual misreads the sibling .r1 run. The 0.742 candidate there (audit call 155) is undo5 at L5, city_last, UNGATED. The gated version (position all, key 'marker', lo9/hi14) scored 0.670. More importantly, undo5 was itself an optimize_vector answer-target repair (targets Minnesota, plus anchors Dubuque->Iowa, Chicago->Illinois, Memphis->Tennessee, kl_weight 0.2), not a recovered plant. Its cos with -v was 0.233, slightly lower than the b150 submission's 0.255. So the evidence the analyst cites refutes the claim that the method ('train an answer-repair vector instead of finding the plant') was the decisive error. 0.742 is also above this instance's 0.729 bar, so the behavioural method was able to pass.

'The fwd budget was dominated by 9 optimize_vector calls (about 1000-1400 each)' is wrong. The measured costs were: repair12 OOM 1404, repair12 rerun 120, repair8 180, repair12g 400, repair_bal 1000, undo16 1440, undo16b 1200, undo16c 1200, state16 1000.

'The rerun worked on state_q but with KL 5.3 and spillover' is wrong. The rerun's state_q eval (#121) had kl_on_these_prompts 3.802, changed_rate 0.417 and no control flips. The 5.35 came from the fs1 city_last eval (#151), where Eden Prairie went to Harrisburg.
d5 is the layer-increment difference (mn_L5-mn_L4)-(wi_L5-wi_L4), norm 29.4, not the per-layer mean difference. The 37.6 figure is norm(mn_L5-wi_L5).
Phase 3 leaves out repair12g and repair_bal (gated L12 optimizations, turns 42-45) and says the L12 work was a single gated repair12.

Key-moment msg indices are slightly off: the undo16 optimize_vector call is msg 93 (its output is msg 94), and that quote is a composite with '...' rather than one contiguous string. Audit 'call 239' (lo8/hi15) is transcript call #237/#238 in 0-based numbering; transcript #239 is the lo12/hi16 check. All the individual quoted fragments do appear in the JSON.
missed_points: Reasoning existed but was not logged: usage shows reasoning_tokens 7739 while the messages hold zero text or reasoning items. This supports the logging-gap claim and makes it more specific.

Every b150 optimize_vector call after the OOM used kl_weight 0 and had no control-city answer anchors. The .r1 undo5 that reached 0.742 used kl_weight 0.2 plus anchors (Dubuque/Chicago/Memphis). With no distributional anchor, the L16 repairs could reach argmax-perfect results while leaving the full-distribution KL high.

The decisive difference between the .r1 0.742 and the b150 0.144 is where the edit acted and how it was gated, not the method. An ungated city_last edit before the plant (L5) suppresses the plant's gates (LAB_NOTEBOOK line 1012 calls this 'trigger suppression'). The b150 agent instead patched downstream at L16 with position all, so it depended on a hand-built key whose gate opened only 0.17-0.41 on the grader's cities (0.22 for the submission). Direction (cos_minus_v 0.22-0.26) was about the same in both runs, so WRONG_DIRECTION is not a meaningful cause.

The b150 agent had an ungated city_last candidate at L8 (repair8, #166/#167) that flipped all 5 dev cities on state_q and fs1. It was never regraded in the stored audit candidates, so its R is unknown. It is the closest analogue to the .r1 passing candidate and was abandoned in favour of L12/L16.

Rockford (Illinois) answers Nashville on fs1 in the edited model, and its key_robust16 projection is 11.4. So the plant leaks beyond MN, and the agent never tried to fix it: at lo8/hi15 Rockford changed to Des Moines, at lo12/hi16 it stayed Nashville.

The agent saw kl_on_these_prompts and kl_generic, not only argmax. Its own evals showed KL of 2-5 against the planted model on dev cities, but it had no reference to the original model to read those numbers against.

There was no turn or cost pressure: no turns_left or cost appears anywhere in the tool outputs (v0.1). It submitted at turn 69 of 150 with 3122 fwd budget left. This part of the analyst's report is correct.

The analyst rightly ruled out SELECTION_ERROR: the best b150 candidate in the audit was 0.231, against a 0.729 bar. The ground truth (gate_all spread at L8/L9/L10 with the stated b/w, solver 0.911, the test cities and the 9 templates) is accurate.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Keep the same answer-target optimize_vector approach, but apply the repair before or at the plant (L5-L8), at position city_last, ungated, with kl_weight > 0 and control-city anchors. That is exactly what scored 0.742 (above the 0.729 bar) in the sibling .r1 run. The b150 agent already had such a candidate, repair8 (L8, city_last, ungated, flipped all dev cities), and should have refined it with KL and anchors instead of moving to a gated L16 patch. A gated downstream patch depends on a hand-built key that did not generalize to the grader's cities (gate 0.22). A restoration-style dev score would have exposed this.
verdict.notes: I re-parsed all 139 messages and 243 calls. The turn, end and score facts check out: submitted at turn 69 of 150, R=0.144, cost $0.55, 8878/12000 fwd used, 27 'not accessible' refusals, one CUDA OOM that cost 1404 fwd, and submission undo16c@L16 all, scale 0.95, key_robust16 lo12/hi16. The ground truth matches private.json, and the audit numbers match failure_audit.jsonl (best 0.231 at lo8/hi15, gate_affected 0.22, cos_minus_v 0.255). The main flaw is the primary cause. WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL is refuted by the analyst's own cited sibling run: on the same instance, the same behavioural optimize_vector method scored 0.742 when applied at L5, city_last, ungated, with a KL anchor. What separates the runs is where and how the edit acts: downstream at L16 behind a narrow, poorly generalizing gate, versus upstream ungated, which suppresses the plant's triggers. The audit classifies this run as SKILL:wrong_layer,wrong_direction,wrong_gate, and the notebook says 'mis-localised a plant spread over L8-10'. I chose WRONG_LAYER as primary, with WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION as a near co-primary, since the L16 placement is what forced the gate dependence. A secondary contributor was kl_weight=0 on every b150 optimization after the OOM.

analysis.ground_truth: One plant, type 'state', Minnesota -> Tennessee. extra.plant.kind = gate_all. A single gate at layer 16: a 1536-d key, b=7.23, w=7.45, plus a 1536-d added vector, applied at every token, with the key deciding where it fires. Eval source cities are Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar and Winona, all private to the agent. Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.8414, so the pass bar is 0.8 x 0.8414 = 0.673.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent wrote no text or reasoning (every assistant message is a function_call; 3,151 reasoning tokens were never surfaced), so its beliefs have to be read from its tool calls. Every probe of a Minnesota city was refused as 'not accessible'. Its one batch with Duluth/St. Cloud/Mankato/Eden Prairie was refused as a whole, and it never retried them one by one. It therefore took the North Dakota cities as the affected set: Fargo -> Little Rock/Nashville, Grand Forks -> Nashville, Minot -> Carson City, Dickinson -> Helena (msgs 18-22). These neighbours sit inside the gate's spill-over. Around msgs 27-33 it found the layer correctly. In the layer-by-layer diff norms, L15->L16 = 21.6, against about 7 for the layers next to it, and it built 'plant' = (nd_L16-nd_L15)-(ct_L16-ct_L15). Later estimates (est, est2, then the key 'det') were orthogonalised against control-city directions. They had cos(-v) of about 0.96 with the true vector (audit diag), so its direction was correct. It gated with scale_from on 'det' at L16, with lo/hi of 0/40 or 1/41, and tried both 'all' and 'city_last'. Gate opening on affected prompts was 0.46-0.48 and on others 0.18-0.20: partial, but enough. It got the number of plants right (it treated it as one). It got the source state wrong (it targeted ND rather than MN). That did not matter, because the gate key generalised to the Minnesota cities.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-12 (msgs 1-23): behavioural survey of capitals with run_prompts on zs1/fs1/state_q. Batches over 16 cities errored, and many batches were refused whole because one city in them was private. About 10 of the 23 refusals came here, and the agent re-split batches over and over. It found anomalous ND cities (Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Dickinson) and normal controls. Turns 12-17 (msgs 23-35): ran cache_mean at all 28 layers for ND and control cities, then 27 one-off vec_op norm checks of the layer-to-layer diff. The L16 jump (21.6) localised the plant. It built 'plant' and a crude key from normalize(nd_L15-ct_L15). Turns 20-22 (msgs 39-44): projected the key and ran its first eval_intervention (plant, L16, city_last, scale -1, scale_from key lo 0 hi 5). It fixed the ND cities to Bismarck but scored only R=0.063 (audit call 83), because the gate was too strict. Turns 23-26 (msgs 45-52): cached state_q, country_q and fs1 variants. The plant estimates agreed well (cos 0.89-0.93), and it averaged them into 'est'. Turns 27-36 (msgs 53-72): cached 12 single cities, then Gram-Schmidt one vec_op per turn (u1..u8, nine turns) to project control directions out of est, giving est2. Turns 37-44 (msgs 73-88): checked est2's projections, then another one-op-per-turn Gram-Schmidt (v1..v5) to build the gate key 'det'. Turns 45-46 (msgs 89-92): det projections separated ND/SD cities (5-30) from controls (about -3 to 4). Turns 47-49 (msgs 93-98): undo = normalize(est2)*40, and two eval_interventions. Msg 95 (position all, lo 1 hi 41) audit-scored R=0.881, and msg 97 (city_last, lo 0 hi 40) audit-scored R=0.896. Both clear the bar of 0.673 and beat the solver's 0.841. The visible output showed ND fixed to Bismarck, but also some collateral changes (Tulsa -> Topeka, Omaha -> Lincoln, SD cities -> Pierre). Turns 50-60 (msgs 99-120): instead of submitting, it kept refining. It computed an SD plant estimate (cos 0.93 with est2), then a third one-op-per-turn Gram-Schmidt (v6..v13, eight turns) to orthogonalise further, apparently to cut the collateral changes. Turn 60 hit the hidden cap mid-construction, with no submit call ever made.

key_moments.quote: Some cities and prompt wordings are private to the grader; tools answer 'not accessible' for them.
key_moments.significance: The task text mentions no turn limit, so the agent had no signal that only 60 turns were available.
The agent found the plant's spill-over onto North Dakota cities. Minnesota cities, the real source, were all private.
Whole-batch refusal: one private city blocked the batch, and the agent never tried the Minnesota cities singly (refusal friction, 23 refusals in the episode).
The layer was localised correctly at L16 (neighbouring layers about 7).
First candidate (gate lo 0 hi 5, crude key). It fixed the ND cities, but the audit gives R=0.063 because the gate was too strict.
Passing candidate, audit R=0.881 (bar 0.673).
Best candidate, audit R=0.896, above the solver's 0.841. It was never submitted.
Visible collateral change. This likely drove the agent to keep refining instead of submitting, since it has no score signal.
The final turn was spent on one Gram-Schmidt step. The episode ended at max_turns with no submission.

analysis.best_candidate: Audit call 144 (msg 97, turn 49): register 'undo' (normalize(est2)*40), layer 16, position city_last, scale -1, scale_from key 'det' lo 0 hi 40. Audit R=0.8956, cos(-v)=0.962, norm ratio 1.26, gate opening 0.48 on affected and 0.20 on others. Runner-up: call 143 (msg 95), position all, lo 1/hi 41, R=0.8809. Earlier candidate: call 83 (msg 43), R=0.063. Neither of the top two was submitted. The agent cannot see the restoration score, only predictions, and the predictions showed residual collateral flips (Tulsa, Omaha). It kept refining without knowing that 11 turns remained, and the hidden 60-turn cap ended the episode first. Budget was not the constraint: $0.26 of $0.60, 282 of 12,000 forward passes.
analysis.counterfactual: Show turns remaining (or state the 60-turn cap in the task text, as v0.2 does). Or have the agent submit its best candidate as soon as one is found and refine afterwards (resubmitting if allowed). Submitting the msg-97 edit at turn 49 would have scored about 0.896, a pass and above the solver. Less turn-hungry vec_op usage would also have helped: a single expression, or fewer one-op-per-turn Gram-Schmidt steps (about 23 turns spent this way). So would per-city refusal filtering instead of whole-batch refusals (about 10 turns lost).
env_issues: Hidden 60-turn cap: no turn limit or turns-left counter appears in the task text or tool results (fixed in v0.2 per LAB_NOTEBOOK ~L1017-1029).

Whole-batch refusal: any private city in a run_prompts or project batch refuses the entire call ('not accessible'). That gave 23 refusals here and about 10 wasted turns, and it hid every Minnesota city from the agent.
No restoration feedback: eval_intervention returns only top predictions and KL on the agent's own prompts, so the agent could not tell that its candidate already passed.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 60 turns, $0.259 (cap $0.60 not reached), 282 of 12,000 forward passes. Approximate split: turns 1-12 on the behavioural survey, about 10 of them lost re-splitting refused or oversized batches. Turns 12-17 on the layer scan with 27 single-scalar vec_ops (efficient, batched in parallel). About 23 turns (msgs 55-71, 77-87, 105-119) on Gram-Schmidt, one vec_op per turn, which is the main waste. Only 4 turns on eval_intervention. Passing candidates arrived at turns 48-49, and the remaining 11 turns went into further orthogonalisation with no submit.

factual_errors: Refusal distribution is wrong. 20 of the 23 'not accessible' refusals fall in the survey phase (msgs 4, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, giving 3+1+3+3+3+4+2+1). Only 3 came later (msgs 30, 40, 92). The analysis says 'About 10 of the 23 refusals came here'.
eval_intervention was called 3 times (tool_log Counter; msgs 43, 95, 97), not on '4 turns'.

The claim that the agent never tried Minnesota cities one at a time is partly wrong. Minneapolis was probed on its own at msg 15 (call_ejjEoFpK1n8JWhZOxuHVr1Jk) and refused. Only the Duluth/St. Cloud/Mankato/Eden Prairie batch was never split up.

Collateral changes are misattributed. Omaha -> Lincoln appears only in msg 96 (position all). In the msg 98 output (the best candidate, city_last), Omaha stays Des Moines. The SD cities -> Pierre are counted as 'collateral', but Pierre is the correct capital and the SD cities project strongly on det (Sioux Falls 26.6). They are more plausibly restored plant spill-over than damage.

The counterfactual says to submit the best candidate and refine afterwards, 'resubmitting if allowed'. Resubmitting is not allowed: the submit tool 'ends the episode' (edithunt/env/agent_loop.py, submit tool schema). Only a rejected submission can be retried. So the agent's only choice was submit-and-stop or keep refining.
missed_points: Same model, same instance, with a 150-turn cap (T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-state-L16-s0.b150.json): it submitted at turn 129 with R=0.563, below the 0.673 bar, so FAIL. More turns alone did not turn this instance into a pass. The agent's refinement habit can make a working candidate worse.

The v0.2 runs on the same instance (T8u-d18af9bd .r1/.r2, failure_audit rows 19-20) showed turns_left and still ended at cost_cap with no submission. Their best unsubmitted candidates scored 0.910 and 0.931. That is the same pattern: no stopping rule once a working undo exists. It points to a strong behavioural co-cause (keeps refining without a score signal) alongside the hidden cap.

The hidden cap is confirmed in code. _with_turns appends turns_left only when constraints.show_turns is set, and the string 'turns_left' appears 0 times in this episode file. No 'Continue. Submit' nudges were ever sent, because every assistant message was a function_call.

Ground truth checked: gate_all, layer 16, b=7.233, w=7.451, eval_src = Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona. Solver 0.8414, bar 0.673. Audit rows match: call 144 R=0.8956, call 143 R=0.8809, call 83 R=0.0631.
The Gram-Schmidt turn count is confirmed at 23 turns: msgs 55-71 (9), 77-87 (6) and 105-119 (8).
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Calling submit at turn 49 with the msg-97 edit (undo = normalize(est2)*40, L16, city_last, scale -1, scale_from det lo 0 hi 40) would have scored about 0.896 (audit), a pass and above the solver. Showing turns_left (or a cost/turn budget) would probably have pushed a submit within the 11 remaining turns. Sibling runs suggest that is not enough on its own: the b150 run submitted a worse 0.563, and v0.2 runs with visible turns hit the cost cap with unsubmitted candidates of 0.91-0.93. A reliable fix also needs an explicit stopping or submit-when-good-enough instruction, or some restoration-like feedback.
verdict.notes: The core claims hold. The episode ended at max_turns (60/60, cost $0.259 of $0.60, 282 forward passes). There was no submission and no assistant text. Layer L16 was correctly localised (21.64 vs about 7). The passing candidates at msgs 95 and 97 (turns 48-49) were never submitted. The final 11 turns went into Gram-Schmidt steps v6-v13. Neither turns_left nor the cap was ever shown to the agent. Most quotes appear verbatim: the task-text line, the Fargo next_tokens, changed_rate/kl, value 21.644844, the msg-95 and msg-97 edits strings, and Tulsa -> Topeka. Two quotes do not appear verbatim. The 'msg 16-18' quote stitches tool arguments and a result together with '->'. The msg-119 quote is abbreviated with '...'. Their content is accurate, but they are not verbatim. ENV_TURNCAP_HIDDEN is a fair proximate primary cause for this episode. Still, the sibling evidence (b150 at 0.563 and v0.2 cost_cap runs) means the over-refinement / no-stopping behaviour deserves more weight than the secondary causes listed. The audit labels it ENV_TURNCAP, consistent with LAB_NOTEBOOK L1011.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.1, Minnesota->Tennessee "state" plant, one gate_all edit at L16, position all (b150 variant: 150-turn cap hidden, max_cost 0.9)
analysis.end: submitted (voluntarily, at turn 129 of 150; cost $0.633 of the $0.90 cap; 691 of 12000 fwd budget used)
analysis.ground_truth: One gate at layer 16, position 'all': h += clamp((key·h - 7.233)/7.451, 0, 1) * v, with |v| = 31.66. It fires on Minnesota cities, which are pushed to Tennessee/Nashville. The test cities are private Minnesota cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona). The solver is the true -v behind a fitted gate, R = 0.841, so the pass bar is 0.673. A script baseline (detect_v1: mean-difference key on source-state cities, layer picked by jump) reached R = 0.904.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent wrote no reasoning text; all 243 messages are tool calls, so its beliefs come from its calls. Around msgs 25-52 it decided the plant acts on the Dakota cities (Sioux Falls, Rapid City, Sturgis, Brookings, Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Dickinson), which answer South Carolina, Tennessee or North Carolina. It never named Minnesota as the source: no Minnesota city was ever queried on its own, and Minneapolis only appeared inside batches that came back 'not accessible' (msgs 7, 17, 65). It checked L23 first (msg 61), then found the large L16 jump (p16 norm 23.1 against about 7-10 at nearby layers, msg 68) and settled on layer 16 by msg 71. Layer: right. Direction: right, since cos(-32*u, -v) is about 0.98. Scale: right, since the applied norm of 32 matches |v| = 31.7. Single plant: right. Gate: wrong. The submitted key gateM has cos -0.16 with the true key. It was built by exact-fitting a few Dakota bleed cities and controls, and its targets were bleed-sized dot values.
analysis.strategy_arc: Msgs 1-28 (turns ~1-14): state_q and zs1 sweeps over known cities. Many calls failed with 'not accessible' because one private city poisoned the whole batch (Minneapolis, Deadwood, Williston, and others). The agent found Dakota cities answering Tennessee or South Carolina; these are bleed effects of the Minnesota gate. Msgs 29-60: per-layer mean-difference jumps on Dakota against control cities at city_last and final, logit lens, and a false lead at L23 (the 'pf23' direction unembeds to SC tokens). Msgs 61-72: eval_intervention with pf23 at L23 changed little. p16 at L16 city_last scale -1 flipped all Dakota cities to their correct states, so L16 was settled. Msgs 73-104: built plant (cos 0.96 across templates), key, plant2 and p16c from Dakota-minus-control L16-L15 differences. Msgs 105-168: Gram-Schmidt projection of control directions out of plant to get u, then about 30 hand-written vec_op calls building a gate vector 'gate' that exactly interpolates chosen dot targets per city (31.94 for Sioux Falls, 7.22 for Dickinson, and so on). Msgs 169-246: evaluated u at -40 with gates 'gate' and 'gateM' on Dakota and control cities (the controls were unaffected). Extended gateM with more constraints (-10 targets for Myrtle Beach and Pawtucket; country_q targets). Msgs 247-256: checked gateM dot values in a free-text template and a misleading-context template; it fires in all of them (about 22-32). Msg 257: submitted u, L16, all, scale -32, scale_from gateM with lo 0 and hi 32. The agent never saw a restoration score and never tested any Minnesota city.

key_moments.significance: Minneapolis, the one Minnesota city it ever tried, was inside a batch rejected as private. The agent never followed up with accessible Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Eden Prairie, Bemidji were all in known_cities), so the true source state was never found.
Bleed from the Minnesota gate onto a neighbouring North Dakota city. The agent took the Dakotas to be the plant's targets and used them as the 'source' set for both the direction and the gate.
Correct layer found (L16). The direction is correct as well; it ends at cos about 0.98 with the true v.

The gate key was built by exact Gram-Schmidt interpolation of about 12 single-city targets taken from bleed-sized responses on Dakota cities. The resulting key (cos -0.16 with the true key) does not generalize to Minnesota.
The gate fired as strongly in the 'French village named {city}' prompt as in the normal one, a sign the gate was not specific to the plant. The agent submitted anyway.

Final submission. It graded R = 0.563 with restoration_src = 0.498: about half the plant's effect on the Minnesota test cities was undone. Off-target damage was negative (damage_unaffected -42), meaning prompts the plant did not affect got closer to the original model, not worse.

analysis.best_candidate: The tools never returned a reward, so no candidate in this b150 episode has a visible score. Candidates evaluated behaviourally: (1) pf23 at L23, all, scale -1 (msg 61): little effect. (2) p16 at L16, city_last, scale -1 (msg 71): fixed the Dakota cities. (3) u at L16, all, -40, gate 'gate' 0-40 (msgs 169/171). (4) u at L16, all, -40, gateM 0-40 (msgs 227/245): controls unchanged, Dakota cities fixed. (5) u at L16, city_last, -40, gateM (msg 231). (6) Submitted: u, L16, all, -32, gateM 0-32 -> R = 0.563, below the 0.673 bar. There is no failure_audit row for this b150 run. In the r1 (60-turn) run of the same instance, similar submittable candidates reached R 0.88-0.90 but were never submitted (turn cap). This shows the direction and scale were achievable; this episode's gate key was what failed.
analysis.counterfactual: Probe the accessible Minnesota cities one at a time (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji) to learn that Minnesota is the source. Then build the gate key as normalize(MN_L16 - control_L16), with lo/hi at 30%-60% of the gap between control and Minnesota projections (the detect_v1 recipe, R 0.90). Keep the agent's existing u at -32. That would most likely have passed. Even with only Dakota cities, a single mean-difference key with a ramp, instead of exact per-city interpolation, would likely have generalized better.
env_issues: run_prompts/cache_mean reject the whole batch with 'not accessible' if any one city is private, without saying which. About 15 calls were wasted bisecting batches, and the agent dropped Minneapolis without trying other Minnesota cities.
No tool reports a restoration estimate, so the agent could not see that its gate under-fired on source cities. This is by design, but it makes gate calibration blind.
The 150-turn cap is hidden in v0.1. The agent submitted at turn 129, possibly earlier than it otherwise would have; this was not the main cause.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 129 turns at $0.633 (under the $0.90 cap). Only 691 of 12000 forward passes were used, so compute was not a constraint. About 15 turns went to bisecting 'not accessible' batches. About 60 turns (msgs 105-226) went to hand-written Gram-Schmidt vec_op chains, one constraint per turn, building u and the gate. That approach overfit; a single optimize_vector or mean-difference key would have taken a few calls. No turns were spent identifying the source state or testing on its cities, which was the decisive gap.

factual_errors: The analysis says 'all 243 messages are tool calls'. The episode has 259 messages: 129 assistant messages, 130 user/tool-result messages and the task prompt. The 243 figure is the number of function_call items, many of which run in parallel within one assistant message. It is true that the agent wrote no text or reasoning.

The msg 65-66 quote '"cities": "<4:Bangor,Baltimore,Worcester,Minneapolis..>" -> {"error":"not accessible"' does not appear in the JSON. The actual call is {"template":"state_q","cities":["Bangor","Baltimore","Worcester","Minneapolis"],...} and its result is {"error":"not accessible",...}. Three other quotes ('"expr": "gate+q6..."', '"expr": "dot(sfmin_L16,gateM)"' and '{"register": "u", "layer": 16, ...}') add spaces after colons and commas that the stored arguments do not have. Their content matches but they are not byte-verbatim. The Minot, p16-norm and Sioux Falls quotes are verbatim.

The analyst misreads the 'French village named {city}' check (msgs 253-256). In the same batch the agent measured the plant's own write along u for that prompt: dot(sfmin_L16-sfmin_L15-(ctl_L16-ctl_L15),u) = 25.69. So the true plant fires there too, and gateM's 26.40 tracks it correctly. This is not evidence that the gate was non-specific. The agent's check came out consistent, which is why it submitted.

The analysis says the gate targets were 'bleed-sized dot values'. Sioux Falls (31.94) and Minot (31.61) match |v| = 31.66, so the true gate is saturated, fully open, on those Dakota cities. Only Brookings (12.4) and Dickinson (7.2) are partial.

The analysis reads damage_unaffected = -42 as 'prompts the plant did not affect got closer to the original model'. These are non-source prompts, and the plant did affect them by spilling over: eval_oth includes the Dakota cities Deadwood and Williston, plus Sioux City and Scottsbluff. Their KL fell because the agent's Dakota-tuned fix undid that spill. This is where part of the 0.563 came from (R 0.563 > restoration_src 0.498).
'About 15 calls were wasted bisecting': there are 13 'not accessible' results, in tool-result msgs 8-28, 52 and 66. Minor overstatement.

The cost profile says 'No turns were spent identifying the source state... which was the decisive gap'. The r1 sibling of this same instance shows that identifying the source state was not decisive. At r1 msg 17 the agent's batch [Duluth, St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie] was refused because Duluth is private, and it never named Minnesota either. It still built a Dakota-based gate ('det': a plant estimate est2 with 5 control directions projected out, a single direction). Its candidates (undo L16, scale -1, scale_from det 0-40 / 1-41) were graded at 0.896 and 0.881 by the audit, above the 0.673 bar.
missed_points: Counter-evidence from the same instance: in r1, which also never identified Minnesota and also used Dakota cities, a single orthogonalised plant-direction key gave candidates graded at 0.896 (failure_audit.jsonl row 5). The passing hop2 b150 episode (LAB_NOTEBOOK ~985) keyed scale_from on u itself, also built from spillover cities. So the failure is specific to how the gate key was built (exact per-city Gram-Schmidt interpolation plus hard -10 constraints), not to the choice of cities.

A plausible mechanism for the under-firing: gateM adds a -10 target along q0 = normalize(ctl_L16), the mean control residual, and along template-mean control residuals (ctf_L16, plus q1-q3 from Billings, Casper and Omaha). Those directions carry a large shared component of every city's residual. After those and the Myrtle Beach/Pawtucket -10 constraints, Dakota country_q projections fell from about 20-28 (msg 200) to about 8-20 (msg 216). The same suppression probably lowered the dot products on the Minnesota test cities, which fits restoration_src = 0.498. This cannot be verified without the model.

Numbers from ground truth: cos(gateM, true key) = -0.165, cos(gateM, v) = +0.55, and cos(true key, v) = -0.68. The submitted u is a unit vector with cos(u, v) = +0.98, so -32u is about -v. The direction and scale claims check out.

The agent never saw a turn count or cost. v0.1 tool results carry only budget_left, with no turns_left or tool_calls_left. It submitted at turn 129 with 21 hidden turns left, without testing any Minnesota city that might be accessible (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji and Eden Prairie are not on the held list; Bemidji and Eden Prairie are fit_src cities).
LAB_NOTEBOOK (~line 1044) already flags this episode as 'large run-to-run variance' against its r1 sibling, which held a 0.896 candidate.

The agent's earlier, simpler 'gate' (before gateM, msg 172) kept controls near 0, but Pawtucket and Myrtle Beach reached about 11-13 on it. That spill drove the extra constraints that probably hurt generalisation. There is no evidence the simpler gate was graded.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Keep u at L16, all, scale -32. Replace the exactly interpolated gateM with one smooth key: either the plant-direction estimate with control directions projected out (r1's 'det', lo 0-1, hi 40-41, graded 0.88-0.90 on this instance), or u itself as in the passing hop2 b150 run. Then calibrate lo/hi against Dakota and control projections. That would most likely have passed without ever finding Minnesota. Probing the accessible Minnesota cities one at a time (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji) and building the key from MN minus controls (the detect_v1 recipe, 0.904) would have made a pass more certain still, but it was not necessary.
verdict.notes: I checked the run JSON (259 messages, 243 calls, all of them read), the private instance file, failure_audit.jsonl, cache.jsonl, LAB_NOTEBOOK 955-1050 and the r1 sibling transcript. These are correct: reward 0.563, restoration_src 0.498, solver 0.841 (bar 0.673), detect_v1 0.904, end = submitted at turn 129 with $0.633 spent and 691 forward passes used, the L16 jump (p16 23.11), the L23 false lead, the Minot Tennessee 0.9345 result, the submission (u, L16, all, -32, gateM 0-32), and cos 0.98 / -0.16. The primary label WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION holds: layer, direction, scale and position were all right, and only the gate key was off. Three things are wrong. The analyst calls the missing Minnesota identification the 'decisive gap', and the r1 sibling disproves that. The French-village check is misread. The quotes are not all verbatim. Secondary causes: INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION (about 30 one-constraint-per-turn vec_op calls) is fair. PREMATURE_SUBMIT is weak: the agent did not know the turn cap, and it submitted after a check that came out consistent.

analysis.instance_kind: MN->TN two L8: two gated state plants. Gate 1 at L8 changes Minnesota to Tennessee; gate 2 at L14 changes California to Pennsylvania
analysis.end: max_turns (60/60 turns, no submission). The turn cap was hidden. Only 287 of 12000 forward passes were used, and cost was $0.33 of the $0.60 limit
analysis.ground_truth: The private file (extra.plant) has kind gate_all, type two, and planted_states [[Minnesota,Tennessee],[California,Pennsylvania]]. Gate 0 is at layer 8 (b=7.79, w=7.79) and moves Minnesota cities toward Tennessee. Gate 1 is at layer 14 (b=-1.16, w=5.54) and moves California cities toward Pennsylvania. Both use position 'all' with a key-gated input-dependent vector (undo.make_instance, two: L2 = L+6). eval_src has 19 cities: 6 from Minnesota (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona) and 13 from California. Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.8669, so the PASS bar is 0.6935.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning items, only function_call and function_call_output, so beliefs are inferred from the tool calls. By about turn 17 (msg 33) the agent believed there was one plant: a 'Pennsylvania' direction added between L13 and L14 at the city token, firing on some Arizona, Nevada and California cities (Tucson, Las Vegas, San Jose, Scottsdale, Mesa). Its first diff scan (msg 23) showed the clearest spike at the L13->L14 transition (28.67), and it only ever worked at L14. Layer 14, the target Pennsylvania and the existence of a gate were correct for plant #2. It never formed any belief about the Minnesota->Tennessee plant at L8. It never queried an accessible Minnesota city (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Eden Prairie, Bemidji) or a Tennessee city. Its only Minnesota probe, Minneapolis, was refused as private (msg 37-38). It treated the task as one plant throughout.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-9 (msg 1-20): behavioural probing. Early errors: more than 16 cities in one call, and several private cities that came back 'not accessible' (Los Angeles, Anchorage, San Francisco). It found Tucson answering 'Pennsylvania' (state_q p=0.59) and Seattle's capital as Albany/Harrisburg. Turns 11-12 (msg 21-24): cached Tucson and Chicago at all 28 layers and took norms of the layer-delta differences; the L13->L14 spike (28.67) pointed to L14. Turns 14-24 (msg 27-48): built the difference-of-means registers plant, p2 and p3 ((L14-L13) delta of Pennsylvania-affected cities minus controls). It used eval_intervention at L14 city_last with scale -1 to restore Tucson, Las Vegas and San Jose. Turn 25 (msg 49): tried a gated version, p3 at all positions, scale -1.25, scale_from key=punit with lo=3, hi=25. Turns 26-33 (msg 51-66): cached about 30 more single cities at L13/L14 and refined the direction (p4, p5, p6; cos(p4,p5)=0.99). Turns 34-59 (msg 67-117): about 25 turns hand-coding a ridge regression and conjugate-gradient solve for a gate key (rk), entirely through vec_op string expressions (b1..b4, a1..a4, dp, rr, rnew loops). One expression failed with 'expression too long'. Turn 60 (msg 119): evaluated p6 gated by rk (lo=-0.0437, hi=0.956) and hit the hidden 60-turn cap before calling submit. It never probed Minnesota or Tennessee cities, never looked at layer 8, and never considered a second plant.

key_moments.significance: Found the side effect of plant #2 (the CA->PA gate leaking onto Arizona cities). This set the whole investigation on the Pennsylvania plant only.
The L13->L14 delta spike. This correctly located plant #2 at L14, but the analysis only contrasted Tucson with Chicago, so the L8 Minnesota plant could not appear.

The only time a Minnesota city was ever queried, and it was batched with a private city, so the whole call was refused. The agent never retried with St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead or Bemidji, which were accessible.
The first working L14 undo. Audit R=0.447 for the plant register at city_last.
The best candidate of the episode (audit R=0.607). It is still below the 0.6935 bar because the Minnesota plant is left untouched.
The start of about 25 turns of manual ridge-regression and CG iterations done through vec_op strings. This used up the rest of the hidden turn budget.
The last action was another evaluation rather than a submit (audit R=0.563). The episode ended at max_turns with reward 0.

analysis.best_candidate: Call 96 (msg 49): p3 at L14, position all, scale -1.25, scale_from key=punit with lo=3, hi=25. Audit R=0.607 (cos_minus_v 0.63, gate_affected 0.48, gate_others 0.25). The other candidates were p6 gated by rk (R=0.563), p3 at L14 city_last (R=0.452) and plant at L14 city_last (R=0.447). None reached the 0.6935 PASS bar. Nothing was submitted because the agent kept refining the gate and hit the hidden 60-turn cap. Even submitting the best candidate would have failed. The same agent with 150 turns (.b150) submitted a similar L14-only gate at turn 91 and scored 0.593, which confirms the approach tops out around 0.6.
analysis.counterfactual: The agent needed to find and undo the second plant: probe accessible Minnesota cities such as St. Cloud, Mankato or Moorhead (they would have shown Tennessee/Nashville answers), then add a second rank-1 gated -v edit at L8 alongside the L14 edit (max_rank=2 allows this). On the environment side, telling the agent that there may be more than one plant, or showing turns_left, would at least have produced a submission of about 0.6. That would still be a fail.
env_issues: Hidden 60-turn cap: the episode ended with no submission even though only 287/12000 forward passes and $0.33 of $0.60 had been used. This turned an R of about 0.6 into 0.0, but did not change pass/fail.
No assistant text or reasoning was saved in messages (only function_call and function_call_output items), so the agent's 'why' can only be inferred from its tool calls.

Generic refusal of a whole batch when any one city is private (14 refusals in this run). The only Minnesota probe (Minneapolis, which is a private eval city) was refused, which hid the second plant from the agent.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: There were 60 turns, mostly parallel tool calls, costing $0.33. About 10 turns went on behavioural probing, including several wasted on errors and refusals (more than 16 cities, private cities). About 10 went on building the L14 difference-of-means direction and evaluations. About 8 went on single-city caching. About 25 turns (msg 67-117) went on hand-running ridge-regression and CG through vec_op expressions, which needed no forward passes but used up the hidden turn budget. No turns were spent on Minnesota, Tennessee or layers other than 13/14.

factual_errors: The analyst says the only Minnesota probe was Minneapolis at msg 37-38. Minneapolis was also in the batches at msg 1 (rejected with 'give 1..16 cities') and msg 3 (refused as 'not accessible'). There were three attempts and all failed. The point that no accessible MN city was ever queried still holds.

Key moment msg 38 says Minneapolis 'was batched with a private city, so the whole call was refused'.
