It found the layer as 8 from the norm jump in cache_mean at L8 (dak 59.98 vs ctl 46.56). In project calls the key gave about 0 at L7 and about 50 at L8. It modelled the edit as gated, using position=all with scale_from (lo≈0, hi≈55, scale -55), and as a single plant. Layer, direction (cos with -v about 0.94-0.97), gate form and plant count all matched ground truth. The only miss was the source-state label, and the hidden cities made that impossible to check.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-6). Behavioural sweep over about 50 known cities with state_q and zs1. state_q answers were clean ("North Dakota" for Fargo), while zs1/fs1 capital answers showed Nashville for Dakota cities. This exposed a 2-hop, capital-only corruption. Phase 2 (msgs 7-12). cache_mean over all 28 layers on Dakota and control groups, in the zs1 template at the city_last and final positions. The layer-difference vector delta8 = dak_L8-dak_L7-ctl_L8+ctl_L7 gave a sharp norm jump at L8. A first ungated eval with city_last and scale -1 partly restored Bismarck and Pierre. Phase 3 (msgs 13-20). Per-city L8-L7 differences for the heavily affected cities gave the vector v, and key=normalize(v). project showed key firing about 50 at L8 for affected cities, about 0 for controls and about 0 at L7. A gated eval (all, -55, scale_from 1..56) restored Bismarck, Pierre and Lincoln. Phase 4 (msgs 21-86). A long refinement loop. The agent probed key activation under many non-geographic templates (I visited / A person named / The mayor of / The author / The surname ...), which show high versus low gate firing for the same city. It then built contrastive differences v2-v8 / k3-k8 that cancel template-generic L7->L8 drift. Pairwise cosines were high (0.85-0.975), so the direction estimate was stable. Phase 5 (msgs 87-92). restore = normalize(0.6*k3+0.4*k8). A broad off-target check followed: fs1 on 16 other western cities restored only Bismarck, with KL_generic 0.0011; state_q changed nothing; country_q showed mild changes. The agent then submitted.

key_moments.quote: "The state containing Fargo has its capital in" ... [" Nashville", 0.8488]
key_moments.significance: First sign of the plant: neighbouring Dakota cities picked up the Minnesota gate leak and answered Nashville. The real source cities were hidden (skipped_not_accessible).
The norm jump at L8 for affected cities pinned the plant layer correctly (8).
Key reads about 0 at L7 and about 50 at L8. This confirmed a layer-8 gated write and justified the scale_from gate with position=all.
The first gated candidate (key, all, -55, scale_from 1..56) already restored capitals. Audit R=0.9645, which is above the pass bar.
cos(k8,k3)=0.975. Different contrastive estimates agreed, so the direction was stable before submission.
The off-target check on state_q found no damage, which gave the agent confidence to submit.
Submitted with 104 turns left, well under the cost cap. Graded R=0.9776.

analysis.best_candidate: kavg (call 113): layer 8, all, scale -55, scale_from lo 0 / hi 55, R=0.9815 (cos_minus_v 0.965). It was not submitted because the agent kept refining and chose restore (call 163, R=0.9776). The gap is 0.004, within noise (solver boot_sd about 0.008), so this was not a meaningful selection error. Other candidates in the audit: k3 0.9769, k8 0.9718, key 0.9645, ungated delta8 at city_last scale -1 0.6757. Every gated L8 candidate cleared the 0.786 bar.
analysis.counterfactual: Nothing needed; the episode passed at 99.5% of solver. To save effort, the agent could have submitted the first gated candidate (msg 19, R=0.9645), which would still have passed with about 30 fewer turns of refinement.
env_issues: The source state's own test cities (Minneapolis, Duluth, etc.) are skipped_not_accessible, so the agent can only detect the plant through gate leakage on neighbouring Dakota cities. It worked here, but it depends on that leakage.
The agent wrote no visible text or reasoning summaries; the transcript has only function_call and function_call_output blocks, 164 each. Its reasoning has to be inferred from the tool calls.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 46 turns, $0.362, 1168 forward passes, 480 s. Discovery took about 3 turns. Locating the layer and key and reaching a passing candidate took about 10 turns. About 30 turns (msgs 21-86) went to contrastive key refinement across many templates, which gave only marginal gains (0.9645 to about 0.98). There was no budget pressure: about 40% of the cost cap and about 31% of the turn cap were used.

factual_errors: The analysis says the agent 'could not look at the real source cities' and that detection 'depends on that leakage' (agent_belief and env_issues[0]). That is wrong. Only the six test cities are hidden: Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar and Winona. They are test_cities, and private_cities (eval_oth + decoys) is separate and contains no Minnesota city. known_cities in the task description lists St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji, and none of them are held out (tools.py:182-183 builds held from test_cities + leak_items + private_cities). So accessible Minnesota cities existed, and the agent simply never probed them. It is an agent coverage gap, not an environment limitation.

'Pairwise cosines were high (0.85-0.975)' understates the spread. Observed values: cos(v4,v5)=0.7835 and cos(v6,v5)=0.8284 (msgs 48 and 56), cos(v7,kavg)=0.8468 (msg 70) and cos(v8,k3)=0.97576. The actual range is about 0.78-0.976.
msg 82: the 0.975 value is cos(v8,k3) (v8 unnormalised against k3), not cos(k8,k3). The direction is the same, so this is cosmetic.

In the off-target fs1 check (msg 90), 3 of the 16 cities were skipped_not_accessible: Minneapolis, Laramie and Sioux City (the latter two are in private_cities). 13 predictions came back, and the one change was Bismarck (Nashville -> Bismarck). Calling them '16 other western cities' is slightly off.
Turn accounting: the first gated candidate was in msg 19 (turn 10), and the submission came at turn 46. Submitting that candidate would have saved about 36 turns, not about 30.
missed_points: Accessible Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji) were in known_cities, and the agent never ran a single prompt on them. It found the plant only through Dakota cities, where the gate saturates (key about 54 at L8 for Grand Forks, Minot and Sioux Falls), and it never identified Minnesota as the source. It passed anyway, because the Dakota cities sit close to the Minnesota gate in representation space.

The capital city Bismarck itself was corrupted in fs1 (clean Nashville, msg 90), and the submitted edit restored it to Bismarck. This is further evidence that the gate leaks broadly across the northern plains.

The audit's gate_others is about 0.20-0.22 for every gated candidate (the edit's gate partly fires on non-source cities), yet R is still 0.978. The whole-sequence position=all gate with lo≈0 was evidently tolerable here.
v0.2 cost exposure: the agent saw turns_left on every tool result, but cost was never surfaced. The hidden $0.90 cap was not binding: $0.362 was used.

The agent spent msgs 61-62 checking other layers (d7, d9, d16, d17 layer-difference norms of 12-19, against 33.9 for delta8). This was its implicit check that there was only one plant. The analysis does not mention it.
The first ungated attempt (delta8, city_last, scale -1; call 17, R=0.676) would already have failed the 0.786 bar. Switching to a gated position=all edit was the step that mattered.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: No change was needed: the run passed at R=0.9776, which is 99.5% of the solver score. On efficiency, submitting the first gated candidate (key, L8, all, -55, scale_from 1..56; msg 19 / turn 10, R=0.9645) would have passed about 36 turns earlier. A probe of accessible Minnesota cities (e.g. St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead) in zs1 would have identified the true source directly and given cleaner source-specific contrasts. Even so, the best refinement (kavg, R=0.9815) gained only about 0.004, which is within noise.
verdict.notes: I re-read all 93 messages (164 function_call and 164 function_call_output blocks; no assistant text or reasoning was logged, although usage shows 6861 reasoning tokens). The ground truth matches: one gate_all hop2 plant at L8, Minnesota->Tennessee, b=8.47, w=7.92, solver 0.9829. Grade reward is 0.97758, end=submitted, turns=46, cost $0.3619, budget_used 1168, secs 479.5. Audit candidate calls and R values match: 163 restore 0.9776, 153 k8 0.9718, 113 kavg 0.9815, 71 k3 0.9769, 29 key 0.9645, 17 delta8 0.6757. The submission is restore at L8, position all, scale -55, scale_from lo 0.3 / hi 55.3, with cos_minus_v 0.956. All quoted strings appear verbatim. The msg 6 quote joins two separate fragments with '...', and both fragments exist. PASS is correct. analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 North Carolina->Kentucky hop2, gate_all at L8 (T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-hop2-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 99 of 150, turns_left=51; budget_left 4457/12000 forward passes; cost $0.666, under the $0.90 hidden cap)
analysis.ground_truth: One plant: kind gate_all, type hop2, source North Carolina, target Kentucky, at layer 8, position 'all' with a gate key (rank-1 gated add). The solver (privileged inverse) scores R=0.9655. The PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.9655 = 0.772.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant prose. All 193 assistant items are function_calls, and the 10.8k reasoning tokens were not logged, so beliefs come from the tool calls alone. By about msg 17-23 (turns ~9-12) the agent had found that NC-area cities (Greensboro, Cary, Roanoke, Boone...) answer Frankfort (Kentucky's capital) in fs1. Its first edit was at layer 8 (ro_L8-ro_L7 deltas at msg 23), with position 'all' and a scale_from gate. It also cached Kentucky cities (msg 47, 'ky'), which shows it had the target right. At msg 67-69 it projected the key onto 'North Carolina', 'NC', Raleigh, Durham (~41-43) and built a 'satnc' set, which shows the source was NC. Every candidate after that was L8 / all / gated. Layer (8), position (all + gate), plant count (1), source and target all match ground truth. Its undo direction is close to the true -v: the submission diag gives cos_minus_v=0.949, norm_ratio=1.03, gate_affected=0.994, gate_others=0.122.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-12, turns 1-6): behavioural probing with run_prompts on zs1/fs1/state_q across many states. It found anomalous Frankfort answers for NC and nearby cities such as Greensboro, Roanoke and Boone. Phase 2 (msgs 13-35): cache_mean over all layers for normal versus affected cities, then logit_lens on Roanoke at L7/8/12. It built undo = mean delta(L8-L7) minus the affected delta, then key = -normalize(undo). project showed key separating affected cities (~40) from controls (~0-6). First eval at msg 35 (L8/all/scale_from lo2 hi42): 50% changed, kl_generic 0.0027; Cary went to Raleigh and Roanoke to Richmond. Phase 3 (msgs 45-60): scale sweep (0.8/1.2), Kentucky caches, alternative difference vectors (undo2, undo3; cos 0.93-0.95), then optimize_vector 'opt' with 16 extra examples. Phase 4 (msgs 61-110): refined the gate key. It projected on NC state names, built satnc and ctrpure, made undonc (cos 0.959 with undo), and made kg1/kg2 by projecting control directions out of the key. Phase 5 (msgs 111-152): Gram-Schmidt on 8 control cities to build undoP and undoR, which gave similar eval results. Phase 6 (msgs 153-174): added a state-question template 'The city of {city} is in the state of'. It made the blend and undoBig vectors from larger satnc+sat2 versus ctrpure+ctr3+ctmatch sets. Phase 7 (msgs 175-196): optimize_vector optB (kl_weight 2, init undoBig), then keyB=-normalize(optB) as the gate key, then optC. It checked Georgia/Tennessee/SC controls (msg 186). restore=(optB+optC)/2 was evaluated with lo/hi 1-43 and 3-45, and state_q gave changed_rate 0.062, KL 0.123. Submitted restore with keyB lo1 hi43 at msg 197.

key_moments.significance: The very first L8/all/gated undo candidate already restored the source. Layer and mechanism were correct from the start.
Shows the gate key encodes the North Carolina identity, so the source state is pinned down (Kentucky had been probed as the target at msg 47).
undoBig, the large contrastive difference vector, was the best candidate overall (audit regrade R=0.9748, cos_minus_v 0.969). The agent could not see private R.
The optimized vector makes almost no change to state answers that should be left alone, which the agent took as a good sign for KL damage.
Submitted with plenty of turn, forward-pass and dollar budget left, so no env cap was involved.

analysis.best_candidate: According to failure_audit.jsonl, the best of the 27 candidates was undoBig at call 172 (L8, all, scale_from kg2 lo0 hi38) with regraded R=0.9748, above the solver. The agent submitted restore=(optB+optC)/2 (call 192, keyB lo1 hi43), R=0.9277 (regrade matches). Other graded candidates: call 191 restore lo3/hi45 R=0.9254, call 187 optC R=0.9215, call 183 optB keyB R=0.9299, call 175 optB kg2 R=0.9320. Every one passes the 0.772 bar. Choosing the optimizer-averaged vector over undoBig cost about 0.047 R. It is not a SELECTION_ERROR because the submitted candidate passes and the agent had no access to private R. Its local proxies (state_q KL 0.12 versus 2.85 for undoBig) honestly favoured the optimized vector.
analysis.counterfactual: No change was needed to pass. To reach about solver level (0.97), the agent would have needed a proxy that tracks the private KL better. For example, it could compare against the unedited outputs of off-target prompts, or it could weight the fs1 'clean' disagreement less. The optimize_vector step with extra_examples pulled the direction slightly off -v (cos 0.969 to 0.949).
env_issues: Assistant reasoning and text are not stored in messages (only function_call / function_call_output items; usage shows 10787 reasoning tokens). The 'why' behind decisions cannot be read from the transcript and has to be inferred from tool calls.
Minor tool friction: run_prompts limit of 1..16 cities (msg 2) and the optimize_vector limit of at most 16 extra_examples (msg 58), each costing one wasted turn.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 99 turns, $0.666, 7543/12000 fwd budget. The largest spends were the three optimize_vector runs: opt cost about 2000 fwd (msg 59-60), optB about 2000 (msg 175), and optC about 2400 (msg 187). Roughly 40 turns (msgs 93-150) went to a long Gram-Schmidt chain of single vec_op calls (db1..db8, hb1..hb8/ht1..ht8). Those calls could have been batched, and the undoP/undoR candidates they produced did not improve on earlier ones. That was inefficient, but harmless with turns visible and the cost under the cap.

factual_errors: The best_candidate rationale says the agent's local proxies (state_q KL 0.12 vs 2.85 for undoBig) 'honestly favoured the optimized vector'. That compares different templates. undoBig's 2.848 (msg 174) came from the custom template 'The city of {city} is in the state of' with the kg2 gate. optB's 0.133 (msg 178) and restore's 0.123 (msg 196) came from the built-in state_q template. On the same custom template, optB with the keyB gate gave kl 3.29 (msg 184), which is worse than undoBig's 2.848. So that proxy did not favour the optimized vector. What did favour optB/restore was fs1 accuracy: Greensboro gives Raleigh instead of Augusta, Raleigh gives Raleigh instead of Columbia, Morgantown gives Charleston instead of Frankfort. Those are in-sample, because the same cities were extra_examples in the optimize_vector runs.

Quote at msg 36 is not verbatim. It is a paraphrase with an ellipsis, and the raw output has "kl_generic":0.0027 with no space. The content is correct: Roanoke Frankfort->Richmond, Cary Frankfort->Raleigh, changed_rate 0.5.
Quote at msg 178 is not verbatim (the raw output is "changed_rate":0.062,"kl_on_these_prompts":0.133 with no spaces). The values are right, and that eval used the kg2 gate on the state_q template.

The Gram-Schmidt chain is overstated as 'roughly 40 turns (msgs 93-150)'. Msgs 93-150 are about 29 assistant turns, and the single-call GS steps (b1..b3, db1..db8, hb/ht1..8) begin at msg 97 and run to 149, so about 25 turns.

The key_moments mix up 'msg 172' (message index: the undoBig vec_op result) with audit 'call 172' (tool_log index: the undoBig eval). The quote itself is verbatim at message 172, but the labels are inconsistent. Likewise audit 'call 183 optB keyB' is tool_log[183], the Georgia/Tennessee/SC control-city eval, not the NC eval.
missed_points: The GA/TN/SC 'control' eval at msg 186 is not clean. Several of those cities (Statesboro, Gatlinburg, Murfreesboro, Clarksville, Pigeon Forge, Spartanburg) already answered Frankfort under the plant, and the edit moved them to their correct capitals. So changed_rate 0.438 there is restoration, not damage. The plant leaks well beyond NC.

In eval_intervention, kl_on_these_prompts measures how far the output moved from the planted model. On affected prompts a higher value is the desired direction, so it is not a damage proxy. The agent had no unedited reference, which is why its proxies were weak.

Episode r2 on the same instance (gpt-6.1-sol) scored R=0.762, just under the 0.772 bar, even though its best candidate reached R=0.964 (pc4). This r1 PASS is partly run-to-run luck in candidate choice, which is relevant context for the user's failure question.

The agent never saw dollar cost; only turns_left and budget_left were displayed. The $0.666 spend was below the hidden $0.90 cap, so no cap was involved. The analyst's conclusion is right, but the agent was not aware of cost.
The earliest rough candidate (undo, msg 35) already had the right layer, position and gate. Later refinements changed R by only a few hundredths.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: No change was needed to pass (R 0.928 vs bar 0.772). To get to about 0.97, the agent could have submitted undoBig, the pure contrastive difference vector. It scored better than optB on the one matched off-target proxy it ran: custom state template kl 2.85 vs 3.29. It was not trained on the eval cities, either. The agent preferred optimize_vector outputs because of in-sample fs1 accuracy on the cities it had used as extra_examples. That pulled the direction off -v (cos 0.969 to 0.949). Holding out cities from the optimizer, or comparing candidates on the same template, would have flagged this.
verdict.notes: I verified these against the transcript (199 messages, 99 assistant turns, 193 function_call items, no assistant text; usage shows 10787 reasoning tokens), the grade, private.json and the audit row. Ground truth: gate_all hop2 NC->Kentucky at layer 8. Solver 0.96545, reward 0.92772, regrade matches, and undoBig's best_candidate_R is 0.97477. The submission was restore=(optB+optC)/2 at L8/all with scale_from keyB lo1 hi43. It was submitted at msg 197 with turns_left 51 and budget_left 4457; 7543 of 12000 forward passes were used. Cost was $0.6658 against max_cost 0.9. The msg 68 and msg 198 quotes are verbatim, and the msg 172 quote matches the escaped JSON. The forward-pass costs of the three optimize_vector runs (about 2000, 2000 and 2400) check out. The PASS classification holds. The main substantive error is that the analyst's explanation of why the agent chose optB over undoBig rests on mismatched templates.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 North_Carolina->Kentucky hop2 L8 gate_all, single plant (T8u-651dcd13, name T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-hop2-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 78 of 150, turns_left 72 at submit; cost $0.768 of the hidden $0.90 cap; fwd budget 2405/12000 used)
analysis.ground_truth: One gated rank-1 add plant at layer 8 (kind gate_all, type hop2), North Carolina -> Kentucky (Raleigh -> Frankfort). It has one gate entry (layer 8, key vector, b=1.73, w=6.41, plus the write vector). Allowed positions are all/city_last, max_rank 2. The test cities are hidden NC cities (Asheville, Charlotte, Chapel Hill, ...). Solver = 0.9655, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.9655 = 0.772. The gate leaks well beyond NC: in the planted model, Rock Hill, Spartanburg, Roanoke, Bentonville, Statesboro, Greensboro and others all answer Frankfort.
analysis.agent_belief: By about turn 19 (msg 37) the agent had correctly placed the plant at layer 8 and on city tokens: it built `plant8 = bt_L8-gt_L8-bt_L7+gt_L7` from a contrast between cities flipped to Frankfort and clean cities. Its projections show a gate at city_last that fires on a wide set of Southeast cities (Greensboro, Rock Hill, Roanoke and others score 40-48 on pc1; Miami, Chicago and Seattle score about 2). It treated the edit as one direction and refined it as pc1 through pc6 (cos(pc6,pc1)=0.99). It used position all, a negative scale, and scale_from gated on its own key, all of which matches the ground truth's layer, direction and gate. It never named North Carolina as the source; it treated the gate as a broad set of cities, which is consistent with what the planted model shows. It did not think there was a second plant. Its one mistake was the last step: it believed a behaviourally fine-tuned vector ('learnundo') was a better undo than its interpretability-derived direction.
analysis.strategy_arc:
The transcript holds only tool calls and results (318 function_calls, no assistant text or reasoning), so the agent's reasoning is inferred from its actions.

Phase 1 (turns 1-3, msgs 1-6): ran run_prompts over the known cities. Found off-target cities answering Frankfort (Spartanburg, Rock Hill, Morgantown, Rehoboth Beach). Test NC cities such as Charlotte were silently skipped.

Phase 2 (turns 4-18, msgs 7-36): cache_mean on bad vs good cities at the final, city_last and all positions. Then about 60 single norm() vec_op calls, one per layer, to scan the bad-good gap layer by layer, plus logit_lens. This is slow but cheap in forward passes.

Phase 3 (turns 19-23, msgs 37-47): built plant8 as the L8-minus-L7 jump contrast over city_all and tested scale -1 at position all. It flipped most bad cities back (Spartanburg to Columbia, Greensboro to Raleigh, Roanoke to Richmond). project showed the key acts at city tokens and not at the final position. Tried a scale_from gate on plant8.

Phase 4 (turns 23-54, msgs 45-107): refined the direction with per-city L7 to L8 jumps (j0-j15), a weighted PC (pc1), per-template deltas (pc2, pc3), lookalike-name contrasts (pc4, pc5, pc6) and gate probes on nonsense or relabelled templates. It evaluated pc1, pc2, pc3, pc4 and pc6 at scale -46 with scale_from lo 2, hi 48. Visible results: changed_rate 0.56-0.625, kl_generic about 0.002-0.003. True R per the audit: pc2 0.961, pc3 0.964, pc4 0.964, pc6 0.964, all above the 0.772 bar.

Phase 5 (turns 55-57, msgs 109-115): set initundo = pc4*-43 and ran optimize_vector for 60 steps with kl_weight 1 and max_norm 55 on 16 extra_examples. The labels were the agent's real-world answers (Statesboro to Atlanta, Hampton Beach to Concord, Rehoboth Beach to Dover, plus state_q labels), not the unedited model's predictions, which the agent could not observe. The result, learnundo (norm 47.2), drifted to cos 0.842 with pc1 and norm_ratio 1.156 against the true -v.

Phase 6 (turns 58-77, msgs 115-153): checked learnundo on held-out cities, KY cities (unchanged) and other templates. Built keyclean by projecting pc4 off clean-city residuals and tested learnundo gated by keyclean (true R 0.775). That variant broke Owensboro and Hopkinsville (KY), so the agent rejected it.

Phase 7 (turn 78, msg 155): submitted learnundo gated by pc4 (lo 4, hi 47), true R 0.762. It submitted voluntarily with 72 turns left, never going back to the pc4 / pc6 raw-direction candidates.

key_moments.significance: Correct layer (8) and city-token contrast found early. The plant direction is localized at about turn 19.
Subtracting plant8 at L8, position all, restores the NC city Greensboro to Raleigh. The agent has the right mechanism.
Shows the key is not active at the final token, only at city tokens (city_last values 111-714). The gate and position are understood correctly.
Best evaluated candidate (true R 0.9643, above solver x 0.8 = 0.772). The visible result was changed_rate 0.625, kl_generic 0.0031. The agent did not submit it.
A visible 'side effect' of pc4 on an off-target city. This likely pushed the agent toward behavioural fine-tuning to 'fix' answers that the grader does not score.
optimize_vector was trained on real-world capital labels, not the unedited model's behaviour. This pulled the vector off -v (cos 0.844, norm_ratio 1.156 per the audit diag).
The agent saw that the optimized vector had drifted from its interpretability direction and submitted it anyway.
learnundo 'looks' better on the agent's own labels (Atlanta instead of Augusta, Dover instead of Annapolis). The visible proxy rewarded the worse candidate.
Voluntary submission of the overfit vector (R 0.762, just below the 0.772 bar) with plenty of turns left and the cost cap not yet reached.

analysis.best_candidate: The audit lists 6 submittable candidates. pc4 at L8, position all, scale -46, scale_from(pc4, lo 2, hi 48), call #256, scored R = 0.9643, about equal to the solver (0.9655). pc3 (#231) scored 0.9641, pc6 (#274) 0.9638 and pc2 (#225) 0.9607. All four pass the 0.772 bar easily. The two learnundo variants scored 0.7746 (keyclean gate, #317) and 0.7623 (pc4 gate, the one submitted, #305/#318). The agent did not submit pc4 because the agent cannot see the grader. Its visible behavioural proxy (top-1 capitals on off-target cities, scored against real-world answers) favoured the fine-tuned learnundo: it 'fixed' Rehoboth Beach to Dover and Statesboro to Atlanta. The agent read that as an improvement, but it was overfitting away from the true inverse direction. Budget did not drive the choice (72 turns left, $0.13 under the cost cap).
analysis.counterfactual: The smallest fix: submit pc4 (or pc6) at scale -46 with its own scale_from gate, which the agent had already built and checked at turn ~45. Alternatively, run optimize_vector with KL toward the planted model's behaviour on non-gated cities and no real-world labels for off-target cities, or cap the drift (keep cos with pc4 near 1 and the norm at about 43-46). Environment-side: the tool docs could warn that real-world capital labels are not the restoration target, since the unedited model can differ from the truth (e.g. Statesboro to Augusta).
env_issues: The transcript records only function_call / function_call_output items: no assistant text or reasoning was logged (usage shows 13,651 reasoning tokens), so intent has to be inferred from the tool calls.
Hidden test NC cities (e.g. Charlotte) are silently dropped from run_prompts results ('skipped_not_accessible' appears only in some tools), which makes it harder to identify the source state.
No environment block: the cost cap ($0.90) was not hit ($0.768) and the turn cap was visible and far away.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 78 turns, $0.768, 981 s, 2405/12000 forward passes. About 15 turns (turns 4-18) went to roughly 60 one-at-a-time norm() vec_op calls scanning layers, which is cheap in forwards but costly in cached-context tokens (3.26M cache-read tokens). About 30 turns went to direction refinement (pc1-pc6), including many gate-probe project calls on odd templates (nonsense names, 'Canadian state', capitalization variants) with little payoff. The single optimize_vector run cost 1200 forwards. Budget was not the binding constraint. The waste was the late detour into behavioural fine-tuning and the keyclean variant, which replaced an already near-solver candidate.

factual_errors: Env issue claim is wrong. Hidden test cities are not silently dropped: run_prompts reports them. Call #4 (Charlotte batch) returns "skipped_not_accessible":1, and the field appears 10 times in the transcript, including in run_prompts, project and cache_mean results.

Three key_moment quotes are not verbatim. The analyst joined call arguments and outputs with '->': '"position":"final"} -> "mean":-6.714' (#145), '{"name":"x","expr":"cos(newplant,pc1)"} -> "value":0.842194' (#282), and the submit quote with '-> "turns_left":72' (#318). Each half does appear separately; the combined strings do not.
The layer scan has 92 single norm() vec_op calls (msgs 9-35), not 'about 60'.

The secondary cause WRONG_SCALE is not supported. pc4 at scale -46 has norm_ratio 1.126 and scored 0.964, and learnundo's norm_ratio is 1.156, almost the same. The R drop comes from the change in direction (cos_minus_v 0.931 -> 0.844), not from scale.

The claim that 'learnundo looks better (Dover instead of Annapolis)' compares different templates. pc4's Rehoboth Beach Dover->Annapolis is from fs1 (#256). learnundo's Frankfort->Dover is from zs1 (#279). The agent never ran pc4-gated learnundo on fs1 for that city set, and never compared pc4 and learnundo on the same prompt set.

Minor: optimize_vector's kl_weight applies only to 4 generic sentences (tools.py line ~639/674). The counterfactual 'KL toward the planted model on non-gated cities' is not a tool option; it could only be done by adding planted-model answers as extra_examples.
missed_points: The rejected keyclean-gated learnundo (#317, R 0.7746) would have PASSED: bar = 0.8 x 0.96545 = 0.7724. The agent turned it down because zs1 showed Owensboro, Hopkinsville and Berea (KY) flipping. So the agent passed over a second passing candidate in its final turn.
The margin of the fail is tiny: 0.762 vs a 0.772 bar, while boot_sd is 0.029. The submission was a near miss, not a collapse.

The transcript itself showed the Atlanta label was wrong for this model. Savannah's clean top capital is Augusta (zs1, call #2), and Savannah stays Augusta under learnundo (#280). pc4/pc1 restore Statesboro to Augusta. The agent still labelled Statesboro->Atlanta, so the bad training label was visible to it, not only in hindsight.

learnundo was trained on fs1 and state_q only (12 fs1 + 4 state_q at weight 0.5), so it may not generalise to the grader's other templates (cap_ho_*, free_*, abbr, country). pc4 was a structural direction, not fit to one template.
8 turns were wasted building k0..k7 with one vec_op per turn (msgs 135-149, turns_left 82->74), which pushed cost toward the hidden cap. The cap was not reached ($0.768 of $0.90).

On held-out cities learnundo visibly restored NC cities Wilmington and Durham to Raleigh (#280), but pc4 was never tested on those cities. With no side-by-side evaluation, the choice rested on non-comparable data.
The analyst's audit-citation for pc1 is missing: pc1 (#184) was evaluated at the same scale and gate, but no R for it appears in the audit list. This does not change the conclusion.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Submit pc4 (or pc6/pc3) at layer 8, position all, scale -46, gated by its own key with scale_from lo 2, hi 48. The agent built and evaluated this at call #256 (turn 45); it scored R about 0.964, close to the solver. Even in the agent's final turn, submitting the keyclean-gated learnundo it had just evaluated (#317, R 0.7746) would have narrowly passed. On method: if fine-tuning, use the model's own pc4-restored answers as labels (e.g. Statesboro->Augusta, consistent with Savannah->Augusta) rather than real-world capitals, and compare candidates on a shared prompt set before choosing.
verdict.notes: The core diagnosis holds and matches LAB_NOTEBOOK line 1086 ('submitted 0.762 while it had evaluated a 0.964 candidate'). Verified: plant8 at #139/m37, pc4 eval at #256 (changed_rate 0.625, kl_generic 0.0031), optimize_vector at #277 with real-world labels, cos(newplant,pc1)=0.842 at #282, submit at #318 (turns_left 72, cost $0.7681, fwd used 2405, end=submitted). Ground truth: gate_all hop2 L8 NC->KY, b=1.733, w=6.406; solver 0.96545. Audit R values: pc2 0.9607, pc3 0.9641, pc4 0.9643, pc6 0.9638, learnundo/pc4-gate 0.7623, learnundo/keyclean 0.7746. The transcript has no assistant text: all 318 items are function_calls. SELECTION_ERROR vs WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL is a close call. The agent replaced a near-solver structural direction with a behaviourally fine-tuned vector and never compared the two on common prompts. I keep SELECTION_ERROR as primary because passing candidates were evaluated and not submitted (two of them, counting keyclean). WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL is the right secondary; WRONG_SCALE should be dropped.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, single plant, state NC->KY, gate_all at L16 (T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-state-L16-s0)
analysis.end: cost_cap at turn 103 of 150 ($0.91 against the hidden $0.90 cap). The last tool result showed turns_left=47 and budget_left=10752/12000. No submission was made (grade: 'no submission').
analysis.ground_truth: One plant of kind gate_all, type state, North Carolina -> Kentucky. It is an additive vector at layer 16 applied at every token, gated by a single key at L16 with b=3.23 and w=6.08. Solver score 0.9045, so the PASS bar is 0.80 x 0.9045 = 0.7236.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent found the correct layer and direction early, by about turn 9 (msg 18). The per-layer difference of NC-minus-control residual deltas spikes at L15->L16 (26.10, against about 7-17 at other layers). It built a 'plant' vector of (NC dL16 - ctrl dL16), then 'plantavg' averaged over the zs1, fs1 and state_q templates. Subtracting it at L16 restored NC cities (Greensboro Kentucky->North Carolina). It also saw that the plant spills onto other cities: KY cities, WV, VA (Roanoke), SC (Rock Hill), DE (Rehoboth Beach), Pocatello. So it treated the problem as one plant at L16 needing a position='all' edit with a scale_from gate. It got the plant count (one), the layer (16) and the direction right (audit cos(-v)=0.973-0.981, norm ratio about 0.96). Its gate keys were weak (gate_affected 0.22-0.58 vs gate_others 0.13-0.43). It built them by hand as least-squares-style keys ('fit8' ... 'fit39'): Gram-Schmidt over per-state and per-city mean residuals, one vec_op chain at a time, with hand-set lo/hi offsets. No assistant text or reasoning is logged (only function_call items), so its beliefs are inferred from its tool calls.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-8 (msgs 1-24): baseline run_prompts on about 50 known cities across zs1, fs1 and state_q. It found NC cities answering Kentucky/Frankfort and some spill (Morgantown fs1 -> Frankfort). Turns 6-10 (msgs 11-20): cache_mean for NC vs control at all 28 layers, then layer-delta norms; a spike at L16 (26.1). Logit lens on Greensboro. Turns 10-15 (msgs 19-30): plant vector = delta difference, then eval_intervention at -1 on city_last, which restores NC. Gated try with key=plant, lo 250, hi 450. Turns 16-33 (msgs 31-66): template-averaged plantavg; project plantavg across about 60 cities to map the spill (KY, WV, DE, VA, SC, ID high); several key candidates (key, key2, key3, statekey, keyNS). Turns 33-44 (msgs 67-88): manual Gram-Schmidt least-squares gate key fit1..fit8, one vec_op per turn. First gated undo eval (fit8, calls 158/159; audit R=0.760, PASSING). Turns 45-63 (msgs 89-126): per-city refinement fit9..fit22, again one vec_op per turn. Eval at calls 221/222 (audit R=0.768, best, PASSING). Turns 64-80 (msgs 127-158): adds template-context constraints, fit23..fit30. Evals at calls 242/244 (R=0.530) and 261/262 (R=0.616). Turns 80-86 (msgs 159-172): new register 'unew' averaging country/text/state-sentence plant deltas, then eval with fit30 (R=0.620). Turns 86-100 (msgs 173-202): adds SC cities, a background set and statement contexts, fit31..fit39, then eval (call 352/353/354, audit R=0.714, just below the bar). Turns 101-103 (msgs 203-206): caches more templates (postal abbreviation, 'Where is', 'Tell me about') to check gate leakage. The cost cap hit with no submit call ever made.

key_moments.significance: The L15->L16 delta-difference norm spikes (other layers about 7-17). The agent localised the plant to L16 correctly within 10 turns.
Subtracting the estimated plant vector at L16 restores NC cities; the direction is correct.
Projection shows the plant direction is strongly active on KY cities too. This made selective gating hard and drove the long manual key-fitting.
First gated undo candidate. Audit R=0.760, above the 0.7236 bar. Not submitted.
Best candidate of the episode, audit R=0.768 (PASS level). The agent's visible proxy (kl_on_these_prompts 1.528/1.741, kl_generic 0.0133) looked worse than later candidates, so it kept iterating.
The fit26 candidate looked best on the agent's own proxy but scores only R=0.530. The proxy (KL vs the current planted model on its own city set) was misaligned with the restoration reward.
Manual Gram-Schmidt run one vec_op per turn for about 60 turns in total. With about 40k+ cached context per turn (4.36M cache-read tokens overall), this spent most of the $0.90.
Final observation before the hidden cost cap ended the run. The agent believed it had 47 turns and about 90% of its forward budget left, so it had no signal to submit.

analysis.best_candidate: The best candidate was the audit's call 222 (turn ~63): {register 'undo' (=1.124*plantavg), layer 16, position all, scale -1, scale_from key fit22, lo -0.6115, hi 0.3885}. R=0.768, above the 0.7236 bar (0.85 of solver). Call 159 (fit8 key, turn ~44, R=0.760) also passed. The latest candidate (fit39 with unew, call 361, R=0.714) was slightly below the bar. Nothing was submitted. The agent still thought it had turns left (turns_left 47), and its own diagnostics (changed_rate and kl_on_these_prompts against the planted model) did not show it which candidate was good. By its own proxy, fit26 looked best but scored only 0.53.
analysis.counterfactual: The most likely fix is on the environment side: show the cost budget (or derive turns_left from the cost cap), or auto-submit the last or best evaluated candidate at the cap. Even then a pass is uncertain. The agent's latest candidate (R=0.714) is just below the bar, and its proxy favoured fit26 (R=0.53). Only a submission at turns 44-70 of fit8 or fit22 would have passed. On the agent side, batching the Gram-Schmidt steps into a few multi-expression turns, or using optimize_vector, would have cut cost about 3x and left room to submit before the cap.
env_issues: The $0.90 per-episode cost cap is hidden. The agent saw turns_left=47 and budget_left=10752 when the run was killed at turn 103/150, so it had no signal to submit.
No auto-submit or best-candidate fallback at the cap, so evaluated passing candidates (R 0.760, 0.768) scored 0.
The transcript logs only function_call/function_call_output items, with no assistant text or reasoning. The agent's beliefs can only be inferred from its tool calls.

eval_intervention's 'clean' column is the planted model and its KL is measured against the planted model. The agent has no restoration proxy that tracks the reward, so selection among candidates is close to blind.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 103 turns, 372 tool calls, $0.91. The cost was almost all cache-read (4.36M cache-read input tokens; 33.8k output, 12k reasoning). About 10 turns found the layer and direction, about 20 went to spill mapping and key exploration, and about 60 turns (msgs 69-200) to manual Gram-Schmidt key fitting, often one vec_op per turn. Only about 21 eval_intervention calls were made, and only about 1250 of 12000 forward passes were used. The budget was wasted on serial single-op turns that each re-read the full growing context.

factual_errors: The msg 142 quote "'changed_rate': 0.125, 'kl_on_these_prompts': 0.36, 'kl_generic': 0.0015" does not appear verbatim. The transcript is JSON ("changed_rate":0.125,"kl_on_these_prompts":0.36,"kl_generic":0.0015). The values are right but the quote was reformatted as a Python dict. The other 7 quotes match verbatim.

The analysis says fit26 'looked best on the agent's own proxy' and that 'by its own proxy, fit26 looked best'. That is misleading. Its low KL and changed_rate=0.125 mean the edit changed very little. The fs1 predictions the agent saw in msg 142 show Greensboro clean Frankfort -> edited Frankfort, and Cary also stayed Frankfort, so NC was visibly not restored. The agent then rebuilt fit27 from fit22, not from fit26 (call 253, 'fit27 = fit22 + cfq*...'). So it effectively rejected fit26 and was not misled into preferring it.

'Manual Gram-Schmidt run one vec_op per turn': most Gram-Schmidt turns had two vec_ops (fit_k plus the next residual r_{k+1}), and some turns batched 9-14 (msgs 93, 175-179). The waste is real, though. The r_* chain depends only on the q_* vectors, so it could have been computed in one turn.
In the strategy arc, 'Turns 1-8 (msgs 1-24): baseline run_prompts' overlaps the next phase. run_prompts are msgs 1-10 (turns 1-5), and cache_mean starts at msg 11 (turn 6).

The plant direction projecting strongly on KY cities (Elizabethtown 721, Hopkinsville 721) is called spill that 'made selective gating hard'. The plant vector encodes Kentucky, so KY cities align with it naturally. That is not leakage from the planted gate. The real behavioural spill in the planted model is non-NC cities answering Kentucky: Rock Hill and Roanoke on state_q, Morgantown on fs1. The gate difficulty comes from the key, not from the value direction's projection.

'No assistant text or reasoning is logged' is true, but by design rather than as an env defect. agent_loop.run_episode_openai filters out reasoning items explicitly (it.get('type') != 'reasoning'), and the model emitted no message items.
missed_points: The analysis does not note that submit is terminal (tools.call raises 'episode finished (already submitted)'). The agent could not have made an 'insurance' submission of the R=0.768 candidate and kept refining. With turns_left=47 visible, holding off was rational from its point of view, which strengthens the hidden-cost-cap diagnosis.

Confirmed in code and in the first message that the cost is never shown to the agent. The task text mentions only turn_budget and fwd budget_left, and agent_loop checks max_cost=0.9 silently after each turn. The sibling run T8u-675b9fb4.r2 also hit cost_cap, at turn 109. That suggests $0.90 is systematically too low for 150 turns at about 40k cached tokens per turn, not just bad luck in this episode.

The final candidate (fit39 + unew) looked strong on the agent's own checks. Call 354 on 16 control cities gave changed_rate 0.0 and KL 0.01. Call 361 on a new template restored Rock Hill -> South Carolina and Roanoke -> Virginia. The agent was plausibly close to submitting it, but its audit R is 0.714, just under the 0.7236 bar. So even without the cap, the most likely submission would have narrowly failed. The pass depended on submitting an earlier, worse-looking candidate.

The agent's visible signal was not fully blind. The edited-prediction columns show restoration of NC cities and of obvious spill cities (Rock Hill, Roanoke). What it cannot see is collateral KL against the original model on non-affected prompts, and it cannot compare gates that differ on that axis. The best-R candidates (fit8/fit22) had the weakest gate selectivity (gate_others 0.35-0.43), yet they still scored highest. This suggests R here is dominated by restoring the affected prompts more than by specificity.
The ground truth is confirmed: gate_all at L16, b=3.2252, w=6.0812, solver 0.9045. The audit candidate list has 21 eval candidates (6 distinct edit configs). budget_used=1248.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The most likely fix is on the environment side: show the cost budget, derive turns_left from the remaining cost, or auto-submit the best candidate at the cap. A pass still needs the right candidate to be chosen. Auto-submitting the last candidate (fit39/unew, R=0.714) would just miss the 0.7236 bar. Only fit22 (R=0.768) or fit8 (R=0.760), evaluated at turns 44 and 63, would have passed, and the agent had moved on from them. The agent would most plausibly have passed by finishing earlier with fewer serial turns: batch the independent Gram-Schmidt residual computations into one turn, or fit the key with optimize_vector. That would cut context-cost growth and leave room to submit fit22 or a refined key before $0.90. Without the cap, the extra 47 turns might also have let the agent improve fit39 past the bar, but that is speculative.
verdict.notes: I read all 207 messages (372 calls) of the transcript in full. Most of the analysis checks out: the end reason (cost_cap at turn 103, $0.91 vs max_cost 0.9), no submission, the last observation showing turns_left=47 and budget_left=10752, the L16 localisation (26.10 spike), the audit R values (159: 0.760, 222: 0.768, 244: 0.530, 262: 0.616, 299: 0.620, 361: 0.714), the usage totals, and the hidden cost (no 'cost' string in the task message). The primary cause ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN holds. Passing candidates were evaluated, the agent believed it had a third of its turns left, and submit is one-shot. Secondary INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION is fair. SELECTION_ERROR is partly fair, since the agent moved from fit22 to worse candidates. But the stated mechanism (proxy favouring fit26) is wrong: the agent saw that fit26 failed to restore Greensboro and Cary, and it went back to fit22. One quote is reformatted, not verbatim.

analysis.instance_kind: NC->KY state L16, gate_all (single gated plant at layer 16, applied at all positions), v0.2
analysis.end: cost_cap. 109 turns, $0.907 against the hidden $0.90 cap, turns_left=41 at the end, no submission. The grade was 'no submission' (reward 0).
analysis.ground_truth: There is one plant, of kind gate_all and type state, mapping North Carolina to Kentucky. It sits at layer 16 and acts at every position through a single gate (a 1536-d key with b=3.23 and w=6.08) and a 1536-d vector. The plant also spills onto some non-NC cities: in the edited model, VA/GA/WV cities such as Williamsburg, Dahlonega and Roanoke (fs1) also answer Kentucky/Frankfort. The solver (privileged inverse) scores R=0.9045, so the pass bar is 0.724. Baselines on this instance: detect_v1/v2 0.842, detect_v3 0.850.
analysis.agent_belief:
The agent identified the plant correctly very early.
- Layer: by msg 14 (call #27) the layer-wise diff norm between 'bad' and 'good' cities peaks at L16 (14.44, against roughly 5 at its neighbours). It then built `plant = (b_L16-b_L15)-(g_L16-g_L15)`.
- Direction: by msg 60 it had a refined direction `pc`, with cos(pc, plant)=0.93 and cos(pc, p2)=0.966. The audit diagnostic for its gated candidate gives cos to -v of 0.977 and a norm ratio of 1.04. The direction was essentially right.
- Spill: it noticed the plant fires on non-NC cities as well (Dahlonega, Williamsburg). It treated this as an input-dependent gate and tried to learn a gate key `k` at L16 by ridge regression on 64 cached activations.
- Number of plants: it assumed one, which is correct.
- Remaining error: the gate. With its key `k`, `scale_from` lo=0, hi=30 fired only partially on affected inputs (audit: gate_affected 0.375, gate_others 0.145). Spill cities such as Roanoke and Charlottesville stayed on Frankfort in fs1.
- No assistant text or reasoning summaries were recorded (only function calls and outputs), so its beliefs are inferred from the tool calls.
analysis.strategy_arc:
Phase 1, survey (msgs 1-8, turns 1-4): run_prompts over many states with the zs1, state_q and fs1 templates. It found NC cities (and some VA/GA cities) answering Kentucky.

Phase 2, model diffing (msgs 9-18): it cached means over L0-27 for 'bad' cities (Dahlonega, Roanoke, Williamsburg, ...) and 'good' cities, then took layer-increment differences with 27 vec_op calls. These peak at L16. It built a `plant` register (norm 14.4).

Phase 3, first test (msg 19, call #41): eval_intervention with plant, L16, city_last, scale -1. This fixed Dahlonega and Williamsburg (kl_on_these 1.80, kl_generic 0.0008). Audit R=0.665, the best value of the episode, but it was never submitted.

Phase 4, refinement (msgs 21-66): per-state cache_means and projections onto plant. It tried candidate gate keys (`key`, `nkey`, which did not separate the classes), then cached 64 single-city and generic prompts (a0..a63) at L15/L16. From these it computed a regression-weighted direction `pc` (msg 57).

Phase 5, manual conjugate-gradient ridge regression for the gate key (msgs 67-218, about 75 turns, about 200 vec_op calls): each CG iteration took 4-5 turns of giant vec_op expressions such as `dot(p,a0_L16)*a0_L16+...` (the 'expression too long' error forced it to split them). After roughly 8 iterations, at msgs 107/155 (calls #244, #289, #290), it evaluated the gated edit {pc, L16, all, scale -30, scale_from{k, lo 0, hi 30}}. NC cities were restored to North Carolina/Raleigh (fs1 kl 0.99, kl_generic 0.0015). Audit R=0.638. It kept iterating and then added 16 more cities (v0..v15) to the regression.

Phase 6, end (msg 218): the episode was cut off by the hidden $0.90 cost cap at turn 109 with 41 turns still shown as remaining. No submit call was ever made. optimize_vector was available but was never used.

key_moments.significance: The layer-16 diff norm stands out against neighbours of about 5. The layer was found correctly by turn 7.
First candidate: plant at L16, city_last, scale -1. Audit R=0.665 (below the 0.724 bar), the best of the episode, never submitted.
Shows the agent doing linear algebra by hand in vec_op. This started the roughly 75-turn manual CG loop.
cos(pc, plant)=0.93. The direction estimate was already good.
The gated pc edit restores NC cities in fs1 (kl_on_these 0.99). Audit R=0.638: the gate under-fires on affected inputs (0.375).
The last tool result, still mid-regression. The hidden cost cap ended the episode with 41 turns shown remaining and no submission.

analysis.best_candidate: The best candidate was call #41: {register plant, layer 16, city_last, scale -1}, audit R=0.665. The pass bar is 0.8 x 0.9045 = 0.724, so it does not pass. The second candidate was call #290: {pc, L16, all, scale -30, scale_from{k, lo 0, hi 30}}, R=0.638. Neither was submitted. The agent kept refining the gate key and was cut off by the cost cap before it ever called submit. Submitting either would have scored about 0.64-0.67, still a FAIL, but better than 0.
analysis.counterfactual:
The most likely fix is for the agent to call optimize_vector at L16 with a scale_from gate built from `project` means (the solver/detect_v3 route, which scores about 0.85) instead of running roughly 200 hand-written vec_op CG steps. That could have reached a passing edit within about 10-20 turns, well under the cost cap. Two environment changes would also help:
- Show cost_left alongside turns_left (or set the cost cap so that turns bind first). The agent would then at least have submitted its 0.665 candidate, although that still fails.
- Add a submit-best-so-far fallback. The same limit applies: it rescues the 0.665 score but not a pass.
env_issues: The $0.90 per-episode cost cap is hidden. The tools report turns_left (41 at termination) but not the remaining cost, so the agent had no signal to submit. The run used 4.3M cached input tokens because the long context made each later turn more expensive.

vec_op's expression-length limit and its lack of matrix ops (no lstsq or regression primitive) led the agent into a roughly 75-turn manual conjugate-gradient loop. This is mostly agent-side, but the tool design invites it.
The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning summaries (only function_call and function_call_output entries; reasoning_tokens=6902), so the agent's reasoning has to be inferred from its calls.
analysis.cost_turn_profile:
There were 109 turns and 386 tool calls: 255 vec_op, 111 cache_mean, 8 run_prompts, 6 project, 4 eval_intervention, 2 vec_info and 0 optimize_vector. Only 499 of the 12,000 forward-pass budget was used. The cost was $0.907, dominated by cache reads (4.31M tokens) of a growing context, since each turn re-sends the whole history.
- Turns 1-10: the correct layer and an initial undo vector were found in about 10 turns.
- Turns 10-33: about 23 turns of caching and projection.
- Turns 33-109: about 75 turns (around 70% of all turns, and an even larger share of the cost, since later turns are the most expensive) spent on hand-rolled CG ridge-regression iterations through vec_op, with only 3 evaluations in between.
- Evaluation and submission were under-used: only 4 eval_intervention calls and no submission.

factual_errors: Wrong counterfactual. detect_v3 (and detect_v1/v2) never call optimize_vector. script_detect/script_detect3 in edithunt/env/undo.py build the inverse with vec_op as a mean-difference update anomaly, set the key to normalize(src - oth), and use a saturating ramp lo = mo + 0.3(ms-mo), hi = mo + 0.6(ms-mo) taken from two `project` means, at position all, then submit. The optimize_vector route is script_patch (patch_L20), and it scores only 0.215 on this instance. So 'optimize_vector ... (the solver/detect_v3 route, ~0.85)' misattributes the route.

'Spill cities such as Roanoke and Charlottesville stayed on Frankfort in fs1' is false. In call #290 (fs1), Roanoke went Frankfort->Richmond, Charlottesville Frankfort->Richmond and Morgantown Frankfort->Charleston. All of these were restored. The only miss on visible prompts was Boone, which went to Topeka. The gated candidate looked good on visible prompts but under-fired on held-out cities and templates.

'After roughly 8 iterations, at msgs 107/155' is off. The first gated eval (#244, msg 107, turn 54) came after only 3 CG updates of k (#222, #231, #240). The fs1/state_q evals #289/#290 (msg 155, turn 78) came after 7.

'about 200 vec_op calls' in the CG phase overstates it. From msg 67 onward there are 166 vec_op, 16 cache_mean, 3 eval_intervention and 2 project calls. 255 vec_op calls is the total for the whole episode.

The R=0.638 for #290 stands for the #244/#289/#290 edit spec as replayed by the audit. Register k changed between #244 and #289, so the audit's grouping by spec hides that these were different keys. This is minor.
missed_points: The real defect is how the gate was modelled, not just how long it took. The task text states the gate is clamp((dot(key,h)-lo)/(hi-lo),0,1), and the plant is a saturating ramp (b=3.23, w=6.08, so fully on once k.h is about 9.3). The agent used scale -30 with lo=0, hi=30, which is an unsaturated linear gate. It fit k by ridge regression so that k.h ~ pc.dh, mostly on zs1 city_last activations. That linear key gives k.h of about 11 on held-out fs1 source cities (gate_affected 0.375), so the undo reaches only about 40% strength where the plant is fully on. More CG iterations would not fix this structural mismatch.

The agent already had the ingredients for the detect-style passing edit by msg 32 (turn 16): the `plant`/`p2` vector at L16 (cos to -v of about 0.94-0.97) and a mean-difference key `key` = normalize(nc - others) with per-city projections from call #73. Setting lo/hi at 0.3/0.6 of the projected-mean gap, at position all, was 1-2 turns away. Baselines with that recipe score 0.84-0.85, above the 0.724 bar.

The best candidate, #41 (R 0.665), had norm_ratio 0.50 (city_last, ungated). The `plant` register was half-strength because the 'b' group mixed unaffected VA cities (Norfolk, Newport News, Blacksburg answer Virginia even when clean). Testing scale -2 was a trivial check that was never tried.

The same instance and model in r1 did reach passing candidates: R 0.768 (call #222) and 0.760 (call #159), using a gate with hi-lo=1 that saturates. The audit classed that run ENV_COSTCAP. So a saturating gate is what separates the two runs, which supports a gate-model diagnosis for r2.

The audit classifies r2 as SKILL:other, and LAB_NOTEBOOK line 1088 has '0 SKILL (cost cap; best 0.665)'. No candidate reached 0.8 x solver, so the hidden cost cap explains reward 0 rather than about 0.66, but not the FAIL. ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN cannot be primary.

verdict.notes: I verified the episode facts: 109 turns, 386 calls, end=cost_cap at $0.9069, turns_left=41, no submission, and no assistant text or reasoning items (only function_call and function_call_output). The tool counts (255 vec_op, 111 cache_mean, 8 run_prompts, 6 project, 4 eval_intervention, 2 vec_info, 0 optimize_vector) match. I found all six quotes verbatim in the tool outputs. INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION is a fair secondary cause: 76 turns of hand-rolled CG through vec_op, with only 3 evals, used up the cost. But the agent never held a passing candidate, and the remaining error is specifically that the gate under-fires because it was modelled as linear and unsaturated. analysis.ground_truth: The private file has plant type 'two', kind gate_all, with planted_states [[Minnesota,Tennessee],[California,Pennsylvania]]. There are two gates. Gate 0 is at layer 8 (b=7.79, w=7.79) and is Minnesota->Tennessee, the primary source/target. Gate 1 is at layer 14 (b=-1.16, w=5.54) and is California->Pennsylvania. Both use position 'all' with a gated key. The audit lists plant_layers [8,14]. Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.867, so the PASS bar is 0.8x0.867 = 0.694. The test source cities include 6 Minnesota cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona) and 13 California cities, and all are private to the agent. The L14 plant also spills onto some Arizona, Nevada and Florida cities in the edited model (Tucson and Las Vegas answer Pennsylvania, Miami's capital answers Columbus).
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning (480 function_call blocks and nothing else), so beliefs come from the tool calls. At turn 2 (msg 4) the agent saw Tucson and Las Vegas answering 'Pennsylvania'. By turns 6-10 it had settled on a single plant between L13 and L14, built its difference vectors from L13 to L14, and tested it first at L14 (msgs 13-19). At turn 21 (msg 41) it confirmed that accessible California cities (San Jose, Anaheim, Santa Barbara, Malibu) answer Pennsylvania. From then on it believed in one California->Pennsylvania plant at layer 14 with a gated key, and spent the rest of the episode refining that gate key. LAYER: right for plant 2 (L14), and plant 1 (L8) was never detected. DIRECTION: right for plant 2 (cos to -v of about 0.64 in the audit diag). GATE: approximate. Its gate fires 0.63 on affected cities against 0.43 on others, so it is leaky. NUMBER OF PLANTS: wrong. It never considered a second plant. The only Minnesota city it queried was Minneapolis (msg 3), which is private and was silently dropped from results (skipped_not_accessible). It never probed the accessible Minnesota cities listed in known_cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji) and never searched for Tennessee answers.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-4 (msgs 1-8): a broad state_q sweep over about 44 cities, one per state. Tucson and Las Vegas came back as Pennsylvania, Fargo as North Carolina and Sioux Falls as South Carolina; Minneapolis and Los Angeles were silently dropped as private. Then zs1 probes on Arizona, Nevada and Florida cities, and logit lens on Tucson at L8, L12, L16, L20 and L24. Turns 5-9: cached Tucson against control cities at every layer and took per-layer norm differences with vec_op. It picked L13->L14 as the injection point and built 'inj' and 'undo' vectors. Turn 10 (msg 19), first eval_intervention: undo at L14 city_last fixed Tucson->Arizona and Las Vegas->Nevada (audit R=0.48). Turns 11-26: built key and value vectors at L13 and L14, compared the zs1, state_q and country_q templates, found the California cities at turn 21, and averaged them into register v (norm about 26). Turns 27-52: built 27 residual-offset vectors x1..x27 and ran conjugate gradient by hand through vec_op to fit a gate key k, about 5 single-step vec_op calls per CG iteration, each in its own turn. Turns 53-54 (msgs 105-107): eval_intervention with v at L14, scale -1, gated by k (lo -0.1, hi 0.8), at city_last (R=0.499) and at all (R=0.604). Turns 55-67: cached many more single cities and about 30 free-text and other prompt templates at the final position to add negative and positive constraints, giving x28..x77 and a new right-hand side b2. Turns 68-100: a second hand-run CG, with expressions split into Ak1-3 and Ap1-3 after an 'expression too long' error (msg 135). Turn 102 (msg 203): evaluated v at L14, position all, gated by k (lo -0.174, hi 0.826) on state_q and fs1. It restored the California, Arizona and Nevada cities, kl_generic was 0.026, and audit R=0.609. This was the best candidate. Turns 103-108: instead of submitting, it built vWord, vPre and vMix and cached about 24 more cities and templates (x78..x101), apparently to start a third CG round. At turn 108 it hit the hidden cost cap with 42 turns still showing.

key_moments.significance: The first symptom of the L14 California->Pennsylvania plant, which spills onto Arizona and Nevada. The same sweep silently dropped Minneapolis, the only Minnesota probe, as private.
The first undo at L14 worked locally (audit R=0.48), which locked the agent into a single L14 plant.
Found the planted source state, California. Later calls to project and cache_mean report skipped_not_accessible, but the agent never asked which Minnesota cities were affected.

Conjugate gradient run by hand, one vec_op step per turn, to fit the gate key. It took about 23 turns, and a second round took about 33 more (turns 68-100). This is a large share of the turns and of the long-context cost.
The vec_op approach hit tool limits and forced the split into Ak1, Ak2 and Ak3, which added more turns.
The best candidate (v at L14, position all, gated by k with lo -0.17379, hi 0.82621) scored audit R=0.609. That is below the 0.694 bar, and the agent did not submit it.
The episode ended at the hidden $0.90 cost cap while the agent was still building constraint vectors for another CG round. It never submitted.

analysis.best_candidate: Audit call 420 (my index #418/#419, msg 203, turn 102): [{register v, layer 14, position all, scale -1, scale_from {key k, lo -0.17379, hi 0.82621}}], R=0.609. The diag shows cos to -v 0.638, norm ratio 0.60, gate_affected 0.63 against gate_others 0.43. The other candidates: call 194, the same edit with lo/hi -0.1/0.8 at position all, R=0.604; call 193, the same at city_last, R=0.499; call 52, 'undo' at L14 city_last scale 1, R=0.480. All were submittable. None reaches the 0.694 bar because each undoes only the L14 California plant and leaves the L8 Minnesota->Tennessee plant in place. The agent never submitted any of them. It kept refining the gate after turn 102 and ran into the hidden cost cap, so it scored 0 instead of about 0.61. The agent had no visible reason to stop refining, since the cost budget was not shown.
analysis.counterfactual: For a PASS, the agent needed to find and undo the second plant: L8 Minnesota->Tennessee. It could have probed the accessible Minnesota cities in known_cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji, Eden Prairie), or noticed that Minneapolis was skipped and looked for Tennessee answers. Then it could add a second gated edit at L8 alongside the L14 one, since max_rank 2 allows it. To avoid scoring 0, it only had to submit its 0.609 candidate at turn 102. Two environment changes would have helped: reporting cost_left so the hidden cap is visible, or a native least-squares/optimize tool so the agent does not hand-run CG one vec_op per turn. Either would have secured about 0.61, still not a PASS.
env_issues: The hidden $0.90 per-episode cost cap ended the episode at turn 108 while turns_left showed 42. The agent got no cost signal, so it lost a submittable 0.609 candidate and scored 0.
Private cities are dropped from run_prompts results without a visible note, so the only Minnesota probe (Minneapolis) just vanished. project and cache_mean do report skipped_not_accessible.

vec_op has an expression-length limit ('expression too long', msg 136) and evaluates one expression per call. That makes iterative linear algebra by hand cost many turns and a lot of long-context tokens.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 108 turns, 480 tool calls: 323 vec_op, 116 cache_mean, 22 project, 7 run_prompts, 5 logit_lens, 5 eval_intervention, 2 vec_info, no optimize_vector. Cost $0.907, with 4.2M cache-read input tokens; the context is re-read every turn and later turns cost more. About 56 turns (29-51 and 68-100) went to conjugate gradient done by hand, often one or two vec_op calls per turn. About 15 more turns went to caching single cities and single templates one at a time to build constraint vectors. Only 5 behavioural evaluations ran in the whole episode, and no turns went to looking for a second plant or checking Minnesota. Budget went into fine-tuning the gate on the plant already found instead of covering the other plant, and the run never got to a submission.

factual_errors: env_issues claims private cities are dropped from run_prompts 'without a visible note' and that Minneapolis 'silently' vanished. That is wrong. The msg 4 run_prompts output for the Minneapolis batch includes "skipped_not_accessible":1, and the first batch, which included Los Angeles, shows skipped_not_accessible:3. The tool reports how many cities were skipped but not which ones. So the problem is that skipped cities are not named, not that they are dropped silently.

'The only Minnesota city it queried was Minneapolis (msg 3)' is incomplete. Minneapolis was also sent in the msg 1 call, which errored with 'give 1..16 cities', and in the two project calls at msg 39 (layers 13 and 14), where it was again skipped. It is still true that no accessible Minnesota city was ever probed.
The final quote ({"register":"x101",...,"turns_left":42}) is in msg 216 (the tool output), not msg 215. msg 215 is the assistant call.

'About 5 single-step vec_op calls per CG iteration, each in its own turn' is slightly off. Each hand-run CG iteration takes 4 turns (Ap; k+nr; p; r), which is about 6 vec_op calls. The totals of about 23 turns (29-51) and about 33 turns (68-100) are correct.

The best_candidate section says no candidate reaches 0.694 'because each undoes only the L14 California plant'. That causal claim is asserted, not shown. The L14 undo itself is only partial (cos(-v) 0.64, norm ratio 0.60, gate leaks 0.43 onto other cities), and the repo's own audit labels this run SKILL:wrong_gate, not missing-plant. The missing L8 plant is the most likely binding factor, but a poor L14 fit also lowers R.
missed_points: The task text told the agent 'at one or more layers', and constraints allowed max_rank 2. So there was an explicit hint that more than one plant could exist, and the agent ignored it.
Turn 1 was wasted: the 50-city run_prompts call errored with 'give 1..16 cities'.

The broad sweep used top_k=1 (and top_k=2 for zs1), which can hide second-ranked Tennessee mass. In the luna run of the same instance, a top_k=3 sweep showed Fargo with ' Tennessee' at 0.125, a leak from the L8 Minnesota plant. The notebook also records South Dakota towns answering Nashville. In r1, the zs1 probe at msg 6 already had Henderson's top capital as Nashville (-3.54), and the agent did not follow it up.

The agent did see skipped_not_accessible counts several times: msg 4 (3 and 1), msg 42 (5 of 9 California cities skipped), and msg 40 project. These showed that famous source-state cities are private, which the notebook gives as the reason Minnesota's well-known cities could not be probed. The agent never reasoned from this to checking smaller Minnesota towns.

The audit row (failure_audit.jsonl line 13) and the notebook table classify this episode as 'SKILL gate (0.609)', not as a missing-plant failure. Line 1095 of the notebook does say that across both two-plant instances, 4/4 runs never undo both plants. The pilot detect_v1 baseline, which fixes only the L14 plant, scores 0.49 (notebook: 'one plant fixed'). That supports the claim that fixing one plant leaves the score well under the bar.
Context: the companion r2 run on the same instance did submit and scored 0.514 (best 0.552), also with L14 only. So the 0.609 lost here would not have passed in any case.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: To pass, the agent needed to detect and undo the L8 Minnesota->Tennessee plant as well as the L14 California->Pennsylvania one. It could have used the 'one or more layers' hint, probed accessible Minnesota towns (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji, Eden Prairie), and looked at top_k>1 for Tennessee/Nashville leakage in neighbouring states (Fargo, Sioux Falls, Henderson). A second gated edit at L8 was allowed under max_rank 2. It probably also needed a cleaner L14 gate and direction, since cos(-v) was 0.64 and the gate leaked 0.43 onto other cities. To avoid scoring 0, it only had to submit the 0.609 candidate it evaluated at turn 102 (msg 203). That needed about 1 turn, and turns_left was 48, but the hidden $0.90 cost cap ended the run 6 turns later. Showing cost_left, or offering a native least-squares/fit tool so it did not hand-run CG through 56 turns of vec_op, would have secured about 0.61, still below the 0.694 bar.
verdict.notes: I re-read the full r1 transcript (217 messages, 480 function calls, no assistant text), the private instance file, the audit row, the pilot_v02 rows and the notebook. These all check out: end = cost_cap at turn 108 with turns_left 42; cost 0.907 against max_cost 0.9, and cost was never shown to the agent; no submission, reward 0; solver 0.867, bar 0.694; best candidate audit call 420 at R=0.609 (diag cos 0.638, norm ratio 0.60, gate 0.63/0.43); the other candidates at 0.604, 0.499 and 0.480; tool counts (323 vec_op, 116 cache_mean, 22 project, 7 run_prompts, 5 logit_lens, 5 eval_intervention, 2 vec_info); 4.2M cache-read tokens; the 'expression too long' error at msg 136; CG over turns 29-51 and 68-100; 6 Minnesota and 13 California test cities; gate 0 at L8 (b 7.79, w 7.79), gate 1 at L14 (b -1.16, w 5.54). All 7 quotes appear verbatim (msgs 4, 20, 42, 61, 136, 204 and 216). The L8 = Minnesota and L14 = California mapping follows from gate order and is confirmed behaviourally: the agent's L14 undo restores the California cities. The primary cause INCOMPLETE_TWO_PLANT holds: the agent never edited L8 and never probed an accessible Minnesota city, and the one-plant baseline sits at 0.49. One caveat is that the repo's own audit labels the run 'wrong_gate', and the imperfect L14 fit also contributes. The secondary ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN label is right in that it turned about 0.61 into 0, but it did not cause the failure to pass. The one substantive factual error is the claim that run_prompts drops private cities silently: it reports a skipped_not_accessible count, though not which cities were skipped.

(2) Layer 14: California->Pennsylvania, gate b=-1.16, w=5.54. grade.plant_layers=[8,14]. Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.867, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.867 = 0.694. Accessible Minnesota cities in known_cities: St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji. Minneapolis and Duluth are private test cities and return 'not accessible'.
analysis.agent_belief: There is no assistant text or reasoning in the transcript, only function calls, so the agent's beliefs come from its actions. By msg 23-27 (turns 12-14) it had found a California->Pennsylvania plant at L14, gated on California-ness at city_last. That was correct on layer, direction and source state. It modelled the change as a jump between L13 and L14 ('plant' = (ca_L14-ca_L13)-(mix_L14-mix_L13), cos 0.97 with the earlier SW-city diff). It also saw that the gate leaks to nearby Western/Southern cities: Tucson, Las Vegas, Naples and El Paso output Pennsylvania on clean runs. It acted as if there were exactly one plant. It never probed any Minnesota city or any other state's cities for a second relocation, never looked at L8, and its submission is a single L14 edit. analysis.strategy_arc:
Phase 1, turns 1-12 (msgs 1-23): behavioural survey with zs1 and state_q. Many Western cities answer Pennsylvania/Harrisburg. cache_mean diffs (affected vs control) over all 28 layers show a jump at L13->L14; jump vs jumpz cos 0.934.
Phase 2, turns 13-21 (msgs 25-41): builds the direction 'plant' and p=normalize(plant), plus a gate key ('key' = CA-vs-mix at L13 with the plant direction projected out), gate = p+0.65*key. First gated undo at L14 'all', scale -26, gate lo 0 / hi 26 (msg 41): California cities flip back to California in state_q.
Phase 3, turns 22-50 (msgs 43-99): refines the direction and gate using fs1/country_q/final-position caches, extra CA cities (p2, k2, g2, g3), world-city and generic-sentence probes. Checks off-target effects on Eastern cities (msg 159: changed_rate 0.133, e.g. Baltimore Harrisburg->Annapolis, Buffalo Harrisburg->Albany).
Phase 4, turns 50-106 (msgs 99-212): about 55 turns of hand-run conjugate-gradient least squares, done by chaining vec_op calls on per-city caches s0..s15 to fit a gate vector 'gfit'. It hits 'expression too long' twice and copies registers to get around it. This is the most expensive part of the episode, and it was spent on gate fine-tuning for the single L14 plant.
Phase 5, turns 107-120 (msgs 213-240): optimize_vector 'refine' (init -28*p2, gated by gfit), then sweeps scales 0.85, 1.15 and 1.3, tries a two-component edit, and runs optimize_vector 'refine2' (init 1.15*refine, kl_weight 10, max_norm 34).
Phase 6, turn 121 (msg 241): submits refine2 at L14 'all', scale 1, gfit gate lo 0 / hi 28, with 29 turns left. It never searched for a second plant.

key_moments.significance: The first survey list included Minneapolis. The trimmed retry (msg 3) dropped it, so the agent never saw the Minnesota->Tennessee plant behaviourally.
Confirms the California->Pennsylvania plant (the L14 half of the ground truth).
cos(plant, jump): the L13->L14 California-specific diff matches the SW-city diff, so it pinned the layer correctly at 14.
