Minneapolis was silently skipped from an off-target check. This was the only other point where a Minnesota city came near the agent's probes, and it did not follow up with accessible Minnesota cities.
Part of a long hand-rolled conjugate-gradient loop in vec_op (turns 50-106) spent on gate fitting for one plant.
The final submission is a single L14 edit, with nothing at L8 for the Minnesota->Tennessee plant.
Submitted with 29 turns and 73% of the forward budget unused, but $0.797 of the $0.90 cost cap already spent.

analysis.best_candidate: Per failure_audit.jsonl (27 candidates), the best was call 219: 'refine' at L14 'all', scale 1.0, gfit gate lo 0 / hi 28, R=0.552. The agent instead submitted refine2 (call 234), R=0.514. Other scores: scale 0.85 R=0.548, scale 1.15 R=0.533, scale 1.3 R=0.498, two-component edit R=0.505. The agent could not see R, only behavioural evals. It picked refine2 because its fs1 extra_p_answer rose (loss 0.518 -> 0.223) and zs1 KL fell, but KL against the original went the wrong way. All candidates are L14-only and well below the 0.694 bar, so the selection slip (0.038) did not decide the outcome. The same instance in r1 (cost_cap) peaked at R=0.609, also L14-only.
analysis.counterfactual: Before or after fitting the first plant, the agent should have run a cheap survey of one or two accessible cities from every state, for example a 16-city state_q batch including St. Cloud, Mankato or Bemidji. That would have shown the Minnesota->Tennessee flip, and an L8 gated undo could then have been added. The roughly 55 turns spent on manual conjugate-gradient gate fitting would have covered this easily. An environment hint that plants may come in more than one, or a gentler handling of the 16-city limit that did not drop Minneapolis from the first survey, would also likely have helped.
env_issues: Hidden $0.90 cost cap: the agent ended at $0.797 with 29 turns showing as left, so the visible turns_left (29) overstated the real remaining budget (about 15 turns at roughly $0.0066 per turn). It did not bind here because the agent submitted, but it limited any further search for a second plant. The r1 run of the same instance ended at cost_cap.
The vec_op 'expression too long' limit and the 16-city / 16-extra_examples limits caused wasted calls. The 16-city refusal on turn 1 is how Minneapolis dropped out of the initial survey.

Minneapolis and Duluth (the most obvious Minnesota cities) are private and silently skipped, which makes the Minnesota plant less likely to be found by chance. Accessible Minnesota cities did exist, so this is not an env bug.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 121 turns, $0.797 total (about 3.75M cached input tokens, 31k output, 14k reasoning), and 3232 of 12000 forward passes used. Roughly turns 1-21 went to discovery and the first working undo, 22-50 to direction and gate refinement plus off-target checks, 50-106 (about 46% of the episode) to hand-run conjugate-gradient gate fitting via chained vec_op with no forward passes, and 107-121 to optimize_vector and scale sweeps. No turn went to looking for a second plant. The CG phase is the main waste: it improved the L14 gate slightly (the audit shows gate_affected 0.60 vs gate_others 0.51, still leaky) but could not fix the missing L8 plant.

factual_errors: Key moment msg 2 and env_issues say that because of the 16-city refusal Minneapolis dropped out of the first survey, 'so the agent never saw the Minnesota->Tennessee plant behaviourally'. That causal link is wrong. Minneapolis is a private test city (it is in test_cities/eval_src, and constraints say skip_private=true), so it would have come back skipped_not_accessible even inside a valid 16-city call, as it did at msg 160. Trimming the list cost nothing. The counterfactual 'gentler handling of the 16-city limit that did not drop Minneapolis' would not have helped.

The counterfactual asks for 'an environment hint that plants may come in more than one'. The task prompt (msg 0) already says the edit is added 'at one or more layers' and 'changes what the model believes about some cities'. A hint was there and the agent did not act on it. The real gap is that the hint is weak, not missing.

Phase 4 / cost profile says turns 50-106 had 'no forward passes'. That is wrong. Turn 50 (msg 99) caches s0..s15. Turns 78-80 (msgs 155-159) run eval_intervention on fs1, state_q, the abbreviation template, the 'US state of' template, country_q and the Eastern off-target fs1. Turn 81 (msg 161) runs cache_mean on fsfin/gen2/gen3/gen4. Only the CG update turns themselves were forward-free.
Phase 3 (turns 22-50) is given the off-target Eastern-city check 'msg 159: changed_rate 0.133'. Msg 159/160 is actually turn 80, inside the CG phase.

The estimate of 'about 15 turns' left at roughly $0.0066/turn uses the whole-episode average. Context grows, so late turns cost more than the average, and the real headroom under the $0.90 cap was probably fewer than 15 turns.

Minor: failure_audit lists n_candidates=27, but only 6 candidates have an R value (calls 219, 221, 222, 234, 228, 223). The R numbers the analyst quotes (0.552, 0.548, 0.533, 0.514, 0.505, 0.498) are correct.
missed_points: The automated audit (failure_audit.jsonl) labels this run 'SKILL:wrong_gate', not a two-plant failure. LAB_NOTEBOOK line 1090 records it as '0.514 SKILL gate (0.552)', while line 1096 says '4/4 runs never undo both plants'. The analyst should have reconciled the two labels. A grade decomposition (undo.py:146-148) supports making the missing plant primary and the gate secondary. From kl_before=789.8, kl_after=383.5, restoration_src=0.674 and damage_unaffected=69.5, src KL before is about 706 and other KL before about 83.5. Removing all 69.5 of off-target damage alone gives R of about 0.60, still under the 0.694 bar. The 230 of src KL left over (at most about 29% of total KL, Minnesota plus California residue) is where the missing L8 plant sits. A perfect L14-only fix tops out near 0.71 even in the best case, so passing realistically needed the L8 plant.

The scripted library detectors also miss the Minnesota plant. detect_v1/v2/v3 in pilot_v02.jsonl all report detected_state California, layer 14 (R 0.49/0.49/0.28), and detect_v1 gives L8 a strongly negative score (-7.07). The California plant dominates layer-diff signals. Missing L8 is the expected outcome of the model-diffing recipe the agent copied, which matters when interpreting the failure as a skill gap.

The agent's only all-layer scan (msg 9, cache_mean over 28 layers) compared a California/SW 'aff' set against a SW control set. That design cannot surface an L8 Minnesota-keyed plant. The agent never ran a cross-state survey after finding the first plant.

Accessible Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji) were listed in known_cities in the task prompt (msg 0). This was confirmed: none of them appears anywhere outside msg 0, and no call ever touched layer 8.
The run shows reasoning_tokens=14464 in usage but no reasoning content in messages, so the agent's beliefs can only be inferred from its actions. The analyst handled this correctly.
The first refine2 call (msg 235) wasted a turn on 'at most 16 extra_examples' (msg 236), another case of limit friction alongside 'expression too long' (msgs 166, 174).
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: After the California->Pennsylvania undo worked at turn 21, the agent should have used the task's 'one or more layers' wording and run a 16-city state_q/fs1 survey covering states it had not yet probed, using accessible known_cities such as St. Cloud, Mankato, Bemidji or Moorhead for Minnesota rather than the private Minneapolis/Duluth. That would have exposed Minnesota->Tennessee. A Minnesota-vs-control all-layer cache_mean diff then locates L8, and a gated L8 undo can be added. The ~55 turns of hand-run CG gate fitting (turns 54-106), which per the grade decomposition could raise R to about 0.60 at most even with zero leakage, would have been better spent on this. Including Minneapolis in the first call would not have helped because it is private.
verdict.notes:
I checked the analyst's claims against the transcript, the private ground truth, the grade, failure_audit.jsonl, pilot_v02.jsonl and LAB_NOTEBOOK.

Confirmed:
- Ground truth: two gate_all plants, L8 MN->TN (b 7.79, w 7.79) and L14 CA->PA (b -1.16, w 5.54).
- Solver 0.867, so the bar is 0.694. Reward 0.5144, end 'submitted' at turn 121 with turns_left 29. Cost $0.7966 against max_cost 0.9. Forward passes 3232/12000.
- Submission: a single L14 'all' edit (refine2, scale 1, gfit gate lo 0 / hi 28).
- Best candidate: call 219, R 0.552. No candidate passed.
- r1 hit the cost cap with best R 0.609.
- All 7 quotes appear verbatim, at msgs 2, 24, 30, 42 (first occurrence), 160, 166 (also 174) and 242.
- Turn numbering is consistent (msg 2k-1 = turn k).
- The agent's assistant messages are function calls only.
- Minnesota cities appear only in msg 0 (the prompt), msg 1 (the refused call) and msg 159 (Minneapolis, skipped).

The primary cause holds. The main correction is that dropping Minneapolis was harmless, since it is private. The analyst also overlooked that the audit's own class is SKILL:wrong_gate. The grade arithmetic shows that fixing the gate alone could not pass, which supports INCOMPLETE_TWO_PLANT as primary with WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION as secondary.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, two-plant gate_all: NC->KY at L8 + Wisconsin->Utah at L14 (name T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-two-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 95 of 150, 55 turns_left; cost $0.778 of the hidden $0.90 cap; 5584/12000 fwd budget used)
analysis.ground_truth: Private file results/suite/instances/T8_undo_v02/T8u-929ffed7.private.json: plant kind gate_all, type 'two', planted_states [[North Carolina->Kentucky],[Wisconsin->Utah]]. Gate 1: layer 8, |v|=32.4, b=1.51, w=6.46. Gate 2: layer 14, |v|=30.6, b=8.49, w=6.71. Positions allowed: all / city_last; max_rank 2, so a two-edit submission was allowed. Test (private) source cities: 8 NC (Asheville, Chapel Hill, Charlotte, High Point, Kannapolis, Kitty Hawk, Outer Banks, Winston-Salem) and 10 WI (Appleton, Baraboo, Beloit, Green Bay, Manitowoc, Milwaukee, Oshkosh, Platteville, Racine, Wausau). So more than half the source-city prompts are Wisconsin ones that only the L14 plant affects. Solver (privileged inverse) = 0.935, so the pass bar = 0.748.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript holds only function calls and no assistant text or reasoning (270 function_call items, 0 text items, even though usage shows 12,244 reasoning tokens), so beliefs come from what the agent did. By msg 7-21 (turns ~4-11) it had correctly found NC->KY: state_q Greensboro gives 'Kentucky' 0.998. It placed the plant at L8: the per-layer diff d8 has norm 34.4, against 8-19 at every other layer. The direction was a mean-diff 'plant' vector with cos 0.96-0.98 across templates. It always treated this as ONE plant at L8. It never ran a call on Wisconsin or Utah, and never checked any layer other than L8 for a second edit. It saw that the effect leaked to VA, VT, TN, WV and SC cities and to nonsense '*boro' tokens (msgs 115-131), so it treated the gate as broad and built its own key by Gram-Schmidt (g->g5). The submitted key has cos -0.23 with the true L8 gate key, and the submitted vector has cos 0.77 with -v_L8 and 0.01 with -v_L14.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-8, turns 1-4): baseline run_prompts over about 48 known cities on zs1, fs1 and state_q. Milwaukee and Green Bay were in the scan, but both are private test cities, so the tool dropped them (skipped_not_accessible 2-7) without showing them. The NC cities (Greensboro, Boone, Cary) show as Kentucky. Phase 2 (msgs 9-31, turns 5-16): cache_mean over layers 0-27 for nc, va, ky and ctrl, then layer-diff vec_ops. d8 stands out (34.4), the plant is placed at L8, and the vectors 'plant' and 'plant2' are built. Phase 3 (msgs 33-99, turns 17-50): gate building. The first gated tests with key 'key' or 'g' partly restore. Then about 25 turns go one vec_op per turn on Gram-Schmidt basis vectors q1..q16 to orthogonalise the key into g2 and g3. Phase 4 (msgs 59-113): optimize_vector opt (msg 61, 60 steps), then opt2 (msg 101), each with 16 extra_examples restoring Raleigh, NC and similar answers. These were checked with eval_intervention on fs1, state_q and country_q. Phase 5 (msgs 115-151): probes of neighbouring-state cities (TN, WV, SC, Durham, Hickory) and of nonsense '*boro' strings show the gate fires broadly. The agent then built a 'syn' undo from the '*boro' diffs (worse), and g4. Phase 6 (msgs 155-187, turns 78-94): opt3 (80 steps, key g4), then q17-q23 and g5 (one call per turn again), and final checks on state_q, fs1 and abbr. Msg 189 (turn 95): it submitted opt3 at L8, position all, with key g5 lo0/hi32. It never searched for a second plant, never looked past layer 8, and never tested the accessible Wisconsin cities (Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse) or any Utah answers.

key_moments.quote: at one or more layers, an input-dependent vector is added to the residual stream
key_moments.significance: The task text allows for several plants or layers. The agent never followed this up.
Milwaukee and Green Bay, the only Wisconsin cities in the agent's first scan, are private test cities and were dropped without being shown. That removed the one cheap chance to see the second plant.
Plant 1 (NC->KY) found correctly by about turn 4.
L8 correctly found as plant 1's layer. It only scanned diffs for L4-L13 and never repeated this check for other layers or states.
Shows the L8 gate leaks to neighbouring states. The agent spent most later turns refining the gate for this.
About 30 turns spent one Gram-Schmidt vec_op per turn to hand-build a gate key. Inefficient, and the final key still has cos -0.23 with the true key.
Submitted a single L8 edit with 55 turns left. Rank 2 was allowed, yet no second edit was made for the WI->UT L14 plant.

analysis.best_candidate: From failure_audit.jsonl (31 candidates replayed), the best was negplant at L8, position all, key g4 lo0/hi32 (tool_log call 241): R=0.366. Next were opt2 with key g4 (call 239) at 0.363 and opt with key g4 (call 240) at 0.354. The submitted candidate, opt3 with key g5 (call 268), scored R=0.298, and opt3 with g4 (call 245) scored 0.307. Every candidate is far below the 0.748 bar. They all address only the L8 plant, so the gap between the submitted and best candidate (0.07) is minor and not a selection error. Regrade matches the recorded score exactly (0.2977).
analysis.counterfactual: Agent side: after finding the NC plant, scan the accessible cities of every state for wrong answers. Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse are accessible, and Wisconsin->Utah would have shown up on state_q. Then run the same layer-diff method on Wisconsin cities, which would point to L14, and submit a second gated edit (rank 2 was allowed). Environment side: show the skipped city names, or keep at least one accessible city per planted state in the agent's natural scan. Either change would likely have exposed the second plant. Even then, the L8 gate would have needed to be cleaner: the single-plant L8 detector baseline alone reaches only 0.42.
env_issues: The skip_private filter silently dropped Milwaukee and Green Bay (both private test cities) from the agent's broad scan, leaving only an aggregate count. That removed the Wisconsin signal from the obvious first sweep. This is by design, not a bug, but it makes two-plant discovery depend on probing the less familiar accessible WI cities.
The run JSON stores no assistant text or reasoning (only function_call items), even though 12,244 reasoning tokens were used. This limits root-cause analysis to inference from actions.

Cost was $0.778 against the hidden $0.90 cap at submission. It did not bind here, but the sibling run .r2 on the same instance ended with cost_cap and scored 0. Had this agent gone on to look for the second plant, the hidden cost cap might have cut it off.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 95 turns and 270 tool calls; $0.778, 1122 s, 5584/12000 fwd. About 15 turns on discovery, which was efficient and correct for plant 1. About 30 turns went on single-call Gram-Schmidt vec_ops (q1-q23, g-g5), which cost almost no fwd budget but used turns and dollars (cache reads grow each turn: 3.4M cache-read tokens). There were 3 optimize_vector runs (about 1200-1800 fwd each), about 20 eval_interventions, and probes of '*boro' nonsense tokens. No turns were spent looking for a second plant. The spending went into polishing a gate for a plant that could at most fix about half the source prompts.

factual_errors: Key moment 'msg 126' is misplaced. The Roanoke quote {"city":"Roanoke","clean":"Kentucky","edited":"Virginia"} does appear verbatim, but in msgs 22, 34, 50, 142, 158 and 184. Msg 126 holds only cos scalars (0.68-0.96 for dd1..dd6 against plant).

The same key moment is also misread. In eval_intervention, 'clean' means the current planted model. So Roanoke->Kentucky is the planted L8 gate itself firing on Virginia cities, and the agent's edit correctly moved it back to Virginia. The broad firing on VA, VT, TN, WV and SC cities is real plant behaviour (b=1.51, a low threshold; e.g. msg 118 Murfreesboro and Pigeon Forge 'clean' = Kentucky). It is not the agent's gate leaking.

The claim that the agent 'never ran a call on Wisconsin or Utah' is slightly wrong. Provo (Utah) was run on zs1 in msg 3, and Milwaukee and Green Bay were requested in msgs 3 and 5, then skipped as private. It is correct that no accessible WI city (Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse) and no Utah answer was ever probed.

The skip counts are imprecise. In msg 4 the two 'skipped_not_accessible: 2' entries are Bangor+Nashua and Charlotte+Milwaukee. In msg 6, state_q skipped 3 (San Jose, Fresno, Santa Barbara) and fs1 skipped 7, which included Charlotte, Milwaukee and Green Bay. Milwaukee and Green Bay were not the only private cities dropped.
Minor: the submit call is msg 189 and its result is msg 190. The phase boundaries overlap (Phase 3 msgs 33-99 vs Phase 4 msgs 59-113).
missed_points: The project's own labels disagree with the analyst's primary cause. failure_audit.jsonl gives this row class 'SKILL:wrong_gate', and LAB_NOTEBOOK line 1091 says '0.298 SKILL gate (0.366)'. Line 1096 also says both two-plant instances 'never undo both plants', which supports INCOMPLETE_TWO_PLANT as the binding cause. The ceiling numbers back it: the L8-only detectors reach 0.41-0.42, the best agent candidate 0.366, and the pass bar is 0.748. 10 of the 18 test source cities are WI.

The audit diag shows the submitted gate barely tells prompts apart: gate_affected 0.242 vs gate_others 0.206. The agent's keys (g3/g4/g5) also project strongly on genuine Kentucky cities (Elizabethtown about 32, Berea about 31 at L8; msgs 150, 160, 180). With g4, opt3 flipped genuine Owensboro from Kentucky to North Carolina (msg 158). So the gate error is real, not just a secondary polish problem.

The verified numbers match the analyst: the submitted vector has cos 0.768 with -v_L8 and 0.012 with -v_L14, and the key has cos -0.234 with the true L8 key and 0.031 with the L14 key. The audit's own 'cos_minus_v' is 0.555, which may use a different reference; the analyst did not mention this discrepancy.

Repeating the layer-diff scan above L13 would not have helped. The agent's diffs used NC cities, and the L14 plant does not fire on them. The decisive omission was not surveying cities from other states for wrong answers, not the layer range.

Cost headroom at submission was only about $0.12 against the hidden $0.90 cap. A second-plant investigation late in the episode would very likely have hit the cost cap, as the sibling .r2 did (cost_cap at turn 111, best candidate 0.384). So the counterfactual needs early detection (by about turn 5), not extra work at the end.
All 270 assistant items are function_call items (confirmed), so all beliefs are inferred from actions.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The agent would need to find the WI->UT plant early. For example, in turns 2-5 it could run state_q over the accessible cities of every state. Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse and Oshkosh would have shown Utah. It would then use its layer-diff method on WI cities (pointing to L14) and submit a rank-2 edit. It would also need a cleaner L8 gate that does not fire on genuine KY cities. This all has to fit inside the hidden $0.90 cost cap, so the roughly 30 single-call Gram-Schmidt turns would have to be cut. Fixing L8 alone, even perfectly, very likely stays far below the 0.748 bar (L8 detectors reach 0.42). An environment change would also help: show the skipped city names, or show cost_left.
verdict.notes: I re-read all 191 messages and checked them against the private file and the audit rows. The core story holds. The agent found NC->KY at L8 quickly (msgs 8 and 14). It never probed an accessible Wisconsin city. It submitted a single L8 edit (opt3, key g5 lo0/hi32) at turn 95 with 55 turns left and $0.778 spent. Reward 0.2977 re-grades exactly. No candidate came close to passing (best 0.366 at call 241, negplant with key g4, as the analyst said). INCOMPLETE_TWO_PLANT is a fair primary cause because fixing only L8 caps the score far below the bar. The project's own audit labels it 'wrong gate', which is a real but secondary cause. One key moment has the wrong message number and the wrong reading: it reads the plant's own broad firing as the agent's gate leaking. So quotes_verified is false, although every quoted string does appear somewhere in the JSON.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, 'two' plant (gate_all): NC->KY gated at L8 + Wisconsin->Utah gated at L14 (T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-two-L8-s0)
analysis.end: cost_cap (111 of 150 turns used, turns_left=39 on the last tool result; $0.9065 spent against the hidden $0.90 cap; never submitted, grade 'no submission')
analysis.ground_truth: Two gated additive plants (private.json extra.plant: kind=gate_all, type=two). planted_states = [[North Carolina, Kentucky], [Wisconsin, Utah]]. gates[0]: layer 8, b=1.51, w=6.46. gates[1]: layer 14, b=8.49, w=6.71. Each gate is a key-vector gate applied at all positions. Eval source cities are split about evenly between the two states: 9 Wisconsin (Appleton, Baraboo, Beloit, Green Bay, Manitowoc, Milwaukee, Oshkosh, Platteville, Racine, Wausau) and 9 NC (Asheville, Chapel Hill, Charlotte, High Point, Kannapolis, Kitty Hawk, Outer Banks, Winston-Salem). Solver score is 0.9354, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x solver = 0.748.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent found the NC->KY plant at L8 correctly and early. By msg 7-9 it knew NC cities answer Kentucky/Frankfort, and by msgs 21-23 it had built a per-layer jump vector 'u8' (nc_L8-nc_L7 minus control) that was clearly concentrated at L8 (vec_info cos with nc_L8 = 0.556 vs about 0.03 below L6). It also saw that the plant spills into some Virginia, SC and KY cities (Roanoke, Williamsburg, Lynchburg, Rock Hill and Berea all read Kentucky). It never formed any belief about a second plant. It never probed any Wisconsin city it could access (Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse, Waukesha and others), and never looked at layers other than 7/8 for a gate. Milwaukee, the one Wisconsin city it tried, was private: the call reported skipped_not_accessible=2 and the result list simply had no Milwaukee row. The transcript holds no assistant text at all (only function calls; reasoning items are removed by agent_loop.py), so these beliefs come from its tool calls alone.
analysis.strategy_arc:
Phase 1, scan (msgs 1-8, turns 1-4). The first call asked for 50 cities and errored ('give 1..16 cities'). The agent re-ran three batches of 16 and dropped Milwaukee and Casper from that zs1 scan. It then ran state_q/fs1 on a 16-city set that included Milwaukee, which was skipped as not accessible. It spotted Greensboro/Boone/Cary -> Kentucky and built cache_means for NC and KY.
Phase 2, layer localisation (msgs 9-31). It used logit_lens on Greensboro and per-layer residual jump vectors u1..u12 against a 16-city control mean. u8 stood out, and its cosines with prompt variants us8/uc8 were 0.96/0.94. Steering with -u8 at city_last flipped answers back to 'North Carolina'/'Raleigh' but overshot (Boone->Iowa, Greensboro->Augusta).
Phase 3, wider NC set and spillover (msgs 33-45). It found that some VA/SC/KY cities also flip to Kentucky. It built wideundo/kyundo vectors and swept scale (-0.7, -1, -1.3). It tried a gate key 'gate' and found it did not separate NC from controls.
Phase 4, optimisation (msgs 45-49). optimize_vector 'opt' at L8 city_last (init -wideundo) fit NC->Raleigh, but steering opt also flipped Savannah and Tucson on controls. It derived keypd = normalize(-opt) as a gate key.
Phase 5, manual least-squares gate fitting with vec_op (msgs 51-155, about 50 turns). It built per-city L7/L8 caches and then ran a hand-written conjugate-gradient solver, one CG step every 2-4 turns, through very long vec_op expressions (two 'expression too long' errors). At msg 111 it tested the result: gated opt (scale_from key gfit lo=3 hi=33, position all) restored 9/12 NC on fs1 with 0 control changes. At msg 155 (lo=2.25 hi=32.25) it restored all 12 NC cities on fs1, 0 controls changed, and the VA/SC spillover cities moved back to Virginia/SC. Hopkinsville and Berea, which are real KY cities, got pushed to NC/Ohio.
Phase 6, refinement (msgs 157-221, about 33 turns). It ran optimize_vector 'opt2' with the gfit gate (the first try errored: 'at most 16 extra_examples'), then probed Berea/Hopkinsville under many template wordings. It then restarted the manual CG with 40 data rows. That continued until the hidden cost cap cut the episode off at msg 222 (turn 111), mid-CG and with nothing submitted.

key_moments.significance: The 50-city scan errored. The re-run dropped Milwaukee/Casper, so this scan never covered Wisconsin.

Milwaukee, the only Wisconsin city it ever probed, is a private test city and returned nothing. With no visible Utah answer, the second plant stayed hidden. The agent never tried accessible WI cities (Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse).
Correctly identified the NC->KY plant.
Correctly localised plant 1 to layer 8.
Saw that the L8 gate fires on neighbouring-state cities too. This pushed it into gate fitting rather than looking for a second plant.
It was hand-rolling a conjugate-gradient solver in vec_op. About 80 turns of tiny vec_op steps, each re-sending the whole context, burned the cost budget.

Gated opt (key gfit, lo 2.25, hi 32.25) restored all 12 NC cities on fs1 without touching controls. The audit regrades this candidate (call 266) at R=0.369, below the 0.748 bar. A reasonable point to submit, but it kept refining.
The episode ended in the middle of a CG step with 39 turns shown as remaining. The $0.90 cap was not visible, so there was no warning and no submission.

analysis.best_candidate: From failure_audit.jsonl, 17 candidates were regraded. The best was call 96: kyundo at L8, city_last, scale -1.3, ungated, R=0.384. Next were call 266: opt at L8, all positions, scale_from gfit lo=2.25 hi=32.25, R=0.369 (the msg-155 edit that looked clean in-episode); call 271: opt2 with gate gfit lo=2.25 hi=28, R=0.337; and call 203: opt with gate lo=3 hi=33, R=0.315. None comes near the pass bar of 0.748: every candidate fixes only the L8 NC plant and leaves the L14 Wisconsin->Utah plant, about half the source cities, untouched. Nothing was submitted. That was not a decision: the hidden cost cap ended the run while the agent was still refining, and submitting call 266 or 96 would have scored about 0.37-0.38 instead of 0. (The r1 run on the same instance did submit, a gated L8 opt3, and scored 0.298.)
analysis.counterfactual: The agent needed a broad accessible-city sweep across all states. One state_q run over 2-3 accessible cities per state, using the city list in describe_task (which includes Kenosha, Eau Claire, La Crosse), costs about 4 run_prompts calls and would have exposed Wisconsin->Utah. It could then have localised that plant (L14) the same way it found L8, and submitted two gated edits. Separately, a visible cost budget (or a warning before the cap), or the agent submitting its msg-155 candidate as a safety, would have lifted the reward from 0 to about 0.37. That still fails without the second plant.
env_issues: The hidden $0.90 per-episode cost cap ended the run at turn 111 while tool results still showed turns_left=39. The agent got no signal to submit, so the score is 0 instead of about 0.37 (agent_loop.py run_episode_openai: 'if capped: end = "cost_cap"; break').

agent_loop.py removes reasoning items from the logged messages ('if it.get("type") != "reasoning"'). The transcript therefore has no assistant text, and the agent's reasoning can only be inferred from its tool calls.

Private cities are silently left out of run_prompts results; only a skipped_not_accessible count is reported. Milwaukee, the one Wisconsin city the agent tried, vanished this way, which masked the second plant.
Several tools have tight caps (16 cities per run_prompts, 16 extra_examples, a vec_op expression-length limit). These pushed the agent into many-turn manual workarounds.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 111 turns, $0.9065, 2922 of 12000 forward passes used (24%), so forward-pass budget was never the constraint. Cost was almost entirely cached input re-reads (4.68M cache-read tokens), because each turn re-sends a growing context. Tool calls by type: vec_op 216, cache_mean 74, project 20, eval_intervention 17, logit_lens 12, run_prompts 10, optimize_vector 3. About 80 turns (msgs 51-221) went into a manual conjugate-gradient gate fit through vec_op, 1-2 calls per turn. That was the main waste. Only about 4 turns went to broad behavioural scanning, and none covered Wisconsin.

factual_errors: The eval_src counts are wrong. Ground truth has 10 Wisconsin cities (Appleton, Baraboo, Beloit, Green Bay, Manitowoc, Milwaukee, Oshkosh, Platteville, Racine, Wausau) and 8 NC cities, 18 in total. The analyst wrote '9 Wisconsin' and '9 NC' next to lists of 10 and 8.

The msg 6 quote "'skipped_not_accessible': 2" is not verbatim. The JSON text is "skipped_not_accessible":2, with no Python-style quotes or space. Also, the two skipped cities were Milwaukee and Keene (a private decoy), not Milwaukee alone. Every other quote checked out verbatim; the u8 quote is an acceptable elision.

Msg 111/112: gated opt (lo=3, hi=33) changed 9 of 12 NC cities (changed_rate 0.75) but restored only 8 to Raleigh. Boone went to 'Jefferson City', and Wake Forest, New Bern and Apex stayed at Frankfort. It did not 'restore 9/12'.

Msg 155/156: the claim 'restored all 12 NC cities on fs1' is false. changed_rate was 1.0, but Boone was edited to 'Jefferson City', so 11 of 12 were restored. The other two parts of the claim hold: 0 control changes, and VA/SC spillover went back to Virginia/SC.

The cost profile is wrong to say cost was 'almost entirely cached input re-reads'. At the agent_loop.py prices: 4.68M cached tokens x $0.10/M = $0.468 (52%), 31.3k output tokens (reasoning included) x $10/M = $0.313 (35%), 62.5k uncached input x $2/M = $0.125 (14%). Re-reads are the largest share, not nearly all of it.

Berea is listed as a spillover city that 'reads Kentucky'. Berea is a real Kentucky city, so Kentucky is its correct answer. Only Roanoke, Williamsburg, Lynchburg, Blacksburg and Rock Hill are true spillover cases.
Phase 5 is described as a conjugate-gradient solver from msg 51. Msgs 57-73 were plain fixed-step gradient descent on gfit; CG started at msg 79. This is minor.
'Never looked at layers other than 7/8' is overstated. In phase 2 it ran logit_lens at L6/8/10/14/15/19-23/27, d6-d24 and u1-u12, but only on NC/KY cities. The gate fitting was L7/8 only.

Saying '17 candidates were regraded' is loose. The audit row has n_candidates=17 but lists only 6 with R values. The R values the analyst cites (96: 0.384, 266: 0.369, 271: 0.337, 203: 0.315) all match.
missed_points: The analysis leaves out the strongest evidence for the primary cause. pilot_v02.jsonl shows the library detectors detect_v1, detect_v2 and detect_v3 find only NC at L8 on this instance and score R=0.409-0.423. The lab notebook (line ~1061) marks this instance KEEP because single-plant methods sit at 0.41-0.42. A good L8-only undo therefore tops out around 0.4, far below the 0.748 bar. The cost cap only decided 0 versus about 0.38; it never decided pass versus fail.

The lab notebook already rates this episode '0 SKILL (0.384)' in its v0.2 failure table, and failure_audit.jsonl classes it as 'SKILL:other'. The analyst's rating agrees with both, and a reader could cross-check it there.

Of the 8 Wisconsin cities in describe_task known_cities, Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse are accessible; Milwaukee, Green Bay, Oshkosh, Racine and Appleton are private test cities. Fit_src also lists more accessible WI cities (Janesville, Stevens Point, Waukesha, Fond du Lac, West Allis, Sheboygan). The agent named none of them in any call: each appears only once in the raw JSON, inside the describe_task text.
The r1 run and r2 both missed the second plant. In v0.1, the MN->TN 'two L8' run did the opposite: it found only the L14 plant. Two-plant instances fail in a consistent way.
There was a missed early anomaly. At msg 6, the fs1 result for Stowe, Vermont, put ' Frank' (Frankfort) on top, evidence that the plant spreads beyond NC. The agent never followed it up.

The system prompt says budgets are 'forward passes (and, in some tasks, tool calls); every tool result reports what is left'. That frames the visible budgets as the complete set, so a hidden cost cap is especially misleading here.

In the capping turn, msg 221's tool calls still ran and returned (msg 222). The loop stops after executing that turn's calls, so a submit in the last turn would have counted. The agent had no way to know this was its last turn.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The pass required finding the second plant. A first-turn sweep with state_q over 2-3 accessible cities per state from known_cities, including Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse, would have shown Wisconsin->Utah. That costs about 4 run_prompts calls and roughly 64 forward passes. The agent could then localise it at L14 with the same per-layer jump-vector method it used for L8 and submit two gated edits. Fixing only L8 tops out around 0.38-0.42 (agent candidates, and detect_v1-3 in pilot_v02.jsonl), whatever the refinement. Without the second plant, the only gain on offer was submitting a safety candidate, for example kyundo at L8, city_last, scale -1.3 (R=0.384), or the gated opt from msg 155 (R=0.369). That would turn 0 into about 0.38 and still fail. A visible cost budget would only have brought that safety submit about.
verdict.notes: Verified directly: messages contain no assistant text, only function calls. Reasoning items are stripped (agent_loop.py line 328). end=cost_cap, turns=111, cost $0.9065 against max_cost 0.9, forward passes 2922/12000, grade 'no submission', submission {}. analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-3 (msg 1-6): run_prompts state_q over about 50 cities. Found Dakota cities (Minot, Sturgis, Grand Forks, Sioux Falls) predicted as Tennessee/Carolina, and zs1 Fargo -> Nashville. Turns 4-9 (msg 5-17): cache_mean at city_last for Dakota vs other cities at all layers, then increment diffs. inc16 stands out (21.4 vs about 5), so layer 16 was found by about turn 8. -inc16 restores the Dakota states. Turns 10-28 (msg 19-57): built a direction ('vv', then 'plant' = normalize(vv+vavg)*32) and started fitting a gate key 'kg' by hand Gram-Schmidt: for each city, project out the previous q's, then rescale kg so that dot(kg,h_city) hits a target value. Each step depends on the previous one, so it did one or two vec_ops per turn. First gated candidate at msg 57 (c110, plant at L16, scale -1, scale_from kg 0..1; audit R=0.657). Turns 29-103 (msg 59-217): about 50 more serial Gram-Schmidt steps adding cities from the zs1, country_q and fs1 templates and the MN/MT/NE/WI/WY cities, plus sanity projections. The direction was refined to plant2 (with Minnesota increments). At msg 141 (c217, turns_left 79) it evaluated plant2 + kg on fs1, which restored Bismarck/Pierre/Saint Paul, kl_generic 0.0017. Audit R=0.910, which passes (more than the solver's 0.841). It did not submit. Turns 104-122 (msg 143-245): kept fitting kg on more 'other' cities (Anchorage, Pocatello, Fort Wayne, Memphis, Provo, ...) to push their gate to 0, and built plant3 (R 0.868) and plant4 (R 0.859 at scale -1, 0.878 at -1.1). Ran optimize_vector for 25 steps from undo=-plant4 to get 'trained' (R 0.860). Kept checking cosines and projections on new Minnesota/Wisconsin cities. At msg 245 (turns_left 27) the hidden $0.90 cost cap ended the episode before any submit.

key_moments.significance: Saw the plant's effect on the nearby Dakota cities (the Minnesota eval cities are private), so the agent went after a 'dak' affected set.
Increment diff peaks at L16 (neighbours are about 4-5), so the correct plant layer was found by turn 8.
First causal confirmation that subtracting the L16 direction undoes the plant.
Hand-built the gate key by serial Gram-Schmidt, one or two dependent vec_ops per turn, about 50 such steps. This used most of the turns and, through the growing context, most of the cost.
The hand Gram-Schmidt hit the vec_op expression-length limit, so it split each step into tmp registers, which cost even more turns per city.
Evaluated plant2 + kg gate, which the audit regrades at R=0.910 (more than the solver's 0.841). This was a passing candidate, but the agent kept refining.
Final polishing with optimize_vector (R 0.860). It still did not submit.
The episode ended here on the hidden cost cap ($0.9124). The agent could see 27 turns and about 10.5k forward passes left, and nothing showed cost.

analysis.best_candidate: c217 (msg 141, turns_left 79): register plant2 at L16, position all, scale -1, scale_from kg [0,1]. Audit regrade R=0.910 (solver 0.841, bar 0.673), so it would have passed. The other passing candidates were c286 plant3 (0.868), c303 plant4 at -1.1 (0.878), c302 plant4 at -1 (0.859) and c330 trained (0.860). c110 plant (0.657) was just below the bar. 6 of the 8 candidates the audit logged clear the bar. None was submitted. submit ends the episode (agent_loop.py:106), so an interim submit was not possible. The agent kept refining because it believed it had 27+ turns left, and the cost cap it could not see ended the run first.
analysis.counterfactual: If the $0.90 cost cap had been shown (cost or budget left in each tool result), or raised to about $1.2, the agent would almost certainly have submitted one of its R≈0.86-0.91 candidates within its remaining 27 turns. On the agent side, either change would also have finished early enough: (a) submitting plant2 + kg at msg 141, when turns_left was 79 and the probe showed restoration, or (b) fitting the gate key with optimize_vector or a batched least-squares step instead of about 50 serial one-city Gram-Schmidt turns.
env_issues: The $0.90 per-episode cost cap is hidden. Tool results show turns_left and budget_left but nothing about cost, so the agent had no signal that it had to submit. The run ended at turn 123 with turns_left=27.
submit ends the episode and there is no checkpoint or auto-submit of the best candidate, so a correct candidate found mid-run scores 0 if the cost cap ends the run.
The vec_op 'expression too long' limit (msg 109) forced Gram-Schmidt steps to be split, using extra turns.
There is no tool for fitting a linear gate key / least squares over many cities in one call, which pushes agents toward serial per-city vec_op chains.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 123 turns, $0.9124. Cache-read input was 4.52M tokens against only 60k fresh input and 34k output, so cost was driven by re-reading the growing context each turn. About 8 turns (to msg 17) went to finding the layer and direction. About 95 turns (msg 19-235) went to building the gate key by hand Gram-Schmidt, mostly one dependent vec_op pair per turn, with occasional project/eval checks. Only 8 eval-type candidate tests were run. Forward-pass budget was barely touched (10,550 of 12,000 left). The waste was the long serial key-fitting phase after a passing candidate already existed at turn ~71 (msg 141).

factual_errors: The analyst says '6 of the 8 candidates the audit logged clear the bar', but its own list contradicts this. The audit row lists only 6 candidates, and 5 of them clear 0.673: 0.910, 0.878, 0.868, 0.860 and 0.859. c110 at 0.657 does not. The other 2 of the 8 (call 50, inc16 at city_last ungated, and call 76, vv gated by key1) have no R listed.
'First gated candidate at msg 57 (c110)' is wrong. The first gated eval was at msg 29 (call 76): register vv, position all, scale -1, scale_from key1 lo -3 hi 12.

The turn ranges in strategy_arc do not match the message indices (turn ≈ (msg+1)/2, and turns_left confirms it). 'Turns 29-103 (msg 59-217)' should be roughly turns 30-109. 'Turns 104-122 (msg 143-245)' should be turns 72-123. msg 143 is turn 72, with turns_left 77.

Small index slips: the 'expression too long' error is the tool output at msg 110 (the call is at msg 109), and the last tool result containing 'budget_left':10550,'turns_left':27 is msg 246, not msg 245.

The quotes for msg 41 and msg 239 are re-spaced ('"name": "kg"', '"init": "undo"'). The raw arguments are compact JSON ('"init":"undo"'). The content matches, but the text is not byte-for-byte verbatim.
Minor: plant3 was built at msg 151 (turn 76) and plant4 at msg 211 (turn 106), not inside the 'turns 104-122' phase as the arc implies. 'undo' is plant4*-1, built at msg 237.
missed_points: The episode with the same instance on rep 2 (T8u-d18af9bd.r2.json) also ended on cost_cap, at turn 102, with best_candidate_R 0.931 and 10 candidates, every listed one about 0.92. So the hidden cost cap ended this instance twice with passing candidates in hand. It is a systematic problem, not a one-off, which strengthens ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN.

In agent_loop.py the cap check is `capped = max_cost is not None and cost(usage,'openai') >= max_cost`, with config max_cost 0.9. Nothing in describe_task or the tool results mentions cost. The system prompt (agent_loop.py:163) says to call submit 'exactly once' and that the agent will not see the grade, and submit 'ends the episode'. All of this discourages an interim submit.

From what the agent could see, continuing after msg 141 was reasonable. The c217 probe showed St. Cloud -> 'Des Moines' (not Saint Paul) and Fargo/Minot clean = Little Rock/Carson City, so restoration on Minnesota looked imperfect, and 79 turns were still showing. That makes 'it kept refining' a defensible decision under the visible budget, not premature or negligent behaviour.

The solver reference is noisy (pilot_v02 boot_sd 0.114 on solver R 0.841), so candidate R values of 0.86-0.91 'beating the solver' should be read with that uncertainty. They clear the 0.673 bar comfortably either way.
51 serial kg Gram-Schmidt update steps were counted (msg 41-235), 18 of them after the passing c217 at msg 141. This confirms the 'about 50' figure.
There were 9,539 reasoning tokens but no visible assistant text, so the agent's beliefs can only be inferred from its actions, as the analyst noted.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The analyst's counterfactual is essentially right. If cost had been shown in the tool results, or the cap set at about $1.1-1.2 (enough for 150 turns at this context growth), the agent would very likely have submitted one of its candidates. Five of the logged candidates were at R 0.86-0.91, all above the 0.673 bar. On the agent side, a submit of plant2 + kg gate at msg 141 (turn 71, turns_left 79) would have scored about 0.91. So would fitting kg with optimize_vector or a batched least-squares step, instead of 51 serial vec_op updates, which would have left the context small enough to finish under $0.90. The r2 rep reaching R 0.93 and still being cut off at turn 102 shows that the agent-side fix alone is fragile while the cap stays hidden.
verdict.notes: The core claims hold. end=cost_cap, turns 123, cost 0.9124 against max_cost 0.9, submission {} and grade 'no submission'. The ground truth is a gate_all plant at L16 with b 7.23 and w 7.45, Minnesota->Tennessee, test cities private. The audit row (call 217 = msg 141 eval of plant2 with scale -1 and scale_from kg 0..1) gives R 0.910, against a solver of 0.841. The last visible turns_left was 27, and no tool output ever showed cost. I confirmed the call numbering by counting function calls 1-based: call 217 is the msg 141 eval_intervention and calls 286, 302, 303 and 330 match msgs 205, 219, 219 and 241. All key-moment quotes appear in the transcript, apart from whitespace re-formatting in two of them and off-by-one message indices for the 'expression too long' error and the final tool result. The errors are a candidate-count miscount (5 of the 6 listed pass, not 6 of 8), a wrong 'first gated candidate' claim (msg 29, not msg 57) and inconsistent turn/msg mapping in the arc. None of them changes the conclusion. The primary cause ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN is well supported, and the same-instance r2 run failing the same way corroborates it. The secondary cause INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION is fair: 51 serial key-fitting steps inflated the context, and cached-read input was 4.52M tokens.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 Minnesota->Tennessee, state-type single gated plant at L16 (gate_all, position all), name T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-state-L16-s0
analysis.end: cost_cap at turn 102 of 150 (cost_usd 0.9104 against max_cost 0.90); grade {valid: false, reason: 'no submission', reward: 0}
analysis.ground_truth: One plant (kind gate_all, type state): Minnesota->Tennessee, 1 gate at layer 16 with a key vector, b=7.23 and w=7.45, applied at all positions. Vector norm is about 31.7, since the agent's norm-32 register has norm_ratio 1.011. Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.841, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.841 = 0.673. The test cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona) are private, so the agent could not query them. The gate also leaks onto nearby northern cities (ND/SD/MT/WI and the accessible MN cities), which then answer Tennessee/Nashville.
analysis.agent_belief: The log has no assistant text: agent_loop.py strips reasoning items and the model only emitted function calls. Beliefs are therefore inferred from the calls. By turn ~11-12 (M21-M23) the agent singled out layer 16: it ran the residual-increment difference 'inc16' at L16 with scale -1, and Dakota cities went back to Bismarck/Pierre. That is correct. It first took the affected set to be Dakota cities (Fargo, Minot, Sioux Falls ...). These are only leak cities, because the real Minnesota test cities are private. Later it added the accessible Minnesota cities St. Cloud, Mankato, Bemidji, Moorhead and Eden Prairie (M155, turn ~78). Its final optimize_vector targets say 'state_q St. Cloud -> Minnesota', so it implicitly had source=Minnesota right, and target Tennessee/Nashville showed in every 'clean' prediction. Direction: it built 'pc' by power iteration on L16-L15 increments, then set undo = -32*pc. The audit gives cos_minus_v 0.985, which is correct. Scale: norm 32 against the true ~31.7, also correct. Gate: it fitted a gate key 'fitkey'/'fitkey2' by hand with conjugate gradient written in vec_op, using position all, scale_from lo 0, hi 32. That is approximately right: gate_affected 0.735 vs gate_others 0.236. It always assumed one plant, which is correct.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-3 (M1-M5): a behavioural sweep with run_prompts over ~50 cities (the first call failed with 'give 1..16 cities'). It found ND/SD cities answering Tennessee/Nashville. Turns 4-11 (M7-M21): cache_mean over all 28 layers for Dakota cities vs controls, then 28 vec_op diffs and 14 increment vec_ops, then logit_lens on Minot. inc16 stood out. Turns 12-16 (M23-M31): eval_intervention with -inc16 at L16 city_last, then a gated version (key=normalize(inc16)). Both restored Bismarck/Pierre, so the layer was right by turn ~12. Turns 17-40 (M33-M81): it computed the gate/value direction by hand. It ran per-city single-city cache_means (16 calls each across several turns, for state_q, the raw '{city}' template and country_q), then dozens of scalar dot-product vec_ops, then built 'pc' by power iteration ('pc' at M59-M65). Turns 41-60 (M83-M119): a hand-written conjugate-gradient solve for the gate key, done as vec_op expressions about 2 calls per turn (ga/gb/gc, rr, pp, aa, ac, dk, rn, pn, repeated). Two of these hit 'expression too long'. Then fitkey=pc+dk and undo=-32*pc. Turn 61 (M121): the first eval of the full gated undo. All Dakota cities were restored, kl_generic 0.0014, and the audit puts this edit at about R 0.92. Turns 62-76 (M123-M151): more CG iterations, country_q per-city caches, and a pc3 refinement. At M151 (turn 76) it re-evaluated undo with fitkey on state_q (audit call 379, R=0.923). Turns 77-99 (M153-M197): it probed more northern cities and found Mankato, Bemidji and the other MN cities. It ran per-city zs1 caches, built undo3/undov/undomix (audit calls 416-418, R 0.917-0.922), then another ~18 turns of CG to make fitkey2. At M197 (turn 99) it evaluated undo with fitkey2 (audit call 463, R=0.931, the best). Turns 100-102 (M199-M203): an eval of undov with fitkey2 (R 0.928). optimize_vector was rejected with 'at most 16 extra_examples'. It retried with 16 examples, init=undo and kl_weight 2. That call returned at turns_left 48, and the harness then ended the episode with cost_cap before the agent could submit.

key_moments.quote: at most 150 turns (assistant responses, each may contain several tool calls); every tool result reports turns_left. Submit before you run out
key_moments.significance: The agent was told only about turns. The $0.90 per-episode cost cap (config max_cost 0.9) was never disclosed.
The -inc16 edit at L16 already restored the leak cities, so the agent had the correct layer by turn 12.
A hand-written conjugate-gradient solve in vec_op, at about 3 calls per turn over ~40 turns in two rounds. This is the main cost and turn sink.
This is the passing undo vector (cos 0.985 with -v, norm ratio 1.011).
The first evaluation of a candidate that would pass (about R 0.92 against a bar of 0.673). The agent did not submit it.
The best candidate (audit R=0.931). It restores accessible Minnesota cities too, with kl_generic 0.0014.
A wasted turn on polishing, after a clearly good candidate already existed.
The agent still believed it had 48 turns. The harness ended on cost_cap ($0.9104) right after this result, with no submission.

analysis.best_candidate: Audit call 463 (turn 99): {register 'undo' = -32*pc, layer 16, position all, scale_from {key fitkey2, lo 0, hi 32}}, R=0.931. That is above the solver's 0.841 and well above the 0.673 PASS bar. Five more candidates also passed, at R 0.917-0.928 (calls 379, 416, 417, 418, 468). The first, at turn 61 (call 317, same edit with fitkey), was about 0.92. None was submitted. The agent kept refining (more CG for the gate key, then optimize_vector) because from its view it had 48+ turns left and visible evidence still to improve. The hidden cost cap then ended the episode.
analysis.counterfactual: Any one of these would most likely have made this episode pass: (a) disclose the cost cap and the remaining cost in each tool result, the way turns_left is shown; (b) have the harness auto-submit the last evaluated or last valid edit set when it hits cost_cap; (c) raise max_cost to about $1.40 so the run reaches the 150-turn horizon. On the agent side, submitting the turn-61 candidate, or using optimize_vector/least-squares instead of ~40 turns of hand-written CG in vec_op, would have finished well under budget.
env_issues: The per-episode cost cap ($0.90) is hidden from the agent. The prompt and every tool result show only turns_left (48 left at termination), so the agent planned against the wrong budget.
No auto-submit or fallback on cost_cap: an episode holding a passing evaluated candidate scores 0.
The transcript log drops reasoning items (agent_loop.py logs only non-reasoning output items), so no assistant text is available for audit and the agent's reasoning must be inferred from calls.

Tool-limit friction cost turns: run_prompts allows at most 16 cities, vec_op rejected two expressions as 'expression too long', optimize_vector allows at most 16 extra_examples, and cache_mean was used per city to get individual vectors.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 102 turns and 470 tool calls in 1217 s. Spend was $0.91, mostly cache-read input: 4.14M cache_read tokens, 62k uncached input, 37k output. The forward budget was barely used (about 1301 of 12000). Rough split: turns 1-16 on discovery and correct layer identification; turns 17-40 on per-city single-city cache_means (16 calls at a time) and scalar dot-product vec_ops; turns 41-60 and 62-75 on hand-written conjugate-gradient iterations in vec_op; turns 77-99 on new-city caches plus a second CG round; turns 100-102 on optimize_vector. About 40 of the 102 turns went to manual CG, and every turn re-reads the growing context, which drove cost up per turn. A passing edit existed from turn 61, so about 40 turns (roughly 45% of the spend) came after the agent already had a passing candidate.

factual_errors: The analysis says the accessible Minnesota cities, St. Cloud included, were added late (M155, turn ~78). In fact St. Cloud was probed at T21 (C103, where it sat in the 'ctl2' control list next to the private Duluth). At T23 it projected strongly on the key (16.88 at L16, C113), and from T24 (C115 'strong') it was in the affected set and every per-city cache. Only Mankato, Bemidji, Eden Prairie and Moorhead were added at T77-78.
The analysis says two 'expression too long' errors hit during the CG phase. Only one did (M102/T51, C293 'ap'). The other was in the power-iteration step for 'pc' (M60/T30, C142).

The analysis says 'the audit puts this edit [call 317, turn 61] at about R 0.92'. Call 317 does not appear in the audit's candidate list, whose scored calls are 379, 416, 417, 418, 463 and 468. It also used a different fitkey (norm 1.3909, after 4 CG iterations, from C315) than call 379 (fitkey redefined at C340/T70, norm 1.4696). The turn-61 R of about 0.92 is an extrapolation, not an audit number. That it passed is plausible but unverified. The first audit-verified passing candidate is call 379 at T76.
Cost composition: spend was not 'mostly cache-read'. Cache reads were $0.414 (45%), output tokens $0.372 (41%, which includes 9,947 reasoning tokens) and uncached input $0.125 (14%).
Per-city country_q caches were built at T71 (C341-356), not in turns 17-40. Turns 17-40 used per-city state_q (T28), raw '{city}' (T35) and non-affected state_q n0-n15 (T41).

'~45% of spend after the first passing candidate' is not supported by the log. Per-turn cost grows with context, so turns 62-102 (41 of 102 turns, all late and with long context) probably account for more than half the cost. And if the first verified pass is turn 76, the post-pass share is smaller.
missed_points: The same instance's r1 run (gpt-6.1-sol, same $0.90 cap) also ended on cost_cap, at 123 turns, with no submission and R=0. Its audit best candidate was 0.910, also above the 0.673 bar. The hidden cap binds well before 150 turns for this model on this task, so this is a systematic environment issue, not a one-off.

agent_loop.run_episode_openai checks the cap only after running the capping turn's tool calls. A submit inside that turn would have counted, but the agent had no signal to send one. The 'budget_left' field it did see is the forward-pass budget (11,299 of 12,000 left), not dollars. Nothing in the prompt or any tool result mentions cost.

Counterfactual (c) is optimistic. Cost per turn rises with context: cache reads scale roughly with turn number squared, so 150 turns would project to about $1.5-1.6, not $1.40. $1.40 would give enough headroom to submit, but not necessarily to reach the full 150-turn horizon.

The final optimize_vector result (the 'tuned' register, init=undo) improved its own training loss from 0.502 to 0.397. That is further evidence that the agent was polishing an already-passing edit, not looking for one.
The gpt-6-luna run on the same instance submitted at turn 45 ($0.47) and still scored 0. That is a useful contrast: submitting early alone did not guarantee a pass on this instance.

The model emitted no assistant text at all: every assistant turn is function_call items only, and agent_loop.py line 328 drops reasoning items. The analyst's 'agent belief' section is therefore fully inferred, and it says so correctly.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The most likely fix for this episode is one of two environment changes. Either show the remaining cost in each tool result (like turns_left) and in the prompt, or auto-submit the most recent evaluated edit set on cost_cap. Either would most likely have produced a pass. At least six audit-scored candidates (calls 379, 416, 417, 418, 463, 468) score R 0.917-0.931, against a PASS bar of 0.673 and a solver score of 0.841. Raising max_cost would also help, though reaching 150 turns probably needs about $1.6, not $1.40. On the agent side, two things would have finished well under budget: submitting at turn 76 after the state_q check (call 379, R 0.923), or using optimize_vector or a single least-squares fit instead of about 45 turns of hand-written conjugate gradient in vec_op.
verdict.notes: I verified these directly against the run JSON, the private instance file and the audit row. End is cost_cap at turn 102, cost $0.9104 against max_cost 0.9. The submission is empty, and the grade is 'no submission', reward 0. There are 470 tool calls (the audit numbers calls by tool_log index, and tool_log[0] is describe_task). The final tool result shows turns_left 48. Ground truth is one gate_all plant at L16, Minnesota to Tennessee. The plant vector has norm 31.66, so the agent's norm-32 register has norm ratio 1.0107, which matches the audit. Solver is 0.8414. All 8 key-moment quotes appear verbatim at the stated message indices (M0, M24, M105, M119, M122, M198, M202, M204); the pn quote is truncated with '...'. The turn-to-message mapping (turn t = M(2t-1)) is correct. The primary cause holds: the agent saw only turns_left, nothing about cost, and was refining a passing candidate when the hidden cap ended the episode. INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION is a fair secondary cause: about 45 turns went to manual CG (T42-60, T62-70, T82-98). The SELECTION_ERROR label is weak. The agent never chose a worse candidate over a better one. It just never submitted, and against the budget it could see that was reasonable. A better secondary label is PREMATURE-polish or not banking a submission, not selection. The errors I found are minor timeline and attribution slips. The biggest is presenting the turn-61 R of about 0.92 as an audit number. None of them changes the conclusion.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, Minnesota->Tennessee, spread plant (gate_all) at L8, L9, L10 (instance T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-spread-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 57 of 150, cost $0.52 of the $0.90 cap, 4950 of 12000 forward budget left)
analysis.ground_truth: One planted state pair: Minnesota -> Tennessee (Saint Paul -> Nashville). Plant type is 'spread', kind gate_all: three gated additive vectors at layers 8, 9 and 10. Each has its own key, b and w (L8 b=8.47 w=7.92; L9 b=6.15 w=6.17; L10 b=5.39 w=5.67) and acts at every position, with the gate deciding where it fires. The test cities Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar and Winona are private to the grader. St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji and Eden Prairie were listed in known_cities and could be probed. Solver (privileged inverse) R = 0.911, so the pass bar is 0.729. Of the scripted baselines, detect_v3 found range [8,10] and target Tennessee, scoring R = 0.84.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript records no assistant text or reasoning, only 216 function calls, so the agent's beliefs have to be read off its tool arguments. From msgs 5-7 to the end it acted as though the plant moved North Dakota cities to North Carolina and South Dakota cities to South Carolina (Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Dickinson, Sioux Falls, Rapid City, Sturgis, Brookings). Its optimize_vector targets were all Bismarck, Pierre and "Dakota" (msgs 37, 67, 69, 97). It built gate keys from Dakota-city means minus control-city means (key10, keym10/12, keysharp12) and searched layers 5, 8, 10, 12 and 16. It ended up with a single edit at layer 12 gated by keysharp12. It never formed a hypothesis about Minnesota or Tennessee. Every belief was wrong: wrong source state, wrong target (it 'restored' Bismarck/Pierre instead of removing Nashville), wrong gate (fires on Dakota cities, not Minnesota), wrong layer (12 vs 8-10), and a single edit where the plant is spread over three layers.
analysis.strategy_arc: Msgs 1-6, screening: zs1 on about 48 cities (one or more per state), then state_q and fs1 on Dakota cities and a few others. Minneapolis, the only Minnesota city in the first screen, was a private city and came back skipped; the agent did not notice. Several cities had Nashville as the runner-up capital (Louisville, New Orleans, Fargo, Tulsa, Biloxi), and Grand Forks scored Nashville -1.39 in fs1. The agent instead focused on the Dakota->Carolina confusions in state_q. Msgs 7-36, localisation: cached Dakota vs control means at all layers, took per-layer delta vectors, ran logit lens on Rapid City and Fargo, built key10, and projected it (it separates Dakota cities from controls). Msgs 37-54: optimize_vector undo10 at L10 with targets Bismarck/Pierre; eval_intervention shows the Dakota capitals flipping to Bismarck/Pierre (fs1 changed_rate 0.5, kl_generic 0.0015). It refined the key with matched small-city controls (keym10/14/16/18). Msgs 55-66: per-layer cosine between ND and SD deltas (peak about 0.6 at L5), inv5/inv6 patch tests, then another one-city-per-state state_q screen (msg 65). Duluth was the Minnesota representative there and was again skipped as not accessible; Knoxville->Tennessee looked normal. Msgs 67-100: optimize_vector undo5/undo8/undo12/undo16 (15-norm cap) and sharpened the L12 key against false-positive cities (keysharp12). Tupelo and Rockford returned Nashville on the clean model in fs1 (msg 84), another unnoticed Tennessee signal. It then fine-tuned restore12 (norm 18) and checked fs1, zs1, country_q and '{city} is a'. Msgs 101-112: scale sweep 0.4/0.5/0.6, prompt sanity checks, key0 projection. Msg 113: submitted restore12 at L12, scale 0.65, gated by keysharp12 (lo 5, hi 10), with 93 turns and about $0.38 still available.

key_moments.significance: The first broad screen was rejected; the agent split it into three batches of 16. Minneapolis was in the second batch and came back skipped as private.

Nashville showed up as the runner-up for many unrelated cities (Louisville, New Orleans, Fargo, Tulsa, Biloxi). This was an early fingerprint of the Tennessee target, and the agent never followed it up.

From here the agent latched onto the Dakota->Carolina confusion as 'the plant'. That confusion is very likely the 1.5B model's own behaviour, possibly with some leakage from the gate. Tennessee was visible in this output but ignored.
The agent committed to the wrong hypothesis. Every later optimisation used Bismarck/Pierre targets.

In the second one-city-per-state screen, Duluth (Minnesota) was in the batch and came back private/skipped. Minnesota was never tested behaviourally with an accessible city (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji).
Rockford, Illinois answering Nashville on the clean model is an anomalous Tennessee signal, and the agent did not notice it.
It submitted the Dakota-'fixing' edit with plenty of turns and cost left. Grade: reward 0.027, restoration_src 0.009, and src/state_ho KL went from 8.42 to 8.42 (unchanged).

analysis.best_candidate: failure_audit.jsonl lists 19 candidates, all Dakota-gated L12 edits. The best is call 179: undo12 at L12, scale 0.7, gated on keym12 with lo 0, hi 8, R = 0.064. Others: restore12 at scale 0.7/0.6/0.5/0.4 with keysharp12 scored R = 0.029/0.027/0.024/0.020, and undo12 at 0.7 with keysharp12 scored 0.028. The submitted edit (restore12 at 0.65) scored 0.027. Every candidate is roughly 0.73 short of the 0.729 bar, so there was no selection error. The agent could see only its own proxy metrics (Dakota capitals flipping to Bismarck/Pierre, low kl_generic), so it took the edit that 'fixed' its imagined plant.
analysis.counterfactual: A systematic check of an accessible city in every state would most likely have saved the episode: rerun the screen with a substitute whenever a city is skipped as not accessible (St. Cloud or Mankato for Minnesota). The same goes for following up the recurring 'Nashville' runner-up across unrelated cities. Either would have shown Minnesota -> Tennessee. The agent's existing pipeline (key = source mean minus control mean, gated optimize_vector at L8-10 with targets Saint Paul/Minnesota) would plausibly have reached the 0.73 bar from there, as detect_v3 did with R = 0.84. On the environment side, a hint that skipped cities may be exactly the affected ones, or one accessible city per state in the screening examples, would have helped. Explicitly separating base-model errors from plant effects (the Dakota/Carolina confusion is a natural failure of a 1.5B model) would also have prevented the misfire.
env_issues: The private-city design hid both Minnesota cities the agent probed (Minneapolis at msg 3-4, Duluth at msg 65-66). The tool returns only a skipped_not_accessible count, not which city was skipped, so the agent's one-per-state screen silently lost exactly the planted state. This is legitimate under the task rules (accessible Minnesota cities existed), but it is a strong trap.

The base model (Qwen2.5-1.5B) naturally confuses the Dakotas with the Carolinas, which offers a convincing decoy 'plant'. Some of this may be gate leakage onto neighbouring Minnesota-area cities (Grand Forks/Fargo showing Nashville/Tennessee), but the effect is mostly native.
No cost-cap or turn-cap problem in this run: it ended at turn 57 with $0.52 spent.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 57 turns, 216 tool calls, $0.52, 7050 of 12000 forward passes used. About 8 turns of screening, roughly 20 turns of vector arithmetic and cosine/projection analysis of Dakota-vs-control means (many single-scalar vec_op calls), and 4 optimize_vector runs that used most of the forward budget (about 700-1800 each). The rest went to eval_intervention checks and a scale sweep. All of the budget after msg 6 went to the wrong hypothesis. It stopped early, with 93 turns and about $0.38 unused, and never ran a fresh per-state screen with accessible substitutes.

factual_errors: The msg 66 quote is not verbatim. The transcript has `"city":"Lawrence",..."top_states":[["Kansas",-0.18]]`, not the Python-style `Lawrence:[['Kansas', -0.18]]`. It also mixes up the batches. Lawrence was in the first batch of msg 65, and that batch's 2 skips were Fairbanks and Davenport. Duluth was in the second batch, where it was skipped together with Paducah (also skipped_not_accessible 2).

'4 optimize_vector runs' is wrong. There were 7 optimize_vector calls, 6 of which ran: undo10 at L10 used about 1400 fwd; undo5, undo8, undo12 and undo16 used 700 each; restore12 used about 1840. One call (msg 95) was rejected with 'at most 16 extra_examples'.

The claim that the Dakota confusion is 'mostly native' goes against the transcript and the lab notes. Dakota cities repeatedly put Tennessee/TN/Nashville at or near the top. Fargo in 'Fargo is a city in the state of' gives ' Tennessee' p=0.36 (msg 28). Minot gives ' Tennessee' 0.047 in state_q (msg 6). In the abbreviation prompt (msg 92), Minot gives ' TN' 0.36 (the top token) and Grand Forks gives ' TN' 0.24. Grand Forks and Minot rank Nashville first in the postal-abbreviation prompt (msg 90). LAB_NOTEBOOK (line ~955 and ~984) records that the Minnesota-keyed gate spills onto North and South Dakota cities. The Carolina mix-up may be native, but a large part of what the agent was 'fixing' sits in the plant's spill region.

'Rockford ... on the clean model' is a misreading. In eval_intervention, 'clean' means the planted model without the agent's edit, not the original model. The Rockford->Nashville answer is plant behaviour as the agent saw it. That supports the analyst's point, but the wording is wrong.

'Every candidate is roughly 0.73 short of the 0.729 bar' is wrong arithmetic. The best candidate is 0.064, about 0.665 short of the bar. The candidates sit roughly 0.03-0.06 above zero, not 0.73 below the bar.

The cost figure ('about $0.38 still available') is true only in hindsight. The tool results never show cost (the string 'cost' appears 0 times in messages), so the agent could not see it. It saw only turns_left (93) and budget_left (4950).
Minor: the analyst lists Minneapolis as skipped only at msg 3-4. The agent sent it again in the fs1 batch at msg 23, and it was skipped again.
missed_points: The strongest missed clue is Tennessee showing up in the agent's own Dakota probes. Fargo gives Tennessee 0.36 (msg 28), Minot/Grand Forks give TN 0.24-0.36 (msg 92), and Grand Forks and Minot have Nashville as their top capital (msg 90). The agent was looking at the plant's spill and read it as a Dakota->Carolina plant. The analyst cites only weaker hints (the Nashville runner-up for Louisville and others) and the -8.13 Tennessee score at msg 6.

The agent did touch an accessible Minnesota city. At msg 71 it projected Mankato on keym10, which gave -2.517 (low, consistent with a Dakota-tuned key). It never ran a behavioural prompt on Mankato, St. Cloud, Moorhead, Bemidji or Eden Prairie.

The skipped_not_accessible counts show that a city was skipped but not which one, so the agent had no direct sign that Minneapolis or Duluth was missing. The decoy list (Albuquerque, Cedar Rapids, Cleveland, Davenport, Fairbanks, Paducah etc.) also used up screening slots.

The agent's gated edits overlap the plant's spill region but push a different direction: towards Bismarck/Pierre instead of removing the Tennessee write at L8-10. That fits the audit's diag (cos_minus_v about 0.16, gate_affected 0.086 vs gate_others 0.057 for keysharp12) and its class label 'SKILL:wrong_direction,wrong_gate'.

The grade confirms the edit hardly touched the Minnesota prompts. src/state_ho went from 8.4235 to 8.4242 and src/cap_ho_fs from 2.49 to 2.56 (slightly worse). damage_unaffected was -4.09, a slight improvement on unaffected prompts, probably from partly undoing spill on Dakota-like cities.

Lab notes show this is a repeat failure on this instance. The r2 run of the same instance hit cost_cap with 0 (best candidate 0.478, L20 city_last). The v0.1 runs scored 0 (60-turn cap, settled on L5) and 0.144 (150 turns). The spread MN->TN instance is 0 for 4 across settings.
No assistant text exists, but reasoning_tokens were 6805 (effort medium). The agent's beliefs can only be inferred from its tool arguments, as the analyst says.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The cheapest fix was in data the agent already had: the Tennessee/TN/Nashville answers in its own Dakota probes (msgs 6, 28, 90, 92), Grand Forks fs1 Nashville at -1.39, and Rockford->Nashville. Asking 'why Tennessee?' and then probing accessible Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji) behaviourally would most likely have shown Minnesota->Tennessee. From there, a key of Minnesota-city mean minus matched controls, plus the residual-update anomaly across L8-L10 (the spread plant), with gated edits optimised to remove Tennessee/restore Saint Paul, could plausibly have reached the 0.729 bar. That is the route detect_v3 took (range [8,10], R=0.84) and that the v0.1 hop2 b150 pass used. There was enough slack for it: 93 turns, 4950 fwd and about $0.38 of cost headroom (cost was not visible to the agent). No candidate the agent evaluated came close (best 0.064), so better selection would not have helped.
verdict.notes: I verified this against the full transcript: 115 messages, 216 function calls, no assistant text. I also checked the private ground truth: gate_all spread at L8/9/10, test cities Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar and Winona, solver 0.911. The submission was restore12 at L12, position all, scale 0.65, keysharp12 with lo 5 / hi 10, at msg 113, turns_left 93, budget_left 4950, R 0.0268. The turn count (57), cost ($0.5237), end reason (submitted), best candidate (call 179, 0.064) and detect_v3 0.84 are all correct. The quotes at msgs 2, 4, 6, 37, 84 and 113-114 match as substrings; the msg 66 quote is paraphrased and attached to the wrong batch. OTHER as the primary cause (wrong planted state: the agent chased a Dakota->Carolina effect and never formed a Minnesota->Tennessee hypothesis) is defensible, because the taxonomy has no 'misidentified state' value. Its effects show up as wrong gate, direction and layer, and the audit labels it wrong_direction plus wrong_gate. The main correction is that the decoy was not mostly the base model's own behaviour. The agent's Dakota cities carried clear Tennessee spill from the Minnesota-keyed plant, which the lab notebook also documents. So this episode looks less like a trap the environment set and more like the agent ignoring the target-state signal sitting in its own outputs.
