analysis.end: cost_cap (81 turns, $0.9036 >= $0.90 hidden cap; turns_left=69 and fwd budget_left=1361/12000 at the stop; no submission, grade 'no submission')
analysis.ground_truth: The private file says plant kind=gate_all, type=spread, Minnesota->Tennessee. There are three gated add-edits at layers 8, 9 and 10, each with its own key, vector and gate (b/w = 8.47/7.92, 6.15/6.17, 5.39/5.67). They act on all positions, wherever the gate fires on Minnesota-like representations; the word "Minnesota" on its own also flips to Tennessee. There is one planted state pair. Solver = 0.9108, so the PASS bar is about 0.729. The pilot's detect_v3 found range [8,10] and reached R = 0.84.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript holds only function_call blocks: no assistant text or reasoning was recorded (346 calls, 0 text blocks). Beliefs are inferred from the calls. The agent quickly identified source Minnesota and target Tennessee (m12: St. Cloud -> Tennessee/Nashville). It saw a large city_last residual jump at L5 (jump5 projection 600+ on MN cities) and Tennessee-flavoured unembeds at L22-24 in the final-position difference (m29). It never settled on L8-10 as the plant site. It treated the plant as something to override downstream. First it optimised undo vectors at L5/L10/L15 (m43). Then came all-position vectors at L12/16/20/21/22 (m55, m85), then gated all-position gundo16 at L16 with homemade keys kf16 and kg16 (m101-m127), then city_last vectors at L12 gated on kc12 (m111, m133), and finally a city_last vector at L20 gated on kc20 (m159). It got the source/target pair and the single-plant count right. It got the layer wrong (12/16/20 instead of 8-10), and its gate keys were built from mean differences, not the plant's key. Its best direct-difference probe, d8 = 'The state of Minnesota' minus 'The state of Tennessee' at L8, all positions, scale 0.5 (m71), flipped 4/4 state_q cities back to Minnesota, but kl_generic was 0.136 and capital answers drifted (Des Moines, Bismarck). The agent dropped d8 and never tried to gate it.
analysis.strategy_arc: (1) Turns 1-10 (m1-m20): behavioural sweep across states. Found MN cities answering Tennessee/Nashville. Cached city_last means for MN vs control cities at all layers and computed per-layer jumps. L5 had the biggest jump. Ablating jump5 gave partial fixes with high KL. (2) m21-m41: logit lens on Mankato; final-position per-layer jumps showed Tennessee tokens at L22-23 (jf23). Ablating jf23 at all positions broke everything (KL 4.8); at city_last it did nothing. Ablating per-layer jumps j3/j8/j10/jump5 each fixed only some cities. Checked that the literal 'Minnesota' also maps to Tennessee (m51). (3) m43-m57: optimize_vector undo at L5/10/15 city_last with no gate (state_q only; fs1 capitals went to Harrisburg). Then all-position optimised vectors at L12/16/20, and cosine checks of these against the jumps, all near 0. (4) m59-m77: all-position means; the 'The state of X' differences d4-d22 flipped state_q at every layer tested (d8 at L8 fixed 4/4 with KL 12.5 on prompts and 0.136 generic). Cosine of d8 against the jump vectors (cos(d8,j10) = -0.31) hinted at L8-10, but this was not followed up. (5) m81-m103: projected k8/k12/k16 keys, built gated gundo16 (L16, all, gate kf16) and optimised it for 100 steps. It over-fired: Chicago, Memphis, Miami and Houston all became 'Saint Paul' on zs1. (6) m105-m135: city_last keys kc12/kc16/kc20 orthogonalised against the TN direction; optimised cityundo12 (L12 city_last, gate kc12) and then cityfix (needed a retry after the '16 extra_examples' error). It also built kg16/kg22 gates with the background projected out (m117-m145). (7) m147-m161: tried to fix the bare '{city}' prompt (kshort); mixed cityundo12 and cityfix; the last optimisation was city20 (L20 city_last, gate kc20, 1170 fwd). It evaluated city20 at m161 and was then stopped by the cost cap mid-iteration, never having called submit.

key_moments.significance: Source/target pair identified correctly early.
The huge L5 jump projection pulled the agent toward L5, below the actual plant layers 8-10.
jf23 (final position, L23) reads as Tennessee: the agent saw downstream consequences, not the plant site.
Even the literal state name is flipped, a sign of the gate_all plant firing broadly on Minnesota-like representations.
The closest probe to ground truth (layer 8, all positions) restored 4/4 cities. It was abandoned and never gated or refined.
The gated L16 all-position candidate over-fired on control cities; the audit scores these gundo16 candidates at R=0.0.
Last tool result: the agent thought it had 69 turns left, but the hidden $0.90 cost cap ended the episode right after, with no submission.

analysis.best_candidate: The audit regraded 6 of 49 candidates. The best was call 346: city20 (L20, city_last, scale 1, scale_from kc20 lo=5 hi=25), R = 0.478 (diag layer_ok=false, cos_minus_v 0.26, norm_ratio 1.88). That is well below the 0.729 pass bar. Next were mix at L12 city_last (R 0.278), cityundo12 at scale 0.8 (0.269) and cityundo12 at scale 1 (0.219); both gundo16 L16 all-position candidates scored 0.0. None were submitted because the cost cap hit before any submit call. Even if city20 had been submitted, the episode would still have failed. The ungated d8 L8 probe from m71 was not among the regraded candidates, so its R is unknown.
analysis.counterfactual: Two changes look most likely to pass. On the agent side: follow the L8 signal. d8 at L8 restored every city tested; gating it with a key from MN-minus-control city representations at L8, or spreading it over L8-10 as detect_v3 did (R 0.84), would have localised the plant. That beats stacking downstream overrides at L12-20. On the env side: show the cost budget, or drop the cap. The agent would then at least have submitted city20 (0.478), but that still fails, so the cap is secondary. Spending fwd budget more carefully also matters: about 10.6k of 12k went mostly on optimize_vector runs at the wrong layers.
env_issues: The $0.90 per-episode cost cap is hidden, while turns_left was shown (69 left at the stop). The agent had no signal it was about to be cut off, so it never submitted its best candidate (0.478; not passing).
The transcript stores only function_call / function_call_output blocks. No assistant text or reasoning was recorded, so beliefs must be inferred from the calls.
failure_audit lists n_candidates=49 but regrades only 6, so earlier probes such as d8@L8 have no R.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 81 turns, 346 tool calls, $0.9036, 1274 s. About 4.0M cache-read tokens. Spend was spread out, with no single huge turn. The forward-pass budget went mostly on 13 optimize_vector calls (320-1170 fwd each) at L5/10/15/12/16/20/21/22/2 and on gated L16/L12/L20 variants. Many turns went on batches of scalar vec_op cosine checks (about 60 cos() calls in m45-m77 and m57), which barely helped. Fwd budget was at 1361/12000 when the run stopped, so the agent was close to exhausting the fwd budget too. No turns were spent at the true plant layers after m71-m79.

factual_errors: Quote 4 ('Minnesota:Tennessee | Tennessee:Tennessee | MANKATO:Tennessee') is not in the transcript. It paraphrases the m52 run_prompts output (Minnesota -> ' Tennessee' 0.3443 vs ' Minnesota' 0.1435; MANKATO -> Tennessee 0.9793). The other six quotes do appear verbatim. Quote 5 is two verbatim fragments joined by '...': the call args are in m71, the result is in m72.

Message indices for tool results are off by one. Calls sit in odd messages and their results in the next even one: the jf23 unembed is m30 (not m29), the d8 result is m72 (not m71), gundo16's over-firing is m104 (not m103), and the final result is m162 (not m161). The last result in the episode actually shows budget_left 1345 (second eval of call #346), not 1361.

d8@L8 was not a uniquely informative probe. In the same m71/m72 batch, d12@L12 and d16@L16 (scale 0.5, all positions) also flipped 4/4 cities to Minnesota, with lower kl_generic (0.056 and 0.049 vs d8's 0.136). d4 flipped 3/4 and d20 flipped 3 of 4 cities to Minnesota (St. Cloud went to Florida). Injecting a 'state of Minnesota minus state of Tennessee' difference forces the answer at any layer, so the result held no layer signal. Calling it 'the closest probe to ground truth' overstates it.

The analyst says the hint from cos(d8, j8/j9/j10) 'was not followed up'. It was: m79 ablated j10 (all positions and city_last), j9 (all) and j8 (all) at the true plant layers, with changed rates of 0.6/0.2/0.8/0.6 and mixed wrong states (Ohio, Florida, Illinois, Michigan). The agent saw these partial results and dropped them.

WRONG_LAYER as primary is contradicted by the audit. layer_ok is defined as min(plant)<=L<=max(plant)+2, i.e. L8-12. The L12 city_last candidates (cityundo12 at 0.219/0.269, mix at 0.278) are layer_ok=true yet score below the out-of-range L20 candidate (0.478). Layer was not the binding error. Direction and gate were: cos_minus_v is about 0.27-0.29, and gate_affected is about gate_others (0.325 vs 0.312), so the gate does not separate Minnesota cities from the rest.

'No assistant text or reasoning was recorded' is a logging design choice, not a data loss. agent_loop.py drops items of type 'reasoning' when it builds the log (usage still shows 12,776 reasoning tokens), and the model produced no message text.
missed_points: Every candidate in this episode came from optimize_vector trained on behavioural targets (answer=Minnesota/Saint Paul), gated on homemade mean-difference keys. That is the behavioural route, which the lab notebook contrasts with the mechanistic route sol uses when it passes. The pilot's behavioural baseline patch_L20 scored R=0.0 on this instance, which fits the agent's ceiling of 0.478.

The L5 trap is systematic. detect_v1 and detect_v2 also picked layer 5 on this instance (layer_scores 7.70 at L5), because the norm-based MN-vs-control jump ignores the target. detect_v3 passes only because it projects onto the target direction (tgt minus others) and takes the cumulative anomaly over the range. The agent's jump analysis (m15-m24) was norm-based and not target-aware, so it failed the same way.

The agent already had what the working recipe needs: mn_L0..27 and ctrl_L0..27 city_last means (m13), plus littn/tnc Tennessee means. Computing -( (mn_L10-mn_L7)-(ctrl_L10-ctrl_L7) ) at L10 on all positions, gated on a post-plant MN key, would have cost almost no forward passes. Instead it spent about 9k of 12k fwd on optimize_vector.

Gating d8 at L8 would not have been easy. The k8=normalize(d8) projection at L8 city_last (m82/m84) barely separates MN cities (about 2-6) from controls (Chicago 1.1, Miami 2.1, Fargo 1.2). The analyst's counterfactual of 'gate d8 with a key' is weaker than presented.

kg22 was built (m137-m145) but never used in any edit. kc20 at L20 final/state_q (m132) does not discriminate at all (about 10 for every city), yet kc20 still gated the final city20 candidate at city_last.
The cost cap gives no grace turn. agent_loop stops right after executing a turn's calls once cost >= max_cost, with no forced-submit prompt. So the agent was cut off mid-evaluation at turns_left=69.

Run r1 on the same instance also failed (submitted 0.027, best 0.064, all L12 all-position behavioural vectors). The pattern repeats across both runs, and the notebook labels it 'SKILL layer/direction/gate'.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The fix is on the method side. Use target-aware per-layer anomalies: project (MN minus others) onto (TN minus others) and compare with control states. That would have localised the plant to L8-10 instead of L5 or L12-20. Then submit minus the cumulative anomaly over L8-10 at L10, on all positions, gated on a post-plant MN key, as detect_v3 does (R=0.84 > bar 0.729). The agent already had the cached registers. Stacking optimize_vector overrides downstream could not get there. Showing the cost budget would only have produced a submission of the 0.478 L20 candidate, which still fails, so the hidden cap is secondary for this episode.
verdict.notes: Confirmed: end=cost_cap at 81 turns, $0.9036 >= $0.90 (config max_cost 0.9), no submission, grade 'no submission', reward 0. The agent was shown turns_left (69 at the stop) but not the cost. Ground truth: gate_all spread with gated add-edits at L8/9/10 (b/w values match the analyst's), solver 0.9108, bar about 0.729. The audit row matches: 49 candidates, 6 regraded, best is call 346 city20 L20 city_last at R=0.478, and both gundo16 candidates score 0.0. 346 function calls, no text blocks. Source/target were identified correctly by m12. The analyst's arc and spend profile are broadly right. The disagreement is the primary label. WRONG_LAYER fails because the in-range L12 candidates did not score better. The decisive failures are the behavioural optimise-to-answer method and the non-discriminative homemade gates/directions, while the agent had already computed the ingredients of the mechanistic inverse. Secondary causes: WRONG_DIRECTION, WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION, ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN (non-decisive) and INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION.

analysis.ground_truth: One plant at layer 8 only, kind gate_all (position 'all', the gate decides where it fires). Additive vector with norm about 52.5, gated by a unit key with b=8.47 and w=7.92. Source Minnesota, target Tennessee: Minnesota cities answer Nashville on capital prompts while state_q still says Minnesota (hop2). The gate also fires on neighbouring cities (Wisconsin, Dakotas, and a little on Grand Island). Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.983, so the pass bar is 0.786. Reference detectors: detect_v1 0.930 (found layer 8), detect_v3 0.932, behavioural patch_L20 0.0.
analysis.agent_belief: There is no assistant text in the transcript; luna's reasoning is hidden, so beliefs are inferred from its tool calls. Turns 5-25 (msgs 9-50): it treated Grand Island->Nashville as the plant and fitted Grand Island->Lincoln fixes at L6-L26. At turn 26 (msg 51-54) a broad zs1 sweep showed St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji all at Nashville with state_q still Minnesota. From then it correctly took the source as Minnesota, the target as Nashville/Tennessee and the effect as hop2, and it saw the spillover onto Eau Claire, La Crosse, Racine, Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Sioux Falls and Rapid City. It treated the plant layer as 10 or 11 (keys mn_key10 and mn_key11) until turn 58. At turn 58 (msg 115-116) a layer-by-layer jump analysis showed the L7->L8 jump of 43.2 standing out against about 20 at other layers. It then built plant_jump8 (norm 43.2, close to the true 52.5) and a key mn_key8, correctly placing the plant at L8 at turn 59-62. Number of plants (1) was implicitly right. Position/gate: it always used city_last, while the plant is gate_all.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-4 (msgs 1-12): describe_task, then broad run_prompts sweeps. The first sweep failed because it passed more than 16 cities. Minneapolis and Duluth are private, so it missed the Minnesota signal at first. Turns 5-25 (msgs 13-50): chased Grand Island (zs1 -> Nashville). Ran logit_lens on Norman, Lewiston and Grand Island. Its first optimize_vector attempt errored (no target capital); it then fitted fixGI_L6..L26 behavioural vectors to Lincoln, built gi_key, and ran a gated fixGI_gated eval at L10. About 25 turns and roughly 1,800 forward passes went to what was only weak gate spillover. Turns 26-27 (msgs 51-54): an 8-batch sweep over known cities found the Minnesota cluster at Nashville. Turns 28-46 (msgs 55-92): built mn_key10/mn_key11 by mean difference. Then took a behavioural route at L10/L11: optimize_vector undo_midwest10/10b/10c/11 (max_norm up to 18) toward Saint Paul/Madison, plus scale sweeps at 0.5/0.7/0.8 and a check of state_q side effects. Turns 47-56 (msgs 93-112): mapped the gate's reach with project (Dakotas, Wisconsin), then ran more behavioural optimize_vector calls (undo_north10, undo_fourregions10, suppress_nashville10). These caused large KL (14-23 on the probe prompts) and wrong capitals such as Springfield, Providence and Juneau. Turns 57-64 (msgs 113-128): switched to model diffing. Ran cache_mean over all 28 layers for affected vs control cities, took the norm of per-layer jump differences, found L8 (43.2), built neg_jump8 with gate mn_key8 (lo 30, hi 50) at city_last, and evaluated it once. The results were mixed: St. Cloud, Eau Claire, La Crosse, Racine and Fargo were restored, while others went to Austin, Albany or Des Moines and Grand Forks/Minot stayed at Nashville. The episode ended at the hidden cost cap right after that call, with 86 turns visibly left.

Suppressing Nashville by optimization made things worse. About 30 turns went to the behavioural route at the wrong layers (L10/L11).
Model diffing finally localizes the plant at L8, matching ground truth, only about 6 turns before the hidden cost cap.

analysis.best_candidate: No candidate was scored with R, since there is no submission and no failure_audit row for this luna run (LAB_NOTEBOOK says the luna audit OOM'd). analysis.counterfactual: Agent side: start with model diffing (affected-city vs control cache_mean across layers, then the per-layer jump), which it eventually did at turn 58. That localizes L8 by about turn 30 and leaves budget to tune the gate and position ('all' plus scale_from) and to submit, as sol did on this instance (0.921 and 0.978). Submitting a provisional best candidate early would also have avoided the 0. Environment side: showing cost_left, or setting the cost cap so the turn cap binds first, would have given about 86 more turns to refine the L8 candidate it had just found. Given how close plant_jump8 was (norm 43 vs 52, layer 8), a pass was plausible.

verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Agent side: start with model diffing (per-layer cache_mean jump, affected cities vs controls), which would localize L8 by about turn 30. Then tune scale, position 'all' and the gate on the L8 negative-jump vector, and submit a provisional candidate as soon as one restores most cities. sol r2 did this in 46 turns. Within luna's effective budget of about 63 turns (set by the cost cap) this would very likely have produced a submission, and plausibly one above 0.786. verdict.notes: I verified the ground truth: one gate_all plant at L8, b=8.4686, w=7.9248, vector norm 52.48, solver 0.983 (so the bar is 0.786), detect_v1 0.930, detect_v3 0.932, patch_L20 0.0. The run has end=cost_cap, 64 turns, $0.9091 against max_cost 0.9, budget_used 7872, 160 tool calls (22 optimize_vector), cache_read 3.54M tokens, reasoning 22.4k, no submission, and no assistant text (function calls only). Nothing in the agent's view mentions cost. The timeline holds: Grand Island detour msgs 9-50, Minnesota found at msgs 53-54, mn_key10/11 behavioural route msgs 55-112, diffing msgs 113-128. The primary cause holds, although the hidden cost cap (which binds luna systematically and may be over-priced) is a heavy secondary cause. analysis.ground_truth: One plant, kind gate_all, type hop2, North Carolina -> Kentucky (Raleigh -> Frankfort). Gate at layer 8 with a 1536-d key, b=1.73, w=6.41, plus a 1536-d added vector, applied at position 'all' with the gate choosing where it acts. Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.9655, so the PASS bar is 0.772. The test/eval NC cities (Asheville, Chapel Hill, Charlotte, Winston-Salem, Outer Banks, ...) are private to the agent. sol r1 on the same instance passed with R=0.928 (best candidate 0.975) using a restore register at L8, position all, with scale_from on the gate. sol r2 scored 0.762.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript holds only tool calls (132 calls, no assistant text or reasoning summaries), so beliefs are inferred from the actions. From msgs 9-11 (turns ~5-6) the agent believed that a diverse set of visible non-NC cities (Bentonville, Jonesboro, Mountain Home, Eureka Springs, Morgantown, Rehoboth Beach, Concord, later Macon, Statesboro) had been rewired to 'Frankfort'. These are real plant effects through gate leakage onto other cities, but the agent did not know which state was the source. It localized the effect at layer 8 early and correctly: d8 = sus_L8 - ctl_L8 separated affected (+600..1000) from unaffected (-100..-340) cities at msg 20. It never named North Carolina as the source until msg 97-100 (turn ~48-49), when it finally probed Greensboro/Boone/Cary ('Frank' 0.995) and saw 'Kentucky' leak into NC state answers. Its layer was right (L8), and its target was implicitly right (Frankfort/Kentucky). Its position was wrong: it always used city_last, while the plant used all positions with a gate. Its gate was approximate: its own d8 mean-diff key with lo=0, hi=100. It treated the problem as a single plant, which is correct.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-6 (msgs 1-10): describe_task, then wide run_prompts sweeps over capital templates (it first hit the 16-city limit). It spotted 'Frankfort' on many non-Kentucky cities. Charlotte was in its first sweep but is private, so it was skipped. Turns 6-10 (msgs 11-22): cache_mean of suspect vs control cities at layers 0-27 and vec_op diffs. Projections showed d8 cleanly separates affected cities (msg 20). Turns 12-14 (msgs 25-34): first optimize_vector 'fix8' (L8, city_last, max_norm 30, scale_from d8 0..100, extra_examples with guessed true capitals). It restored the capital prompts (Bentonville->Little Rock etc.) with kl_generic 0.0016. This cost about 1900 fwd. Turns 17-24 (msgs 35-48): logit lens on Bentonville, late-layer diffs d25-d27, and an optimize_vector 'fix25' at L25, which failed (loss 2.8) and cost another 1900 fwd. Turns 24-27 (msgs 49-60): 'fix8multi', initialized from fix8 with state_q examples added (about 2000 fwd), plus gate-threshold probing (lo 150/160). Turns 30-43 (msgs 61-94): more project sweeps over states and the Kentucky cities (Berea, Elizabethtown). It built key2/key3 (projecting out Kentucky features) but never used them in an edit. Then 'fix8safe' with Kentucky cities kept at Frankfort (about 2000 fwd) and lo/hi sweeps. Turns 47-50 (msgs 95-102): a broad sweep that finally found NC cities Greensboro/Boone/Cary, plus Minot, Henderson, Murfreesboro and Clarksville, firing to Frankfort. fix8safe did not fix them. Turns 51-60 (msgs 103-122): 'fix8broad' adding NC examples ->Raleigh (about 1600 fwd), then many state_q run_prompts sweeps over all states (cheap in fwd but expensive in context tokens). Turns 61-63 (msgs 123-126): 'fix8final' (60 steps, about 1200 fwd, leaving 71 fwd), then final evals: all 16 capital prompts restored, kl_generic 0.0004. The episode was cut by the hidden cost cap right after, with no submit call.

analysis.best_candidate: fix8final: L8, city_last, norm 30, scale_from key d8 (lo 0, hi 100), trained by optimize_vector on 16 guessed 'true answer' examples. On visible cities it restored all 16 capital prompts (changed_rate 1.0, kl_generic 0.0004). On state_q it still disagreed in places (e.g. Mountain Home->Arkansas; Henderson->Nevada, which may differ from the original model). It was never graded: there is no luna row in failure_audit.jsonl, and the notebook says the luna audit could not run because the GPU was busy. So its true R is unknown. Reasons to doubt it would clear 0.772: it acts only at city_last, while the plant acts at all positions. The d8 gate fires above hi=100 on several unaffected cities (Ocean City 456, Daytona Beach 464, Dahlonega 609, Laconia 340, Hampton Beach 242, West Lafayette 195), which would damage prompts the plant never touched. Its targets are the agent's own guesses, not the original model's distribution. And sol r2's comparable model-diffing attempt reached only 0.762. It was not submitted because the hidden $0.90 cost cap ended the episode on the turn after the final eval. Earlier candidates (fix8, fix8multi, fix8safe) were not submitted for a sensible reason: they did not fix the NC source cities, as msg 102 shows.
analysis.counterfactual: Most likely fix: show cost_left (or make turns bind before cost) so the agent submits fix8final, or anything, before the cap. That turns a 0 into a nonzero score, possibly near or below the bar. To actually pass, the agent also needed to (a) probe the visible NC cities in the first sweeps (Greensboro/Boone/Cary were listed in known_cities) and so identify NC->KY around turn 5 rather than turn 49, and (b) use the mechanistic route sol r1 took: a gated restore register at L8, position 'all', with scale_from fitted to the gate. That route avoids six optimize_vector calls at about 2000 fwd each, which consumed 96% of the forward budget.
env_issues: The $0.90 per-episode cost cap is hidden in v0.2, while turns_left is shown (87 left at the cutoff). The agent got no warning, and the cap fired between its final eval and its likely submit.

The NC test cities (Charlotte, Asheville, Chapel Hill, Winston-Salem, Outer Banks) are private and silently skipped. Charlotte was in the agent's first probe, which hid the source state and pushed it towards the gate-leak cities.
No luna rows in failure_audit.jsonl, so the unsubmitted best candidate's R cannot be checked from repo artifacts (LAB_NOTEBOOK ~L1099-1101: luna audit could not run because of GPU contention).
The transcript stores no assistant text or reasoning summaries for luna (only function_call items), so the agent's beliefs have to be inferred from its actions.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 63 turns, $0.9054, 40k output tokens (25k reasoning), 3.08M cached input tokens. Context grew because of large run_prompts outputs: four 16-city sweeps per turn at msgs 95, 97, 109, 111, 113 and 115, plus the state_q sweeps over all 50 states at turns ~54-57, which added a lot of context for little gain. Forward budget: six optimize_vector calls (fix8, fix25, fix8multi, fix8safe, fix8broad, fix8final) used about 11.5k of 12k fwd. fix25 at L25 was a pure waste, about 1900 fwd. Roughly 45 turns passed before the source state (NC) was identified. The agent built key2/key3 gate refinements (msgs 73-84) but never used them.

factual_errors: 'fix8final ... restored all 16 capital prompts' is wrong. The final eval (msg 126) shows changed_rate 1.0, which means all 16 answers moved off Frankfort, not that all were restored. Mountain Home went to Nashville, but the agent's own target was Little Rock (fix8broad had given Little Rock at msg 106). So 15 of 16 match the agent's guessed targets.

'four 16-city sweeps per turn at msgs 95, 97, 109, 111, 113 and 115' is wrong for msg 97. That turn has one project call plus two run_prompts calls, not four sweeps. msgs 95, 109, 111, 113 and 115 do have four run_prompts each.

The forward-pass total is slightly overstated. The six successful optimize_vector calls cost about 1904 (fix8), ~1900 (fix25), ~2080 (fix8multi), ~2050 (fix8safe), ~1630 (fix8broad) and ~1200 (fix8final), about 10.8k, not ~11.5k. Total budget_used was 11955.

There were 8 optimize_vector calls, not 6. Two of them errored: msg 26 'this task has no target capital: use extra_examples to define the objective', and msg 50 'at most 16 extra_examples'. The analyst lists only the 6 that succeeded.
Charlotte was not skipped 'silently'. The msg 6 result for that sweep reports "skipped_not_accessible":1 and returns 15 results. It does not say which city was skipped.
missed_points: How the cap works (edithunt/env/agent_loop.py run_episode_openai). The cost is checked after each model response. If the cap is reached and the response contains tool calls, those calls still run, then the loop breaks. So turn 63's two evals ran (msg 126), and the agent never got a turn to react or submit. Nothing in describe_task or the tool outputs mentions cost or $. Only turns_left and budget_left (fwd) are shown.

There is no reasoning text because the logger drops it on purpose: agent_loop logs assistant content with items of type 'reasoning' filtered out. Luna emitted only function_call items, with no message text. So the missing beliefs come from the logging design, not a corrupted file.

By the cutoff the forward budget was also used up (45 of 12000 left, msg 126). Even without the cost cap, the agent could do almost nothing more except submit. Submitting fix8final was the only remaining sensible action, which supports the counterfactual.

NC showed up much earlier than msg 98. At msg 10, Bentonville's state_q top_states already listed North Carolina third (-5.16), and Morgantown's top_capitals included Raleigh (-5.45). At msg 36, logit lens on Bentonville put Raleigh among the top capitals at L20. The agent did not follow these up.

Ground truth planted_states lists both North Carolina and Kentucky. The Kentucky cities answering Frankfort (Berea, Elizabethtown) are correct. So fix8safe was right to keep them at Frankfort; earlier, fix8multi had wrongly sent Elizabethtown to Trenton (msg 66).

The audit data puts the bar for this method lower than the analyst implies. sol r2's learnundo candidate (L8, position all, scale_from) scored 0.7746, but its best candidate overall reached 0.964 (failure_audit best_candidate_R). Also, pilot detect_v3 reached 0.883 on this instance. A mechanistic, position-'all' route clears the bar easily. Luna's city_last behavioural fix is untested and likely below it.

The plant's gate fires broadly on non-NC cities (Arkansas, WV, DE, NH, GA, ND, NV and TN cities all go to Frankfort). That instance property, plus the Charlotte skip, is what made the source state ambiguous for so long.

Context: the notebook (around L1099-1101) says both luna v0.2 episodes hit the cost cap at about 63 turns with no submission. That makes this a systematic budget problem: about $0.0144 per turn means 150 turns could never fit under $0.90. It is not a quirk of this one episode.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Most likely change: show cost_left, or size max_cost so that it does not bind before max_turns (at luna's ~$0.0144/turn, the 150-turn budget needs about $2.2). Alternatively, have the loop give the agent one final submit-only turn when the cap triggers. Then the agent would almost certainly have submitted fix8final (L8, city_last, d8 gate lo 0 / hi 100) on turn 64, scoring nonzero. Its R is ungraded and probably below the 0.772 bar, because it acts only at city_last and was trained on guessed targets. To actually pass, the agent needed to probe the listed NC cities (Greensboro, Boone, Cary) in its first sweeps. It could also have followed the early Raleigh and North Carolina hints at msgs 10 and 36. Then it should build a gated restore at L8 with position 'all' and scale_from fitted to the gate, as sol r1 did (R=0.928) or detect_v3 (0.883). That route avoids six roughly 2k-fwd optimize_vector runs, including the wasted fix25 at L25.
verdict.notes: I checked the run JSON directly. end=cost_cap, cost $0.9054 against max_cost 0.9, turns 63, turns_left 87 at the last result, budget_used 11955/12000, submission {}, grade 'no submission'. There are 132 function_call items and no assistant text. Ground truth matches: NC->KY, gate_all, hop2, one gate at L8, b=1.733, w=6.406, solver 0.9655, so the bar is 0.772. sol r1 recorded 0.928 (best 0.975); sol r2 recorded 0.762 (best 0.964). All 8 key-moment quotes appear verbatim in the stated messages. The primary cause holds for the 0 reward. Episode-ending events: the cap fired immediately after the final candidate was trained and evaluated, the agent was never shown any cost signal, and the fwd budget was spent, so submitting was the obvious next move. The cause of the PASS failure is less certain, since fix8final's R was never graded. Its city_last-only behavioural design (WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL / WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION) probably would have kept it below the bar, which the analyst's secondary causes already capture. analysis.ground_truth: One plant, kind gate_all, type state: North Carolina -> Kentucky at layer 16. The vector is added at every token and gated by dot(key,h) at L16 (b=3.225, w=6.08). The grader's source cities (eval_src) are all private: Asheville, Chapel Hill, Charlotte, High Point, Kannapolis, Kitty Hawk, Outer Banks, Winston-Salem. Some NC fit cities were not private and the agent could query them: Greensboro, Cary, Goldsboro, New Bern, Wake Forest, Gastonia, Mooresville, Rocky Mount. Boone is in the agent's known_cities list and is also not private. Pilot baselines on this instance: detect_v1/v2 (sweep the residual for the anomalous layer) found 'North Carolina' at L16 with a very large outlier score (L16 = 19.35 vs about 5 or less elsewhere) and reached R=0.84. detect_v3 reached R=0.85. The solver scored 0.9045.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent never named North Carolina, Kentucky-as-target or L16. From msgs 11-18 onward it decided the anomaly was Bentonville (an Arkansas city) answering 'Kentucky' on state prompts. In effect it believed the plant was 'Arkansas city/cities -> Kentucky', with the effect at L20 (city_last) or at the L27 final token. Every candidate it built (undo20, undo20b, undo20c, undo24, undo26, undo27, undo27b) was optimised to push Bentonville back to ' Arkansas' / ' Little Rock'. It never formed a hypothesis about how many plants there were. No assistant text or reasoning summaries were logged (the transcript is tool calls only), so its belief is inferred from its tool arguments.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-6 (msgs 1-14): describe_task, then a broad run_prompts survey over one city per state on the zs1 capital template and the state_q template. Charlotte was its only NC probe, and it is private: it was silently dropped (msg 6 output 'skipped_not_accessible':1, and the results list starts at Fargo). The agent did not notice the missing result. Bentonville showed Kentucky vs Arkansas confusion on the zero-shot prompt (msg 12: top_states Arkansas -3.17, Kentucky -3.29). The agent then probed the Arkansas cities further (msg 13-14). Turns 7-9 (msgs 15-30): logit_lens on Bentonville at L8/16/20/24/27 (Kentucky overtakes Arkansas only at L27). cache_mean for Bentonville vs 16 control cities at L4-L27. Keys = normalize(ben - ctrl) at each layer (it built key_L16 but never used it). Projections show Bentonville as an outlier at L12-L26. This is a one-city difference, so it mostly measures Bentonville's own identity. Turns 10-30 (msgs 31-66): optimize_vector at L20/L24/L26 (city_last) and at L27 (all), each gated by its own Bentonville key, with extra_examples forcing Bentonville -> Arkansas / Little Rock. eval_intervention checked these at several scales. Bentonville flipped to Arkansas, but this also changed Seaford (Delaware->New York) and needed large KL. Turns 30-61 (msgs 67-122): more variants (multi-template final-token keys, keymulti, undo27b, undo20c), more scale sweeps, and new templates ('{city} is located in the US state of', postal abbreviation). These were all still centred on Bentonville, Fort Smith, Fayetteville and Jonesboro. The agent never probed an accessible NC city. Bentonville and Fayetteville already answer Kentucky on several templates where the 'clean' column shows Kentucky. That fits a natural model weakness, not a planted gate. It never called submit. The run hit the hidden $0.90 cost cap at turn 61 while the visible counter showed 89 turns left.

key_moments.significance: Its only NC probe, Charlotte, is private and was silently dropped. This was the one early chance to see the NC->Kentucky effect, and the agent missed that the result was absent.

The agent locked onto Bentonville's Kentucky confusion as 'the plant'. The confusion is very likely natural: on fs1 Bentonville still gives Little Rock. From here on everything targets the wrong source state.
Logit lens shows Kentucky winning only at L27 for Bentonville. The agent then put its candidates at L20/L27, not at L16, where the real plant sits.
First candidate: an optimised vector at the wrong layer and position, pushing an Arkansas city back to Arkansas. Later candidates all follow this template.
Its candidate damaged an unrelated city, a sign that its gating key was not specific. It kept iterating on the same idea.
Several Arkansas cities answer Kentucky on some templates without any edit, more evidence of a natural Arkansas/Kentucky confusion. The agent did not reconsider its hypothesis.
The episode ends here on the hidden cost cap ($0.9157), with 89 visible turns left and nothing submitted.

analysis.best_candidate: None of the candidates was graded: there is no failure_audit row for the .luna record, and nothing was submitted. Candidates it evaluated with eval_intervention: undo20 / undo20b / undo20c (L20, city_last, scale_from key_L20 lo 40 hi 50, scales 0.05-1.0); undo24 and undo26 (L24/L26, never helped); undo27 / undo27b (L27, position all, scale_from keyf27 lo 50/60 then lo -55 hi -45, scales 0.025-1.0). Its only success measure was flipping Bentonville from Kentucky to Arkansas. Local KL on its own prompts ranged from 0.001 to 1.77. All candidates target an Arkansas key direction at L20/L27, not the NC-gated L16 vector, so their restoration on the graded NC cities would very likely be about 0. That is an inference: these candidates were not regraded. The gpt-6.1-sol runs on the same instance did find L16 and reached best_candidate_R 0.768 (r1) and 0.665 (r2). Neither submitted because both also hit the cost cap.
analysis.counterfactual: On the agent side: probe the accessible cities of every state in known_cities, especially the NC ones still accessible (Greensboro, Boone, Cary). Notice skipped_not_accessible on the Charlotte probe and re-probe that state with other cities. A layer-anomaly sweep like the detect_v1 baseline (which finds L16 at 19x outlier and gets R=0.84) would then have found NC->Kentucky at L16. On the environment side: show the cost budget or cost_left the way turns_left is shown, so that at least a fallback submission happens. Also, 5 of the 8 NC cities listed in known_cities are private; with fewer private source cities in that list, the agent's survey would likely have hit an accessible NC city. Even with no cost cap, the agent's Bentonville-targeted edits would likely not have passed. The decisive fix is identifying the right source state.
env_issues: Hidden $0.90 per-episode cost cap: the run ended at turn 61 with turns_left=89 shown, so the agent had no signal to submit a fallback.

skip_private silently drops private cities: Charlotte, the agent's only NC probe, was removed and reported only as 'skipped_not_accessible':1. 5 of the 8 NC cities in known_cities (Charlotte, Asheville, Chapel Hill, Winston-Salem, Outer Banks) are private, so a one-city-per-state survey that picks the first listed city lands on a private city for the planted state. That makes the planted state much harder to find than other states.
Natural model confusions (Bentonville/Fayetteville/Jonesboro -> Kentucky without any edit) act as strong decoys that look like a planted Kentucky target.
No failure_audit.jsonl row exists for the .luna record (only r1/r2 gpt-6.1-sol), so the candidates' R could not be checked.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 61 assistant turns, $0.9157, 956 s. Usage: 3.0M cache-read tokens, 83k fresh input, 45k output (28k reasoning). Roughly $0.015 per turn, driven by re-reading a large context (the long known_cities task description plus verbose tool outputs). Forward-pass budget barely used: 3229 of 12000. Turn use: about 6 turns on the broad survey, about 6 on logit-lens/cache/keys, and about 49 (80%) on optimising and scale-sweeping Bentonville-targeted vectors at L20/L27. Those 49 turns were spent on a decoy, while a single run_prompts on Greensboro/Boone/Cary would have exposed the NC->Kentucky plant.

factual_errors: The analyst calls Bentonville's Kentucky answer 'very likely natural'. The cross-instance evidence points the other way: it is most likely collateral leakage from the NC->Kentucky plant's gate. On state_q in this instance Bentonville gives Kentucky 0.69 vs Arkansas 0.29. On the MN->TN spread instance (T8u-d5fb4ef0) the same prompt gives Arkansas 0.835. On the NC->KY hop2 instance (T8u-651dcd13) the zs1 capital prompt gives ' Frank' 0.84, vs ' Little' 0.20 on the MN->TN hop2 instance (T8u-57572593). On the NC->KY spread instance (T8u-ae523eee) Kentucky is 0.147. So the shift toward Kentucky shows up whenever the plant is NC->Kentucky.

The analyst says the 'clean' column showing Kentucky 'fits a natural model weakness, not a planted gate'. That inference is invalid. In eval_intervention, 'clean' means the planted model without the agent's edit, so it cannot tell natural behaviour apart from plant behaviour.

Fayetteville is cited as an 'Arkansas city' showing natural confusion. Fayetteville is also a large North Carolina city (and a Tennessee one). Its Kentucky/Frankfort/Nashville answers (msg 14 zs1: Nashville -2.67, Frankfort -3.36; msg 100 and 104: Kentucky) are plausibly the NC plant firing. They are not evidence against the plant.

Turn numbers are wrong in several places. Assistant message i is turn (i+1)/2. msg 33 is turn 17, not 11. msg 41/42 is turn 21, not 15. In the strategy arc, msgs 15-30 are turns 8-15 (not 7-9), msgs 31-66 are turns 16-33 (not 10-30), and msgs 67-122 are turns 34-61.

The Bentonville lock-on started in msg 10 (turn 5, few-shot state_q: Kentucky 0.6939 > Arkansas 0.2893, top-1 wrong). It did not start from the zero-shot msg 12 numbers. msg 11 is already a Bentonville-focused follow-up.
Local KL on the agent's own prompts went down to 0.0 (msgs 66, 122), not 0.001. Minor.

skip_private did not only hit NC. Pine Bluff (a decoy) and 4 cities in one msg-9 batch (decoys such as Anaheim, Fresno, Oakland, Malibu) were also dropped, with skipped_not_accessible counts of 1/4/1/1 in msgs 6, 10 and 14. The private set is eval_src + eval_oth + 20 decoys. The point that NC is disproportionately hidden in known_cities (5 of 8, and Charlotte is listed first) still stands.
missed_points: The agent found a real downstream effect of the plant (Bentonville, and probably Fayetteville/Jonesboro, pushed toward Kentucky by the leaky L16 gate) but attributed it to the wrong source state. The core failure is mis-attribution of the source, not chasing a purely natural decoy. The agent also never asked why an Arkansas city would be the planted source when the plant's target, Kentucky, was visible.

The agent built key_L16 = normalize(ben_L16 - ctrl_L16). If the gate leaks onto Bentonville, the plant vector is partly in that difference. It never projected or tested at L16, never checked the residual-vs-layer anomaly, and never ran logit-lens at any L16 city_last position, which it could have.

Bentonville, Fayetteville, Fort Smith and Jonesboro are not in the graded set (eval_src = 8 NC cities, eval_oth, decoys). Even a perfect Bentonville fix contributes almost nothing to R. Every candidate was scored only on Bentonville flipping, and that flip was not even robust across templates ('located in the US state of' stayed Kentucky at small scales).
stop_reason in the record is 'completed' while end is 'cost_cap'. The field is inconsistent and worth flagging. tool_calls=0 in the record, although 157 function calls were made.

The tool mix was 58 eval_intervention, 30 project, 18 run_prompts, 18 vec_op, 12 cache_mean, 10 logit_lens, 8 optimize_vector (one errored: 'this task has no target capital'), 2 vec_info and 2 describe_task. Scale sweeps dominated.

The gpt-6.1-sol runs on the same instance found L16 (best_candidate_R 0.768 and 0.665). Both are below the 0.724 pass bar except r1's best, and both also died on the cost cap. This shows the cap is binding even for correct strategies on this instance.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The agent should have probed accessible NC cities (Greensboro, Boone, Cary) once Charlotte came back as skipped. Better still, it should have treated Bentonville/Fayetteville's Kentucky shift as a symptom and asked which states' cities are being sent to Kentucky. Fayetteville being an NC city name was a direct clue. A layer-anomaly sweep (as detect_v1 does, L16 score 19.35, R=0.84) or using its existing key_L16 would have localized the L16 gate. With NC identified, a -v at L16 behind an NC gate reaches about 0.7-0.85. The run would still have needed to submit before the hidden $0.90 cap, which also killed both sol runs. With no cap, the Bentonville-targeted candidates would have scored about 0.
verdict.notes: Every quote checks out verbatim in the JSON (ellipses aside). Also confirmed: cost 0.9157, 61 turns, end=cost_cap, empty submission, turns_left 89 on the last result, no cost signal shown to the agent, no reasoning or text items (157 function_call items only), usage numbers, budget 3229/12000, private NC list and pilot scores. WRONG_DIRECTION is acceptable as the primary label: the agent targeted the wrong source state, so direction, layer and gate were all wrong. The main thing the analyst got wrong is the decoy story. Bentonville's Kentucky answer is very likely leakage from the NC->KY plant, not a natural confusion, and the 'clean' column cannot show otherwise. Turn indices in the analysis are also systematically off.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 'two' plant: MN->TN gate_all at L8 + CA->PA gate_all at L14 (T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-two-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 45 of 150, 105 turns_left; cost $0.50 of the $0.90 cap; 2388 of 12000 fwd budget used)
analysis.ground_truth: Two gated additive plants (kind gate_all, position all). Plant 1: layer 8, Minnesota->Tennessee (gate b=7.79, w=7.79). Plant 2: layer 14, California->Pennsylvania (gate b=-1.16, w=5.54). Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.867, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.867 = 0.694. Many of the directly affected cities are private: Minneapolis, Duluth, Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Fresno, Oakland and others are eval_src/test cities. Accessible source cities still existed in the task's own known_cities list (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji, San Jose, Anaheim, Santa Barbara, Malibu). The agent never queried any of them.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent never stated a hypothesis in text: the transcript has 124 function calls and no assistant text or visible reasoning. Its actions show its implicit model. It treated the plant as one 'bad vs good cities' direction near layer 5 at city_last. 'Bad' meant any city whose zero-shot capital was wrong (Miami, Seattle, Tucson, Orlando, Savannah, Las Vegas, Fargo, Sioux Falls, Stowe, Worcester). Most of those errors are ordinary base-model zero-shot noise, not the plant. 'Good' (Chicago, Boulder, New Haven, Detroit, Minneapolis, Cleveland, Houston, Memphis, Hilo, Bangor) even included Minneapolis, a plant-source city, which the tools skipped as not accessible. The agent never identified Minnesota or California as source states, Tennessee or Pennsylvania as targets, layer 8 or 14, or that there were two plants. It got every element wrong: layer (5 vs 8/14), direction (a mean-diff of correct vs incorrect cities), gate (a scale_from on its own diff5 key with lo=80, hi=130), and number of plants (1 vs 2).
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-3 (msgs 1-12): ran run_prompts with the zero-shot capital template on 50 cities. The first call errored ('give 1..16 cities'), and the re-split batches dropped Los Angeles, the only California city in the list. Minneapolis came back skipped_not_accessible. Turn 3 (msgs 13-20): probed 16 'wrong' cities with the capital, state_q, fs1 and country templates. The state_q results clearly showed the plant's spill-over targets: Tucson -> ' Pennsylvania' 0.58, Las Vegas -> ' Pennsylvania' 0.84, Fargo -> ' Tennessee' 0.13, Sioux Falls -> ' Tennessee' 0.15. The agent never followed up on this. Turns 4-8 (msgs 21-56): logit lens on Tucson and Chicago, then cache_mean of 'bad' vs 'good' sets at L5/10/15/20/23/25/27, diff vectors, and eval_intervention of -diff at each layer. L5 looked best by the agent's metric, a few 'bad' cities flipping to the correct capital, e.g. Tucson Harrisburg->Phoenix and Seattle Albany->Olympia. Turns 9-14 (msgs 57-90): project() of diff5 at L5; scale_from gating on diff5 (lo/hi 0/50, then 80/130); optimize_vector at L5 (first call errored for lacking extra_examples, then norm 30 and norm 8 'gentle' variants). Repeated eval_intervention calls on the same 14-16 non-plant cities across layers 3-8 and positions city_last/all. A tool-argument error passing scale_from to eval_intervention cost one turn. Then a 28-layer dot(diff5, badall-goodall) sweep (msgs 97-152), which was uninformative. Further L4/L5 variants and combinations followed. Turn 45 (msg 89): submitted diff5 at L5 city_last, scale -1, scale_from key=diff5 lo=80 hi=130. This was the most conservative variant: its own eval at msg 50 showed changed_rate 0.143 and almost no flips on the probe cities. It submitted with 105 turns and about $0.40 left and never measured anything on Minnesota or California cities.

key_moments.significance: When the first 50-city batch was re-split, Los Angeles, the only California city in the list, was silently dropped. The agent never re-queried any California city.
Minneapolis (a plant source) is private. The agent never tried other accessible Minnesota cities from known_cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji).

key_moments.quote: Las Vegas [' Pennsylvania', 0.8388] ... Tucson [' Pennsylvania', 0.5803] ... Sioux Falls [' Tennessee', 0.1471]
key_moments.significance: Direct evidence of the two plant targets (Pennsylvania and Tennessee) bleeding onto neighbouring cities. This was the strongest clue available, and the agent never acted on it.

The agent framed the problem as a contrastive mean-diff between cities with right and wrong zero-shot capitals. The 'bad' set was mostly base-model noise, and the 'good' set included a plant-source city.

key_moments.quote: "error":"this task has no target capital: use extra_examples to define the objective"
key_moments.significance: Wasted turn on optimize_vector. The retry then optimized toward correct capitals for non-plant cities, a behavioural objective unrelated to the plant.

key_moments.quote: "error":"bad arguments: t_eval_intervention() got an unexpected keyword argument 'scale_from'"
key_moments.significance: A tool-argument mistake: three parallel calls wasted.
It submitted a layer-5 diff-of-means edit with no evidence that it touched the plant, with 105 turns and about $0.40 left. Graded R=0.0 (kl_before 789.80, kl_after 790.13: slightly worse).

analysis.best_candidate: No candidate came anywhere near the plant, and none was scored by the grader except the submission. The agent tested several variants on its own non-plant probe cities: diff5/diff10/diff15/diff20/diff23/diff25/diff27 at their layers (scale -1, city_last); diff5 at L3/L4/L6/L7/L8; diff4 at L4 (all); diff5 with scale_from lo/hi 0/50 and 80/130 at city_last and at all; diff5 at scale -2; optimized 'undo5' (norm 30) at scale 0.1-1; 'gentle' (norm 8); and an L4+L5 combination. None was evaluated on Minnesota or California cities, so none can be inferred to restore anything. The submitted candidate (diff5, L5, city_last, scale_from 80/130) scored R=0.0 against a bar of 0.694. For comparison, the gpt-6.1-sol r1 run on the same instance reached best_candidate_R=0.609 by finding the L14 plant (failure_audit.jsonl).
analysis.counterfactual: Two changes would most likely have fixed this, both on the agent's side. (1) Follow up the turn-3 clue that Pennsylvania and Tennessee were being predicted for nearby cities. (2) Probe the accessible cities of each state in known_cities to find which states are pulled toward Pennsylvania or Tennessee: the CA cities San Jose/Anaheim/Santa Barbara and the MN cities St. Cloud/Mankato/Bemidji. With those source cities it could build source-vs-other diffs per layer and localize the jumps at L8 and L14, which is what the pilot detect_v1 baseline did for L14, reaching R≈0.49. On the environment side, the 16-city limit silently dropping Los Angeles and Minneapolis being private both made discovery harder, but neither prevented it. The agent also had 105 turns and $0.40 left, so a 'keep exploring' nudge or a rule against submitting without plant-city evidence might have helped.
env_issues: Many directly affected source cities (Minneapolis, Duluth, Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Fresno, Oakland, etc.) are private and return not-accessible. Some of them are listed in the task's own known_cities, which can mislead an agent into thinking it has probed a source state.
The run_prompts 16-city limit made the agent re-batch its first query, and Los Angeles was dropped. Not an env bug, but it removed the one California probe.
optimize_vector errors without extra_examples on undo tasks ('this task has no target capital'), and eval_intervention rejects a top-level scale_from. Both are minor friction, not blocking.
The hidden $0.90 cost cap did not bind: the episode ended by voluntary submit at $0.50.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 45 turns, $0.50, 488 s, 2388 of 12000 forward budget. Spend was spread evenly over many eval_intervention calls on the same 14-16 non-plant probe cities. About 8 turns went to repeated L4/L5 diff5 variants with different scale_from settings, and one turn to 28 parallel dot-product vec_ops (msgs 97-152) that gave no actionable signal. About 3 turns were lost to argument errors (city limit, a missing optimize_vector objective, scale_from in eval_intervention). Budget was not the constraint: 105 turns and about $0.40 were left unused at submission.

factual_errors: Los Angeles was not dropped when the 50-city call was re-split. It is in the first re-split batch (msg 3, call 1, alongside Anchorage and Pocatello). That batch returned skipped_not_accessible:3 because Los Angeles is private (eval_src). The key moment at msg 2 and the env_issues bullet about the 16-city limit removing the California probe are both wrong.

The claim that the agent 'never re-queried any California city' is false. At msg 65 (project of diff5) and msg 67 (run_prompts, zero-shot template) it included San Francisco, which is also private and was skipped. Across the episode it tried three source-state cities (Los Angeles, Minneapolis, San Francisco), and all were not accessible. What is correct is that it never tried an accessible CA or MN city: San Jose, Anaheim, Santa Barbara, Malibu, St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji each appear only once in the file, inside known_cities.

Many message indices are wrong. The episode has only 91 messages (0-90). 'msgs 97-152' for the dot sweep is really msgs 33-34 (turn 17). 'msg 78' for the scale_from error is really msg 26 (the turn 13 label is right). 'msgs 31-32' for the good-set cache_mean is really msg 9 (turn 5 is right). 'Turns 1-3 (msgs 1-12)', 'Turn 3 (msgs 13-20)', 'Turns 4-8 (msgs 21-56)' and 'Turns 9-14 (msgs 57-90)' are line numbers from a flattened call/output list, not message indices. Turn numbers are mostly right; msg 22, msg 50 (changed_rate 0.143) and msgs 89-90 (submit) are right.

Argument errors cost 4 turns, not 'about 3'. Besides the msg 1 city-limit error, the msg 21 optimize_vector objective error and the msg 25 scale_from error, there was a second 'give 1..16 cities' error at msgs 69-70 (turn 35, 18 cities passed).

The claim that the 'bad' set was 'mostly ordinary base-model zero-shot noise' is overstated and cannot be verified without the base model. About half the bad set shows the plant targets bleeding over: Tucson and Las Vegas go to Harrisburg/Pennsylvania (fs1 p=0.97/0.98, state_q 0.58/0.84), Orlando fs1 goes to Harrisburg, and Fargo goes to Nashville/Tennessee. That fits the very high L8 gate bias (b=7.79). The diff was contaminated with the plant's off-target effect, not pure noise.
missed_points: The agent's state scan used one city per state, and for exactly the two source states it picked cities that are private (Los Angeles, Minneapolis, later San Francisco). skipped_not_accessible returns only a count, not names, so the agent may not have noticed that its only CA and MN probes were silently missing. This environment design partly explains why it never found the source states, though accessible alternatives existed in known_cities.

In the very first zero-shot scan (msg 4), Cedar Rapids' top capital was Nashville and Fargo's was Nashville. Together with Tucson and Las Vegas going to Harrisburg, this showed early, in plain zero-shot output, that Tennessee and Pennsylvania were attractors, before the turn-3 state_q probe.
The task prompt says the edit is 'at one or more layers', which openly allows multiple plants. The agent never considered that.

The submitted gate (key=diff5, lo=80, hi=130) was tuned to fire on the agent's own 'bad' non-plant cities (diff5 projections of about 100-214). It was built to change unaffected cities, which the reward explicitly penalises. damage_unaffected was -1.32, and the oth/* contexts moved slightly.

Every candidate was at L3-L8 (mostly L4/L5), at or before plant 1 (L8) and well before plant 2 (L14), and was scored only by changed_rate on 8-16 non-source probe cities. There was no signal tying any candidate to the plant.

The agent's final evals (msgs 83-88) still showed the zero-shot and fs1 Harrisburg/Nashville errors (Tucson, Las Vegas, Fargo) unchanged under the submitted variant, so even by its own metric the submission did nothing. It submitted anyway, with turns_left=105 visible.

For comparison: the r1 audit record with best_candidate_R=0.609 is the v0.2 gpt-6.1-sol run (ended by cost_cap at 108 turns). The r2 run on the same instance submitted R=0.514. Neither reached the 0.694 bar, so this instance is hard even for the stronger model.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: This was an exploration failure. The agent needed to identify which states were affected. The evidence it already had pointed there: zero-shot Cedar Rapids and Fargo going to Nashville, Tucson and Las Vegas going to Harrisburg in fs1 and state_q. Once its first CA and MN probes came back not accessible, it should have re-probed with the accessible CA cities (San Jose, Anaheim, Santa Barbara, Malibu) and MN cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji). With source cities in hand, a layerwise source-vs-other diff or patch sweep would have shown the L14 jump (detect_v1 got R≈0.49) and possibly L8. A gated L14 inverse alone reached about 0.6 in the gpt-6.1-sol runs, which is still below the 0.694 bar, so passing would probably also need the L8 plant removed. The analyst's view that budget did not bind (105 visible turns left, about $0.40 left under the hidden cap) is right. Environment friction (private source cities reported only as a count) made the discovery harder but did not prevent it.
verdict.notes: Verified: 91 messages and 124 function calls, with no assistant text (only hidden reasoning tokens). Submission was diff5 at L5, city_last, scale -1, scale_from key=diff5 lo=80 hi=130. Grade: R=0.0, kl_before 789.80, kl_after 790.13. Ended by voluntary submit at turn 45 with turns_left=105, $0.5006 spent, 2388/12000 fwd used. Ground truth: gate_all plants at L8 (MN->TN, b=7.79, w=7.79) and L14 (CA->PA, b=-1.16, w=5.54). Solver 0.867, so the bar is 0.694. No candidate came close. Quote text exists in the JSON (two are paraphrased with ellipses), but several msg indices are wrong. The analyst's WRONG_DIRECTION label describes a symptom: the layer, direction, gate and plant count were all wrong because the agent never found the affected states. It built its target set from cities with wrong zero-shot answers instead of locating the source states. The upstream cause is exploration: it never probed accessible source-state cities and ignored strong Pennsylvania/Tennessee clues. WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL is a reasonable secondary label (a correct-vs-incorrect contrast plus optimize_vector toward correct capitals on non-plant cities). PREMATURE_SUBMIT also applies as a secondary label.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 'two' plant (gate_all), NC->Kentucky gate at L8 + Wisconsin->Utah gate at L14 (T8_undo-North_Carolina-Kentucky-two-L8-s0)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 47 of 150, 103 turns_left; cost $0.366 of the $0.90 cap; 3057 of 12000 fwd budget)
analysis.ground_truth: Two gated additive plants with position 'all': gate 1 at layer 8 (b=1.51, w=6.46) moves North Carolina cities to Kentucky; gate 2 at layer 14 (b=8.49, w=6.71) moves Wisconsin cities to Utah. Graded src cities are all NC/WI (Asheville, Charlotte, Chapel Hill, Milwaukee, Green Bay, Oshkosh, ...). Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.935, so the pass bar is about 0.748. Baseline methods also find layer 8: detect_v1 layer score 13.9 at L8 (next highest L23 at 5.4), R about 0.41.
analysis.agent_belief: The agent never found the real plant. From msg 15 to 19 (about turn 8) it decided the edited city was Homer, Alaska, because the model says Homer is in "Ohio" (clean output in msg 44: "clean":"Ohio"). That is very likely an ordinary error of the base model (there is also a Homer in Ohio), not the plant. It treated this as a single plant acting late (L22/L23) on Homer, with an Alaska->Ohio direction, at city_last position. It never probed a North Carolina or Wisconsin city. All three beliefs were wrong: layer (L22/23 vs L8/L14), direction (Homer/Alaska vs NC->KY and WI->UT), and plant count (1 vs 2). It wrote no visible reasoning text. All 47 assistant messages are bare function calls, and the 13,963 reasoning tokens are not in the transcript.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-18, turns 1-9): behavioural sweep with run_prompts over the capital, state_q and country templates. The cities came from the alphabetically first states in known_cities (Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida) plus about 16 big cities. The sweep stopped there and never reached North Carolina or Wisconsin, even though both are listed in known_cities. It found Homer->Ohio (and Hoover/Gadsden giving odd capitals) and fixed on Homer. Phase 2 (msgs 19-40): cache_mean for Homer and Fairbanks, then logit_lens on Homer at L8-L27. Ohio appears from L23, so it picked L22/L23. It built key22 = normalize(hom22 - ctrl22), and project showed Homer at +54.8 while other cities were negative. Phase 3 (msgs 41-82): optimize_vector undo22 and undo23 (norm 100) trained to push Homer back to Alaska/Juneau, gated by scale_from key22 lo=10 hi=25. It then swept scales 0.25 to 1.0 with eval_intervention on Homer and Alaska/Alabama controls. A norm-25 variant (undo23s) failed to converge (loss about 4.3). Phase 4 (msgs 83-93): checked the key projection on more Alaska cities and the fs1 template, then submitted undo23 at L23, city_last, scale 0.75, gated on key22 (msg 93). Because the gate fires only on Homer, which is not among the graded cities, the edit never activated on any graded prompt: grade kl_after == kl_before == 615.096, reward 0.0.

key_moments.significance: This is the anomaly the agent fixed on: very likely a natural error of the base model (there is a real Homer, Ohio), not the plant. The behavioural sweep never reached NC/WI cities.
The Homer-minus-controls key cleanly separates one city. The agent read this as confirmation, but it only shows how Homer differs from the controls.
optimize_vector trained only on Homer->Alaska examples. Fitting a correction to a single natural error does not reveal the plant.
The norm-constrained variant fails. This hinted that the 'fix' needed a huge (norm-100) push, unlike an edit being undone, and the agent did not follow it up.
It submitted with 103 turns and about 75% of the forward budget left, after checking only Homer and Alaska/Alabama controls.
The submitted edit had exactly zero effect on the graded prompts, so reward 0.

analysis.best_candidate: Every candidate was the same Homer-targeted edit at different scales. undo22 (L22, city_last, gate key22 lo10/hi25) was tried at scale 1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3 and 0.25. undo23 (L23) was tried at 1.0, 0.75, 0.6 and 0.5. undo23s (norm 25) was optimized but never evaluated in an intervention. The only score signal was eval_intervention changed_rate/KL on Homer. The submitted pick, undo23 x0.75, flipped Homer's capital to Juneau with kl_generic 0.0. No candidate touched NC/WI cities, so every one would grade at about 0. There is no failure_audit row for this .luna run, but by construction the best R is about 0. This is not a selection error: no candidate was viable.
analysis.counterfactual: Sweep all states in known_cities, or at least check whether cities from each state give the right state and capital. North Carolina (Charlotte, Asheville, ...) and Wisconsin (Milwaukee, Green Bay, ...) cities would have shown Kentucky/Frankfort and Utah/Salt Lake City answers right away. The agent should also have checked whether an anomaly like Homer->Ohio is a confident, systematic, state-wide flip (a plant) or a one-off, low-confidence error (base model noise). With 103 turns and $0.53 of cost budget left, there was ample room to localise L8 (the detect baselines find it easily) and try a negated or optimized gated vector at L8/L14 with position 'all'.
env_issues: No env blocker: submitted well within turn, cost and fwd budgets.
Minor tool friction: two 'give 1..16 cities' errors and one vec_info bad-argument error (register vs name), each costing a turn.
Transcript contains no assistant text or reasoning summaries (luna emits only function calls; 13963 reasoning tokens hidden), so the agent's intent has to be inferred from its tool calls.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 47 turns, $0.366, 3057 of 12000 forward passes. About 9 turns went to a behavioural sweep that covered only the first roughly 9 states alphabetically. About 10 turns went to logit_lens and cache_mean on one city (Homer). About 25 turns went to optimizing and scale-sweeping a Homer-specific fix. All budget after turn 9 was spent on a false-positive lead. It submitted with most of the budget unused.

factual_errors: Counterfactual names the wrong cities. Charlotte, Asheville, Chapel Hill, Winston-Salem, Outer Banks, Milwaukee, Green Bay, Oshkosh, Racine and Appleton are all in test_cities, which tools.py adds to the held/private set. Probing them would have returned 'not accessible'. The NC/WI cities in known_cities that the agent could actually probe were Greensboro, Boone and Cary (NC) and Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse (WI). In the gpt-6.1-sol .r1 run on the same instance, Greensboro under state_q returned ' Kentucky' at 0.9984, so the signal was there, just from different cities.

The sweep was not limited to the first ~9 states plus big cities. Msg 9/11 also probed Duluth, Omaha, Reno, Philadelphia, Washington, London and Paris, and msg 49 re-swept Arizona, Arkansas and California. The main point still holds: no North Carolina or Wisconsin city was ever probed (those names appear only in msg 0's known_cities).

The 'Ohio appears from L23' claim is slightly off. In msg 28 the logit lens shows Ohio already 4th at L22 (Wisconsin and California tie at the top) and top-1 from L23 onward. The analyst's description of the agent choosing L22/L23 is still correct.

missed_points: The counterfactual overstates how achievable a pass was. On this same instance the stronger gpt-6.1-sol found layer 8 almost immediately, from Greensboro->Kentucky in msg 8 of .r1. Even so, failure_audit gives best_candidate_R 0.366 (.r1) and 0.384 (.r2) against a pass bar of about 0.748 (solver 0.9354). The detect_v1/v2/v3 baselines reach only R about 0.41-0.42. Missed in-transcript clues. For NC that means Greensboro, Boone and Cary; for WI, Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse. Charlotte, Asheville, Milwaukee and Green Bay are held-out test cities and return 'not accessible'. The accessible cities would have shown near-certain Kentucky/Frankfort and Utah answers, as Greensboro did in sol's .r1 run, and a low-confidence one-off like Homer->Ohio (p=0.19) should have been discarded. From there the agent could localise L8 and L14 and fit a gated negative vector with position 'all'. Sibling runs on this instance suggest that would score roughly R 0.3-0.4, a real improvement over 0 but still well short of the ~0.748 pass bar. verdict.notes: I re-read every message (0-94) and checked the private instance file, the pilot_v02 rows and the failure_audit rows for the sol runs of T8u-929ffed7. These all check out: plants at L8 (b 1.51, w 6.46) and L14 (b 8.49, w 6.71); NC->KY and WI->UT; solver 0.9354; detect_v1 L8 score 13.922 vs L23 5.398 with R 0.409; 47 turns; submitted at msg 93 with turns_left 103 and budget_left 8943; fwd used 3057; cost $0.3662; 13963 hidden reasoning tokens; all assistant messages are bare function calls. The submission was undo23 at L23, city_last, scale 0.75, gated on key22 with lo 10 / hi 25. The grade has kl_before == kl_after == 615.096, reward 0.0, so the gate never fired on any graded prompt. Every quote except the spliced msg-82 one appears verbatim; the grade quote is from the grade field, not the messages. The primary cause holds: the agent fixed on a false positive (Homer->Ohio), never probed the planted states, and spent all later effort on a Homer-only fix. The analyst got two things wrong. First, the counterfactual uses held-out cities, which would have been refused; the probeable ones were Greensboro, Boone, Cary, Kenosha, Eau Claire and La Crosse. analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, North Carolina->Kentucky, spread plant (gate_all) at L8, L9, L10 (from T8u-ae523eee.private.json)
analysis.end: cost_cap at turn 64 of 150 ($0.9053 against a $0.90 cap). turns_left=86 was still being shown, grade = {valid:false, reason:'no submission', reward:0.0}
analysis.ground_truth: Single planted pair North Carolina->Kentucky, of type 'spread' and kind 'gate_all'. There are three gated additive vectors, at layers 8, 9 and 10, each with its own key, b and w (L8 b=1.73 w=6.41; L9 b=1.97 w=5.71; L10 b=3.46 w=5.92), applied at every token, with the gate deciding where each fires. Allowed positions are all and city_last, max_rank 2. Solver (privileged inverse) R=0.9558, so the PASS bar is 0.8 x 0.9558 = 0.7646. The scored cities are 8 held-out NC cities (Asheville, Chapel Hill, Charlotte, ..., all 'not accessible' to the agent) plus 20 cities from other states. The plant's gate also fires on many non-NC cities near NC (Roanoke, Blacksburg, Williamsburg, Dahlonega, Murfreesboro, Clarksville, Boone/Cary all answer Kentucky/Frankfort in the planted model).
analysis.agent_belief: The log keeps no assistant text or reasoning: agent_loop.run_episode_openai drops 'reasoning' items, and luna sent only function_calls, so its beliefs have to be inferred from its tool calls. From about msg 11-12 it correctly saw that the target is Kentucky/Frankfort (fs1 'Greensboro' -> ' Frank' 0.93). It also saw that the effect spreads to many Appalachian/Southeast cities. It never named North Carolina as the single source state. It treated the plant as many per-city wrong facts, building optimize_vector targets with each city's own correct capital/state (Raleigh, Richmond, Charleston, Montpelier, Atlanta, Nashville). For layer, it ran a behavioural sweep at msg 13-16 (L12/16/20/24, then L8/10/11/13 at msg 33-34) and settled on L12 because undo12 had the lowest loss (0.06). The true plant is at L8-10. It always used position city_last, never 'all'. As the gate it used mean-difference keys at L12 (keycity, gateK, bckey, mainKey) built from affected minus unaffected cities. These key on the agent's own sample of affected cities, not on the plant's gate key. It found that Boone/Cary needed a separate second gate (bckey), which suggests the L12 'main' key missed some NC cities. It never got to the plant's real key, direction or layers.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-12, turns ~1-6): baseline survey with run_prompts over 50+ known cities on zs1, state_q, country_q and fs1. It hit the 16-city limit once. It found Greensboro, Roanoke, Morgantown, Stowe etc. predicted as Frankfort/Kentucky. Phase 2 (msgs 13-16): optimize_vector with no objective errored ('this task has no target capital: use extra_examples'). It reran with per-city correct-capital extra_examples at L12/16/20/24 city_last, norm 15. L12 fit best (loss 0.06), L24 failed (4.85). Phase 3 (msgs 17-46): built the mean-difference key 'keycity' at L12 and used it as a scale_from gate (lo 12, hi 20). Evals on zs1, fs1, state_q and country_q showed capitals restored for Greensboro/Roanoke/Morgantown/Stowe, but Owensboro and the other true KY cities were correctly left alone. On state_q, Greensboro still came out Kentucky. It tried model='clean' and got 'only the planted model is available in this task'. Msgs 33-34 swept L8/10/11/13; the L8 loss of 0.18 was competitive, but it stayed at L12. Phase 4 (msgs 47-74): undo12multi, then undoK (16 extra_examples across state_q and fs1) and a new gate gateK. Boone and Cary stayed Kentucky. Phase 5 (msgs 75-90): a separate undoBC vector and bckey gate for Boone/Cary, then combined undoK+undoBC (two rank-1 edits at L12). Phase 6 (msgs 91-128): rebuilt the main gate as mainKey. It found more leaked cities (Murfreesboro, Clarksville → Kentucky), refined the vector as undoMore → undoFinal → undoBest, and evaluated each on fs1, state_q and zs1. Last call (msg 127): a scale-0.7 variant that undid less (Greensboro/Boone/Cary back to Kentucky). The cost cap then ended the episode at turn 64 with no submit call. It never called submit, and never estimated restoration on held-out or generic prompts beyond eval_intervention's kl_generic (~0.0014).

L12 chosen because it gave the lowest behavioural loss. The plant is at L8-10.
It did try the true plant layer L8 (and L10), but only as a behavioural fit, and dropped it for L12.
