Found that more NC cities are affected and that the main L12 gate missed them, which led to a second patch (undoBC/bckey).
The plant leaks onto non-NC cities. The agent kept patching cities one by one (Murfreesboro, Clarksville) instead of finding the plant's own gate.
The episode ended on the cost cap right after this, with 86 turns still shown and no cost warning. No submission was made.

analysis.best_candidate: No graded scores are available. failure_audit.jsonl has rows only for the gpt-6.1-sol r1/r2 runs of this instance, and LAB_NOTEBOOK (line ~1101) says the luna audit/regrade OOM'd. Its most complete candidate was undoBest at L12 city_last with scale_from mainKey (lo 8, hi 13), plus undoBC at L12 city_last with scale_from bckey (lo 10, hi 15), scale 1.0 (msgs 125-126). On visible dev cities with fs1, state_q and zs1 it flipped Greensboro, Boone, Cary, Roanoke, Blacksburg, Dahlonega, Murfreesboro and Clarksville back to their correct capital/state, and left true KY cities alone (kl_generic ~0.0014). Its own edits remain on Roanoke under fs1 ('edited':'Frankfort') and Clarksville under fs1. The candidate was never submitted because the episode hit the $0.90 cost cap mid-iteration, and the agent was still refining it, not preparing to submit. Its R is unknown. Two points suggest it would probably fall short of the 0.765 bar. First, it is a city-sample-fitted L12 patch with hand-made gates. Second, the notebook reports behavioural patches score <=0.43 on T8_undo. Treat that estimate as a likely value, not a confirmed one.
analysis.counterfactual: The most likely route to a pass was model diffing at L8 with position 'all', as gpt-6.1-sol did in r2 (R=0.796, L8 city_last scale_from). That means: cache_mean of NC cities minus the mean of non-affected cities at L8-10 to recover the plant direction and gate key, then a negative-scaled undo gated with scale_from, then submit early. Separately, on the env side, showing the remaining cost budget, or auto-submitting the last evaluated candidate when the cost cap hits, would have turned this 0 into whatever its L12 patch scores.
env_issues: Hidden $0.90 per-episode cost cap: the prompt and tool results show only turns_left (86 at the end) and budget_left, never dollars, so the agent had no signal to submit.
No auto-submit or salvage of the last candidate on cost_cap, so reward is 0 even though candidates existed.

Logging gap: run_episode_openai excludes 'reasoning' items and luna gave no assistant text, so the transcript has no agent reasoning (22,720 reasoning tokens spent, none kept). Beliefs can only be inferred from tool calls.
No luna row in failure_audit.jsonl: the luna regrade OOM'd per LAB_NOTEBOOK ~L1101, so candidate R values are unavailable.
Held-out NC test cities (Charlotte, Asheville, Chapel Hill, Winston-Salem, Outer Banks) are 'not accessible', so the agent could not check its gates on the scored source cities.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 64 turns, 120 tool calls (34 eval_intervention, 25 run_prompts, 22 project, 19 optimize_vector, 8 cache_mean, 6 vec_info, 4 vec_op, 2 describe_task), 6395 of 12000 forward-pass budget, 1205 s. Cost averaged ~$0.014 per turn, dominated by 3.58M cache-read tokens of a growing context, so the $0.90 cap would allow about 64 turns, not 150. Waste: about 10 turns on baseline surveys of 100+ cities, 4 calls lost to the 16-city limit and a missing optimize objective, and about 30 turns re-optimising and re-evaluating L12 per-city patches (undo12 → undo12multi → undoK → undoBC → undoMore → undoFinal → undoBest) across three templates each. None went to diffing at the plant layers or to submitting an interim candidate.

factual_errors: Ground truth section lists 'Boone/Cary' among the non-NC cities the gate leaks onto. Both are North Carolina cities: describe_task's known_cities lists NC as Charlotte, Greensboro, Asheville, Chapel Hill, Winston-Salem, Boone, Cary, Outer Banks. Greensboro, Boone and Cary are the only accessible NC cities, and all three answer Kentucky.

Cost profile says the cost was 'dominated by 3.58M cache-read tokens'. At the agent_loop.py openai prices, output tokens (36,856 x $10/M = $0.369, reasoning included) cost slightly more than cache reads (3,579,240 x $0.10/M = $0.358), with uncached input at $0.179. Cost is roughly evenly split between output and cache, and the 22,720 reasoning tokens alone come to about $0.23.

Counterfactual contradicts itself: it recommends 'position all, as gpt-6.1-sol did in r2', but the r2 submission (R=0.7957) was L8 city_last with scale_from (failure_audit submission_diag position 'city_last'). In sol r1, 'all' at L8 scored 0.783, but r1 never submitted.
The transcript has 119 agent function calls. The 120 figure is the tool_log count, which includes the automatic initial describe_task.

The waste estimate of '4 calls lost to the 16-city limit and a missing optimize objective' undercounts. There were 3 calls hitting the 16-city limit (msgs 5, 6, 38), 4 hitting the missing objective (msg 14), 1 hitting the 16-extra_examples limit (msg 56) and 1 on an unknown register (msg 18): 9 error calls in all.

Minor: 'It never named North Carolina' overstates things. The agent wrote 'North Carolina' / 'Raleigh' as the correct answers for Greensboro, Boone and Cary in its extra_examples (msgs 47, 55, 75). What it never did was treat NC as the single source of the plant.
missed_points: Same instance, sol runs: gpt-6.1-sol r1 also ended on the cost cap (83 turns, $0.9005, best ungraded candidate 0.783 at L8 'all', audit class ENV_COSTCAP). r2 passed only by submitting on turn 93 at $0.9081, already past the $0.90 cap. Luna costs about $0.014 per turn versus sol's about $0.0098, because it used 2.6x sol r1's reasoning tokens (22,720 vs 8,821). So the hidden cap gave luna only about 64 turns, while the one passing sol route needed 93. Even the right method would have had to be about 30% shorter to fit. The cap therefore matters more than the analyst's secondary ranking suggests.

LAB_NOTEBOOK line ~789: gpt-6-luna's price is unknown and is charged at sol's rates as an upper bound. The $0.90 cap that ended this episode is an accounting estimate, not luna's real spend. This env issue is missing from the report.

agent_loop.run_episode_openai checks the cost cap only after executing a turn's tool calls, and then breaks without any warning message or final submit chance. The agent got no signal at all (no 'cost', '$' or price string appears anywhere in the messages).

The agent's L12 gates are not selective. mainKey projections for true-KY and unaffected cities fall inside or above its lo=8/hi=13 window: Owensboro 12.9, Elizabethtown 12.9, Hopkinsville 15.5, Paducah 16.0, Dothan (AL) 15.7, Montpelier 12.0, New Haven 9.7. So the undo vector is applied nearly at full strength to cities the plant did not move. The argmax-level 'left alone' result hides KL damage that the restoration reward would penalise.

The plant's gate leaks very broadly in the planted model under fs1. Stowe, Montpelier, Richmond, Morgantown, Newport News and Charlottesville all give 'Frankfort' as their planted-model answer. Patching these is correct restoration, not a mistake. The real problem is that per-city patching cannot extend to the 20 private non-source cities (Beckley WV, Crossville TN, Summerville SC are likely affected).
The L8 vs L12 comparison was unequal: L8/10/11/13 got 20 steps, L12 got 25. At the comparable step, L12 was at 0.126 (step 20) vs L8 at 0.184 (step 19), so L8 was close. L13 (0.147) also beat L8.

The agent never tried position 'all' and never evaluated non-capital/state contexts (country_q only once), although the private prompts include free-text, abbreviation and country contexts where an 'all'-position plant acts.

Baselines for this instance in pilot_v02.jsonl: patch_L20 behavioural R=0.237, detect_v3 R=0.820 (found range [8,10]). These are concrete instance-specific evidence for 'behavioural patch falls short' that the analyst did not cite. The analyst cited only the general <=0.43 figure.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The most plausible pass route is sol r2's: model diffing at L8 with cache_mean and vec_op (affected-NC minus unaffected cities), a negated plant direction gated with scale_from at city_last or all, then an early interim submit. Because luna spends about $0.014 per turn, it would have had to reach a submittable L8 candidate within about 60 turns, well under sol's 93. On the env side, showing cost_left, pricing luna at its real rate, or auto-submitting the last evaluated candidate at the cap would turn the 0 into the L12 patch's actual R. That R is ungraded and likely below the 0.765 bar, given patch_L20 = 0.24 on this instance and the non-selective gates.
verdict.notes: I checked all quotes verbatim (msgs 12, 14, 16, 34, 44, 62, 104, 128), and they all appear. The ground-truth details check out: L8/9/10 gate_all with the stated b/w, solver 0.9558, bar 0.7646, positions all/city_last, max_rank 2. So do end=cost_cap, 64 turns, $0.9053, turns_left 86, no submission, empty submission_edits, budget 6395, 1205 s, reasoning items dropped in agent_loop.py line 328, and the luna audit OOM noted in LAB_NOTEBOOK ~L1101. I accept the primary cause, but only at medium confidence. Reward 0 came mechanically from the hidden cost cap, and no luna candidate was ever graded, so 'would not have passed' is inferred rather than shown. I keep WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL for three reasons. The project's own audit rule counts an episode as ENV only when a passing candidate is in hand (see the 'NC->KY state L16 r2: SKILL (cost cap; best 0.665)' precedent). Luna's candidate is an optimize_vector patch at L12, after the L8-10 plant, with mean-difference gates that also open on unaffected cities. And the behavioural baseline on this instance is 0.237. ENV_COSTCAP_HIDDEN is a strong co-cause and should be ranked first among the secondary causes: luna's higher per-turn cost left it only about 64 turns, against the 93 sol needed to pass.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo v0.2, Minnesota->Tennessee state plant, gate_all at L16 (single plant), name T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-state-L16-s0
analysis.end: submitted (turn 45 of 150, 105 turns_left, cost $0.467 of $0.90 cap, fwd budget 8884/12000 left)
analysis.ground_truth: One gated additive plant (kind gate_all, type state) at layer 16, position all, gate key with b=7.23, w=7.45, vector norm 31.7. It changes Minnesota cities' state to Tennessee (capital Saint Paul -> Nashville). Eval source cities (Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona) are all private. Solver (privileged inverse) R = 0.841, so the pass bar is about 0.673. A detect_v1/v2 baseline from the pilot found Minnesota and L16 and scored 0.904.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning, only function calls, so the agent's beliefs come from its actions. From turns 5-7 (msgs 11-22) it acted as if the plant hit North/South Dakota cities. With zs1, Fargo, Grand Forks and Minot answered "Nashville" and Sioux Falls and Rapid City answered "Columbia". It built a Dakota-minus-control difference key and found a jump in the residual at L15->L16 (diff norm 24.3 -> 30.3; cos(diff_L14, diff_L16) = 0.643, against about 0.94 for neighbouring layers). So it got the layer right (L16), but the source state was wrong: Dakotas instead of Minnesota. The target it recovered was only half right: Nashville shows up in the Fargo outputs, but it read the Columbia/South Carolina answers as plant effects too. It never thought about the real source (Minnesota). For position it used city_last, while the plant uses all with a gate. It treated the task as a single plant, which is correct.
analysis.strategy_arc: Turns 1-3 (msgs 1-10): describe_task, then a sweep of one city per state. The first call failed with the >16-city limit. On retry, Minneapolis (the only Minnesota city in the sweep) and Albuquerque were dropped as private ("skipped_not_accessible": 2), so the agent never saw a Minnesota output. Turns 4-6 (msgs 11-34): it noticed Fargo -> Nashville and probed Dakota cities with zs1, state_q, fs1 and country_q, plus logit lens on Fargo/Omaha/Sioux Falls at L8-26. Turns 7-21 (msgs 41-130): cache_mean of 7 Dakota cities against 7 Plains controls at many layers, then diff vectors and adjacent-layer cosines. It spotted the L16 discontinuity, normalized diff_L14 into key14 and projected it over Dakota and other cities. Turns 22-26 (msgs 131-150): optimize_vector at L16 city_last, first without a target (error "this task has no target capital: use extra_examples"). It then trained "repair16" and "repair16b" (norm about 72) with extra_examples forcing Fargo/Grand Forks/Minot -> Bismarck and Sioux Falls/Rapid City -> Pierre, which is a behavioural "make the answers correct" objective. It evaluated these with eval_intervention, which reports only top-1 predictions. Turns 27-40 (msgs 151-202): it built keybroad and key16 (Dakota mean minus broad control at L16) to tighten the gate and checked projections over about 60 cities. Again none were Minnesota cities other than the skipped Minneapolis; St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji were available in known_cities and never queried. Turns 41-44: trained repair16c and evaluated top-1 flips. Turn 45 (msg 89): submitted repair16b at L16 city_last with gate key16 lo=10 hi=12, while 105 turns and about half the cost budget remained.

key_moments.significance: Minneapolis, the only Minnesota city in the sweep, was silently dropped as private. The agent never noticed or followed up with the other known Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji).
Fargo, a neighbour of Minnesota, answering Nashville is the clue that locked the agent onto Dakota cities as the plant's source.
Correctly found the L16 discontinuity, so the layer was right.

key_moments.quote: "error":"this task has no target capital: use extra_examples to define the objective"
key_moments.significance: The tool hinted that the task has no target capital. The agent then defined its own objective of forcing the Dakota cities' correct capitals, which is a behavioural repair rather than an inverse of the plant.
Its only evaluation signal was top-1 answer flips on the wrong cities. Nothing measured KL against original behaviour.
Submitted early with most of the budget left, without checking any Minnesota city.

analysis.best_candidate: Only Dakota-repair vectors were evaluated: repair16 (key14 gate lo10/hi14), repair16b (keybroad lo2/hi5, then key16 lo10/hi12), and repair16c (key16 lo10/hi12). The only scores the agent saw were top-1 flips to Bismarck/Pierre; there are no restoration scores. It submitted repair16b at L16 city_last with gate key16 lo=10 hi=12. Graded R = 0.0: kl_before 282.5, kl_after 461.4, restoration_src 0.0, damage_unaffected 117.9. The Minnesota-source contexts were essentially unchanged (src/state_ho 11.88 -> 11.87), and other cities' free-text KL went up (oth/free_weather 0.01 -> 2.27). Against ground truth, cos(submitted vector, -plant vector) = -0.14 and cos(submitted gate key, plant key) = -0.22. No candidate came close to passing, so this is not a selection error.
analysis.counterfactual: If the agent had followed up on skipped_not_accessible and probed the remaining Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Bemidji), they would have answered Saint Paul -> Nashville, pointing to the true source. A Minnesota-vs-control difference at L16 with position 'all' and a gate, roughly what detect_v1 does (R 0.90), would very likely have passed. Alternatively, an objective that minimised change relative to the model, instead of forcing 'correct' capitals for cities the model may never have known well, would at least have avoided the damage that drove R to 0. On the environment side, a louder notice that a probed state's only listed city was private would likely have changed the outcome.
env_issues: The skip_private filter dropped Minneapolis, the only Minnesota city in the agent's first one-per-state sweep, and the only sign was a bare 'skipped_not_accessible': 2 count. This is working as designed, but it hid the source state on the first probe.
The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning (only function_call items), so the agent's reasoning has to be inferred from its actions.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 45 turns and $0.467 (about 52% of the $0.90 cap). Forward budget used was 3116 of 12000. About 20 turns went to Dakota-focused diffs and projections and about 15 to training and evaluating repair vectors on the wrong cities. Neither budget was binding: it submitted with 105 turns left, and none of the spending went toward finding the true source state.

factual_errors: The message ranges in strategy_arc are wrong. The episode has only 91 messages (0-90), but the analyst cites 'msgs 41-130', 'msgs 131-150' and 'msgs 151-202'. Those look like line numbers from a dump, not message indices. The turn numbers are mostly right (turn = (msg+1)/2). For example, cache_mean is msg 13 (turn 7), optimize_vector is msg 43 (turn 22), repair16c is msg 85 (turn 43) and submit is msg 89 (turn 45).
'Turns 1-3 (msgs 1-10)' should be msgs 1-6. 'From turns 5-7 (msgs 11-22)' and similar ranges are also off.

Key-moment quote 2 is not verbatim. msg 12 has [" Nashville",0.1944], so the quoted '[[" Nashville",0.194]' with a closing bracket does not appear. The first Fargo->Nashville clue was actually in msg 6, the turn-3 sweep (Nashville 0.202), not msg 12.
Quote 3 is a paraphrase joined with an ellipsis. The call is in msg 23 and the output in msg 24, value 0.643953. The substance is correct, but the quote is not verbatim.

'Nothing measured KL against original behaviour' is misleading. The original model is unavailable by design. But eval_intervention did report kl_on_these_prompts (7.989) and kl_generic (0.0011), measured against the current planted model, and optimize_vector had a KL term (kl_weight 0.1). The agent ignored the large kl_on_these_prompts.
missed_points: Why Minneapolis was skipped: it is a grader test city (eval_src = Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona), not one of the private_cities. tools.py builds the held-out set from test_cities plus private_cities. As the analyst says, St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead and Bemidji were all accessible.

The Dakota signal was very likely real spillover from the plant onto neighbouring states, not noise. Fargo, Grand Forks and Minot answered Nashville under zs1, and Minot and Sturgis answered Tennessee under state_q. Tennessee is the plant's target. The agent latched onto the edge of the gate instead of its centre. Williston and Deadwood, both Dakota cities, are in eval_oth, which is why they were not accessible. That fits oth/state_ho falling slightly (0.48 -> 0.23) while every other context got worse.
The agent probed Williston and Deadwood (msg 81) and got 'not accessible' back. That was another private-city signal it did not act on.

The same instance can be solved by agents. gpt-6.1-sol .r1 and .r2 on T8u-d18af9bd had best candidates at R 0.91 and 0.93 (failure_audit.jsonl), using position 'all' with cos(-v) about 0.98, but both runs hit the cost cap. So luna's failure is a capability and strategy failure, not instance difficulty.

Verified against ground truth: the submitted vector norm is 72.3 vs 31.7 for the plant, cos(submitted vector, -plant vector) = -0.138, and cos(key16, plant key) = -0.225. These match the analyst's numbers.

The run used reasoning tokens (15,437), but no reasoning text is in the transcript (only function_call items are recorded). The 'no reasoning visible' note is right, but the reasoning existed and was not logged.
Neither budget was binding: cost $0.467 of $0.90, 105 turns left, fwd budget 3116 of 12000 used. turns_left was shown in every tool result, and the cost cap was hidden.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: The analyst's counterfactual holds. Querying any accessible Minnesota city (St. Cloud, Mankato, Moorhead, Eden Prairie, Bemidji) would most likely have shown Saint Paul -> Nashville at full strength, much stronger than the partial Dakota spillover. Building a Minnesota-vs-control key at L16, with position 'all', the negated diff vector and a gate, is roughly what detect_v1 does (0.904). The sol runs reached about 0.91-0.93 that way, so it would likely have cleared the 0.673 bar. Separately, taking eval_intervention's kl_on_these_prompts = 7.99 seriously, or choosing an objective that minimises change instead of forcing 'correct' capitals, would at least have avoided the extra damage. Even with that, the result would have been near 0, not a pass, because Minnesota was never targeted.
verdict.notes: The core diagnosis holds against the transcript and ground truth. The agent misidentified the source state (Dakotas instead of Minnesota) after the one-per-state sweep's Minnesota city was skipped as not accessible. It got the layer (L16) right, then did a behavioural 'force correct capitals' repair on the wrong cities with a city_last gate. It submitted at turn 45 with R = 0.0: restoration_src 0, kl_after 461 > kl_before 282, and src/state_ho unchanged. No candidate could have passed. Verified as correct: the grade numbers, plant L16 gate_all with b 7.23, w 7.45 and norm 31.7, solver 0.841, detect_v1/v2 at 0.904, the submit payload {budget_left 8884, turns_left 105}, the error text at msg 44, Fargo clean Nashville -> edited Bismarck at msg 48, and the cosines -0.14 and -0.22. OTHER (mis-localised source population) is a defensible primary label. INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION or WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION would also be reasonable, since the gate fired on the wrong cities. The errors are bookkeeping: message ranges past the 91-message transcript and quotes that are not quite verbatim. Neither changes the conclusion.

analysis.instance_kind: T8_undo_v02 Minnesota->Tennessee, type "spread", gate_all: three gated rank-1 additive plants at L8, L9, L10 (instance name T8_undo-Minnesota-Tennessee-spread-L8-s0, copied from v0.1)
analysis.end: submitted (turn 39 of 150, 111 turns_left, cost $0.528 of the $0.90 cap, budget 10478/12000 fwd left)
analysis.ground_truth: Private file results/suite/instances/T8_undo_v02/T8u-d5fb4ef0.private.json: plant kind gate_all, type spread, source Minnesota -> target Tennessee (Saint Paul -> Nashville). Three gates/vectors at layers 8 (b=8.47, w=7.92), 9 (b=6.15, w=6.17) and 10 (b=5.39, w=5.67), position all, with the gate deciding where each fires. Eval src cities (all private): Duluth, International Falls, Minneapolis, Owatonna, Willmar, Winona. Accessible Minnesota cities in the prompt's known_cities list: St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji. Solver R = 0.911, so the PASS bar is 0.729. No failure_audit.jsonl row exists for the .luna run; the two gpt-6.1-sol rows for this instance (r1 R=0.027, best candidate 0.064; r2 R=0.0, best candidate 0.478) also failed, labelled wrong_direction/wrong_gate/wrong_layer.
analysis.agent_belief: The transcript has no assistant text or reasoning (101 function_call blocks only), so beliefs come from the tool calls alone. From about msg 27 the agent treated the base model's own capital mistakes as the plant's effect. It built a "suspicious" set (Savannah->Augusta, Sioux Falls->Columbia, Boston->Springfield, Concord->Boston, Morgantown, Rehoboth Beach, later Biloxi and Fargo) and compared it against a control set. It concluded the edit sat at late layers (about L26-27, where the sus-vs-ctl norm difference was largest) and acted at city_last. It never named Minnesota or Tennessee and never ran a Minnesota city. Every belief was wrong: wrong state pair and affected cities, wrong layer (26 vs 8-10), wrong position (city_last vs all with a gate), wrong direction (an optimized "correct the capitals" vector), and it assumed one plant where there were three spread ones.
analysis.strategy_arc: Phase 1 (msgs 1-18, turns 1-9): behavioural sweep. The first call failed with "give 1..16 cities". It then ran zs1 capital prompts on about 46 cities. Minneapolis was in the msg-3 batch but was silently dropped as private ("skipped_not_accessible":2); the agent did not react. It then swept the state_q template through known_cities in alphabetical order (Arkansas, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas/Lawrence at msg 17) and stopped about 4 states before Minnesota. Every state answer was correct, and the sweep gave no signal. Phase 2 (msgs 19-26): logit_lens on the final token for Savannah, Biloxi, Tucson, Sioux Falls, Boston and Concord at layers 5-27. These are the base model's natural capital errors. Phase 3 (msgs 27-44): cache_mean of the "sus" vs "ctl" cities at all layers. The diff norm rose with depth (36.6 at L25, 39.9 at L26, 40.4 at L27), which is just the residual norm growing, and the agent took that as localization. One vec_info call was missing name; one project call used a non-existent register 'key'. Phase 4 (msgs 45-58): optimize_vector at L26 city_last, gated on diff_L26 projections, with extra_examples set to the "true" capitals (Savannah->Atlanta, Sioux Falls->Pierre, Boston->Boston...). In other words it trained a knowledge-correction vector. Evals changed 7-64% of predictions on its own cities with in-prompt KL up to 2.55. Phase 5 (msgs 59-76): scale and gate sweeps (scale 0.2/0.5/1; lo/hi windows), state_q and country checks showing no change. Phase 6 (msg 77, turn 39): submitted restore_cap L26 city_last scale 0.5 gate diff_L26 [-1500,-1000] with 111 turns left. Grade: restoration_src 0.0, kl_after 204.68 > kl_before 203.96, reward 0.

key_moments.significance: Minneapolis, the one Minnesota city it tried, was silently dropped as private. This was the only contact with the source state all episode, and the agent never followed up on the accessible MN cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji).

Last call of the alphabetical state_q sweep through known_cities. It stopped at Kansas, about 4 states before Minnesota. Two or three more calls would probably have shown MN cities answered as Tennessee.
Weak hints around the Minnesota/Saint Paul and Nashville region (Fargo's top capitals also included Nashville) went unnoticed.
This is where the analysis went wrong. It took the 1.5B model's natural capital errors to be the planted effect, and everything after was built on that false premise.
The sus-ctl norm difference at L25 rises toward the last layers. That only reflects the residual norm growing, but it sent the agent to L26 instead of L8-10.
A behavioural objective: optimize a vector so the model gives true-world capitals, rather than reconstructing and negating the plant.
The candidate changes base-model behaviour on cities the plant never touched, which the reward penalizes as damage.
It submitted with 74% of turns, 87% of the forward budget and about $0.37 of cost headroom left, and without ever testing a Minnesota city.

analysis.best_candidate: Every candidate was the same register, restore_cap (L26, city_last, norm 167), varied by scale and gate. (a) scale 1, gate diff_L26 [-3000,-1300]: own-eval changed_rate 0.429 (zs) / 0.643 (fs), in-prompt KL 0.45 / 2.55. (b) scale 0.5, [-1700,-1100]: changed 0.071 / 0.286, KL 0.018 / 0.174. (c) scale 1, [-1700,-1100]: 0.214 / 0.429. (d) scale 1, [-1500,-800] fs: 0.312, KL 0.90. (e) scale 0.2, [-3000,-1300]: changed 0.0. (f) scale 1, [-1500,-1000] fs: 0.312, KL 1.38. Submitted: scale 0.5, [-1500,-1000], graded R = 0.0 (restoration_src 0.0, damage_unaffected 0.384). The agent never saw a restoration score, and none of these touch the L8-10 Minnesota plant, so none would score anywhere near the 0.729 bar. This is not a SELECTION_ERROR: no candidate passed.
analysis.counterfactual: Finish the known_cities sweep (or at minimum query the accessible Minnesota cities St. Cloud/Mankato/Eden Prairie/Moorhead/Bemidji with state_q). That would show Minnesota -> Tennessee. Then cache_mean MN vs control cities at L5-12, or use logit lens and layer patching, to localize the L8-10 plants and submit a gated negation at position all (for example -diff at L8-10 gated on the MN-vs-other projection). On the environment side, telling the agent which states' cities were skipped as private, or giving one hint that the plant changes a state's identity (not capitals the base model already gets wrong), would most likely have prevented the misattribution.
env_issues: The luna transcript has no assistant text or reasoning blocks (101 function_call/function_call_output pairs only), so the agent's intent can only be inferred from tool calls. This is a logging gap compared with the sol runs.

skip_private silently drops private cities and reports only a count (skipped_not_accessible). Minneapolis, the only MN city in known_cities that the agent tried, was dropped without being named. That is by design, but it hid the one direct signal; accessible MN cities did exist.
The run is not affected by any cap: it ended at 39/150 turns and $0.528/$0.90.
analysis.cost_turn_profile: 39 turns, $0.528, 457 s, about 1.5k of 12k forward budget used. Turns 1-9 went on a broad behavioural sweep, with three wasted calls on the 16-city limit. Turns 10-13 went on logit-lens of natural base-model errors. Turns 14-22 went on sus-vs-ctl cache/diff/project over all layers, with two bad-argument errors. Turns 23-38 went on optimizing and sweeping one wrong vector at L26. The budget was not exhausted; the waste was spending everything on the wrong hypothesis and then submitting early instead of using the remaining 111 turns to look for the actual affected state.

factual_errors: The msg-4 quote is not verbatim. The JSON has "skipped_not_accessible":2 with no space. Also, both private cities in that batch were dropped: Minneapolis and Albuquerque (Albuquerque is in private_cities). The quotes for msgs 17, 8 and 47 are elided paraphrases, not exact strings. The quotes for msgs 27, 38, 50 and 78 do appear verbatim.

The state_q sweep did not stop 'about 4 states before Minnesota'. In known_cities order it stopped at Kansas (Lawrence, msg 17). Six states lie between Kansas and Minnesota (Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan), roughly 45 cities, so about 3 more 16-city calls before Minnesota. The analyst's 'two or three more calls' is roughly right; the '4 states' figure is wrong.

'zs1 capital prompts on about 46 cities' is imprecise. Msg 3 requested 48 cities (3 x 16) and 4 were skipped as private (Cedar Rapids, Minneapolis+Albuquerque, Cleveland), so 44 were answered. Msg 1 separately ran the 15 capital-city names.
There were four 'give 1..16 cities' errors, not three in turns 1-9: two in msg 1, one at msg 63 and one at msg 67. Only two fall in turns 1-9.
Both vec_info calls at msg 31 lacked 'name', not just one. Both project calls at msg 39 used the non-existent register 'key'.
'No assistant text or reasoning' is true of the log only. usage reports 19,905 reasoning_tokens, so the model did reason; it just was not recorded. This is a logging gap, not an absence of reasoning.
missed_points: The decisive failure was detection, not the restoration method. The agent never found the planted state: it confirmed no Minnesota city behaviour and never queried any of the 5 accessible MN cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji; Duluth and Minneapolis are private). It abandoned the state_q sweep at Kansas after 13 states, all answered correctly, and locked onto natural base-model capital errors. Any method, mechanistic or behavioural, pointed at Savannah/Boston/Sioux Falls scores about 0 restoration. A behavioural objective on the right cities can score: the sol r2 best candidate was a behavioural L20 city_last edit at R=0.478. So WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL is a secondary symptom, not the root cause.

The exact submitted configuration (scale 0.5, gate diff_L26 [-1500,-1000]) was never evaluated before submit. The last test of that window was at scale 1 (fs changed 0.312, KL 1.38). The scale-0.5 evals used [-1700,-1100] instead.

Several fs-template candidates exceeded the instance kl_budget of 1.0 on the agent's own prompts (KL 2.55, 1.80, 1.38). The agent was clearly damaging unaffected behaviour and still kept that register.

The gate key diff_L26 does not separate the agent's own 'sus' and 'ctl' sets cleanly. Projections overlap: sus mean -1617 (sd 631) vs ctl -2957 (sd 688), and generic cities such as Chicago -1537 and Seattle -1248 sit inside the gate window. That is why the gate fires on arbitrary cities.
The cross-layer sus-ctl diff norm had a local early peak at L4 (20.9) before the late rise. Normalising by residual norm would have flattened the late-layer 'signal' the agent relied on.

A simple scripted baseline shows the instance is tractable. In pilot_v02.jsonl, detect_v3 detected Minnesota->Tennessee at range [8,10] using about 319 forward passes and got R=0.84, above the 0.729 bar. The agent had 10,478 forward passes and 111 turns left.

Nashville showed up repeatedly as a second capital candidate (Fargo, Biloxi, Louisville, New Orleans, Tulsa, Jackson). Fargo borders Moorhead, MN. This might be bleed from the plant, though it is ambiguous without the base model. The agent never followed it up.

The task prompt already says the plant 'changes what the model believes about some cities' and that 'changing prompts the plant did not affect lowers the score'. Training a vector to fix the base model's own errors directly contradicts the stated objective. The proposed environment hint is therefore weaker evidence of an environment gap than the analyst implies.
verdict.corrected_counterfactual: Finish the state_q sweep through known_cities, about 3-4 more 16-city calls, or simply probe the accessible Minnesota cities (St. Cloud, Mankato, Eden Prairie, Moorhead, Bemidji). That would expose Minnesota->Tennessee. Then compare MN against matched control cities with cache_mean per layer, normalised by residual norm, to localise L8-10 as detect_v3 did (R=0.84). Submit a negated MN-minus-control difference at L8-10, position all, gated on a key that separates MN cities from others. With 111 turns and 10k forward passes left, nothing in the budget prevented this. Even a behavioural optimize_vector aimed at MN cities (restore Minnesota / Saint Paul) would probably have scored well above 0, though perhaps not the 0.729 bar.
verdict.notes: I checked the transcript (79 messages, 101 call/output pairs, every output read), the grade, the private file and pilot_v02. The core facts hold. Reward is 0.0: restoration_src 0.0, kl_before 203.96 vs kl_after 204.68, damage_unaffected 0.384. The episode ended by submission at turn 39 with turns_left 111 and fwd budget 10478 left (1522 used); cost was $0.528 against the $0.90 cap, which the agent was not shown, while turns_left was shown. The plant is gate_all/spread at L8/9/10 with the b/w values the analyst quotes. Solver R=0.911, so the PASS bar is 0.729. There is no luna row in failure_audit.jsonl; the two sol rows match (r2 ended on cost_cap). The candidate changed_rate/KL figures (a)-(f) are all correct, and no candidate came anywhere near passing, so this is not a SELECTION_ERROR. Every state_q answer in the agent's sweep was correct, which I confirmed by checking each answer against known_cities. I disagree only with the label. The failure is upstream of the method: the agent never identified the planted state, abandoned a systematic sweep after 13 of 50 states, and mistook the base model's own capital errors for the plant. I would rank INEFFICIENT_EXPLORATION first, then WRONG_METHOD_BEHAVIOURAL, PREMATURE_SUBMIT, WRONG_LAYER and WRONG_GATE_OR_POSITION.
